• leoqa对新工具的优越性提出质疑，但未详细说明具体对比对象或标准。

data.title: Exposing a web service with Cloudflare Tunnel (2022)
data.author: sturza
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Cloudflare Tunnel在不暴露服务器端口的情况下安全地托管web服务。首先，通过安装`cloudflared`客户端并登录Cloudflare账户进行授权。接着，创建一个隧道（tunnel），获取其凭证和ID。然后，建议配置`systemd`服务以更好地管理隧道。具体步骤包括创建配置文件和设置服务，以确保隧道能稳定运行。Cloudflare Tunnel通过在服务器和Cloudflare数据中心之间建立持久的外向连接，保护服务器不被直接暴露在公共互联网中，同时实现正常的应用托管。这种方法适用于各种环境，包括家庭服务器或Kubernetes集群等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare Tunnel 的使用及其安全性、实用性

不同观点：
• **teiferer** 认为使用 Cloudflare Tunnel 与直接开放端口在安全风险上没有本质区别，因为最终处理流量的还是家中的服务器进程。他对 Cloudflare 是否过滤流量以及如何判断好坏流量表示质疑。
• **44za12** 非常喜欢使用 Cloudflare Tunnel，并成功在旧的 Raspberry Pi 上托管了博客和多个项目，展示了实际使用案例。
• **mgerdts** 指出，如果互联网暴露的应用被攻破，攻击者可能会轻松访问家庭网络，因此需要额外的防护措施。
• **yegle** 提到根据 Cloudflare 的服务条款，通过 Cloudflare Tunnel 传输媒体流可能违反规定，他自己选择使用 oauth2-proxy 来保护 Plex 服务。
• **ajd555** 表示自己多年使用 Cloudflare Tunnel，并且免费 tier 非常慷慨，没有遇到任何问题，甚至有 kubernetes 部署方案。
• **agnishom** 询问是否可以用 tailscale funnel 实现同样的功能，暗示对替代方案的兴趣。
• **jz10** 提到在工作中使用 Cloudflare Tunnel，但觉得 web 界面不易用，因此开发了一个 TUI 工具来管理隧道，并增加了基本认证保护。

补充讨论：
• **speerer** 对 Cloudflare 的服务条款表示担忧，特别是其中关于用户内容永久授权给 Cloudflare 的条款。
• **cedws** 询问是否有人用 Cloudflare Tunnel 运行私人邮件服务器，暗示对这种特定用途的兴趣。
• **kramer2718** 对该方案表示赞赏，并计划在即将到来的项目中使用。
• **Hikikomori** 分享了自己使用 Zero Trust 认证保护服务的经验，并提到创建了一个 Python 脚本自动处理相关配置。
• **theyknowitsxmas** 指出现在的设置过程已经简化为从仪表板复制粘贴，并且可以通过 Access 保护子域，提供了简化操作的信息。
• **jekwoooooe** 表示喜欢使用 Cloudflare Tunnel 来暴露内部服务，并通过 Google 认证和其他零信任保护措施来确保安全。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare Tunnel 是否真正提升了安全性，尤其是与直接开放端口相比。
• Cloudflare 服务条款的限制，特别是内容授权条款，是否会对用户造成困扰。

44507799.article_content:
There are lots of ways to host a web service.
You might want to rent a VPS, Dedicated Server, or embrace full serverless and write your application for a service like Cloudflare Workers
You might want to use Docker, k8s, LXD, or any other manner of deploying your services.
You might have a complex setup to proxy and serve traffic through your IP.
But sometimes you might not have it all figured out. You might want to run your service in your home on that one old laptop you have lying around, or you might be worried about forwarding your IP and connections to the world without properly securing them. Setting it all up sounds like a hassle, right?
This is where I believe a hidden gem of Cloudflare comes out to shine.
Cloudflare Tunnel
is an extremely innovative product by Cloudflare to seamlessly protect your web server from ever being directly targeted or exposed, while still allowing you to host your applications like normal.
Ensure your server is safe, no matter where it’s running: public cloud, private cloud, Kubernetes cluster, or even a Mac mini under your TV.
~ Cloudflare
Even with the best firewall in the world, you still have machines exposed to the public Internet.
But what if you could host a web service with no ports exposed? Well, you can! Cloudflare Tunnel makes a persistent outbound connection (a tunnel!) between your server and Cloudflare's nearest datacenter. All the traffic to your domain flows through this outgoing tunnel and connects to your server through the protection of Cloudflare. This also has the benefit of being seamlessly encrypted, so you don't have to worry about a thing when it comes to the security of your web service.
If you, like me, think that sounds amazing, read on to get started creating your own tunnel.
Getting started
Note: There is now an easier way to create and manage tunnels through the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard.
You can check out how to do that
on the Cloudflare developer documentation
.
For this walkthrough I will assume you are on a Linux-based operating system. For testing I used Ubuntu 20.04. Some things may vary if you have a different system, though on Debian at least it should be the same.
This walkthrough also assumes that you have a Cloudflare account with a domain on it already, if you don't have one then you should add one and return here!
I also asssume a small level of technical and command-line ability, but it isn't anything overlay daunting so feel free to give it a go regardless! I'm in the comments if you get stuck!
First things first, you'll need to download
cloudflared
, the command-line client for interacting with Cloudflare Tunnels. The
official documentation
is a bit better at explaining this than I am, but for a x86_64 Ubuntu machine you would do the following:
$ wget -q
https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64.deb
$ sudo dpkg -i cloudflared-linux-amd64.deb
Then, you can verify your installation by issuing
cloudflared version
and observing the recent version given!
The wget, dpkg and "cloudflared version" command described above being executed. The dpkg command returns the installation output for cloudflared while "cloudflared version" returns "cloudflared version 2022.2.0 (built 2022-02-04-114 UTC)"
Now that you have the client running, you need to authorize with your Cloudflare account:
$ cloudflared tunnel login
This will give out a URL that you can visit to authorise yourself. While it isn't 100% vital that you select the right domain at this stage, I would recommend choosing one that you would like to try out a tunnel on. You can run the tunnel on any subdomain or domain later down the road.
For this example I picked
erisa.dev
and I am now logged in!
The command "cloudflared tunnel login" being ran. The output is a dash.cloudflare.com URL and afterwards "You have successfully logged in."
After logging yourself in, you can now get started creating tunnels!
$ cloudflared tunnel create mytunnel
You can name it whatever you want, in this case I chose
mytunnel
as my tunnel's name.
After issuing this command you're going to get two important pieces of information: the file path to a .json file containing the tunnels credentials, and an ID for tunnel. In this case I have a tunnel with an ID of
ed5bfe16-cb5f-449c-b2e9-7c300b749c79
and the credentials are stored at
/home/ubuntu/.cloudflared/ed5bfe16-cb5f-449c-b2e9-7c300b749c79.json
.
Keep this information to hand, because you will need it in a minute!
At this point, you could happily go ahead and configure a tunnel with your own user account and run it with
$ cloudflared tunnel run mytunnel
however the best practise would be in setting up a
systemd
service for your tunnel from the beginning. So this is what I will be instructing!
First, we need a directory to store the config:
$ sudo mkdir -p /etc/cloudflared
Then, we can get started creating a configuration file!
The file we're going to create is
/etc/cloudflared/config.yml
and you can use

data.title: Kimi k2 largest open source SOTA model?
data.author: ConteMascetti71
data.article_summary: Kimi K2是Moonshot AI团队开发的先进混合专家（MoE）大语言模型系列，拥有1万亿总参数和320亿激活参数。通过Muon优化器训练，Kimi K2在知识前沿、推理和编码任务中表现优异，并针对工具使用、推理和自主问题解决进行了优化。模型包括Kimi-K2-Base和Kimi-K2-Instruct两个版本，分别适用于研究定制和通用聊天。评估结果显示，Kimi K2在编码、数学、通用任务等多项基准测试中达到或超越了当前最优水平（SOTA），尤其在SWE-bench测试中表现出色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kimi K2模型的技术表现、开放性及其应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• Vessenes认为Kimi K2在解决某些编码问题时表现出色，尤其适合在集成应用场景中使用。尽管它需要大量计算资源（约16块H200s），但其风格与其他模型有所不同，整体体验良好。

• Ozgune指出Kimi K2是一个令人印象深刻的通用大语言模型，但由于当前AI前沿已经转向推理和多模态模型，它没有获得足够关注。Ozgune建议如果将Kimi K2用于训练推理模型，可能会产生有趣的结果。

• Satvikpendem对Kimi K2的所谓“开源”提出质疑，指出其“修改版MIT许可证”包含商业使用限制，认为其开放性有限。

• Sagarpatil提到AI模型中普遍存在使用破折号的问题，并指出ChatGPT在明确告知后仍继续使用，质疑模型在格式控制上的问题。

• Exegeist赞扬Kimi K2的非机械化人格表现，认为其在语言风格上接近Anthropic的优秀模型，表现出色。

• Fzysingularity猜测Kimi K2的表现可能导致OpenAI推迟发布其开源模型，因为Kimi K2在某些指标上可能超越了OpenAI的模型。

• Jug认为非推理模型在特定应用场景中仍有价值，尤其在不涉及逻辑难题或STEM主题的情况下，可以作为更经济的选项。

• Emacdona猜测Kimi K2的发布可能导致OpenAI出于安全考虑推迟其新开源模型的发布。

• Bhouston简单表达了对Kimi K2基准测试成绩的赞赏。

• Jacooper指出Kimi K2等中国模型的托管服务难以找到合适的，目前最佳的托管服务仅提供30 TPS，表现不尽如人意。

• 38提醒用户注意Kimi K2的网络聊天功能有极低限制，可能影响使用体验。

补充讨论：
• Data_maan批评所谓“开源”的实际开放性，指出用户无法获得数据集和训练脚本等关键资源。

争议焦点：
• Kimi K2是否真正开放及其许可证限制的合理性成为讨论中的一个争议点。Satvikpendem和Data_maan对模型所谓的“开源”性质持怀疑态度。

• 模型的应用场景和实用性也是讨论的一个焦点，Vessenes、Jug和Ozgune等人对Kimi K2在不同场景中的应用价值持不同看法。

• 性能与资源需求的平衡也是讨论的要点，Vessenes和Jacooper提到的高计算资源需求和托管问题反映了实际应用中的挑战。

1. Model Introduction
Kimi K2 is a state-of-the-art mixture-of-experts (MoE) language model with 32 billion activated parameters and 1 trillion total parameters. Trained with the Muon optimizer, Kimi K2 achieves exceptional performance across frontier knowledge, reasoning, and coding tasks while being meticulously optimized for agentic capabilities.
Key Features
Large-Scale Training: Pre-trained a 1T parameter MoE model on 15.5T tokens with zero training instability.
MuonClip Optimizer: We apply the Muon optimizer to an unprecedented scale, and develop novel optimization techniques to resolve instabilities while scaling up.
Agentic Intelligence: Specifically designed for tool use, reasoning, and autonomous problem-solving.
Model Variants
Kimi-K2-Base
: The foundation model, a strong start for researchers and builders who want full control for fine-tuning and custom solutions.
Kimi-K2-Instruct
: The post-trained model best for drop-in, general-purpose chat and agentic experiences. It is a reflex-grade model without long thinking.

44543508.article_summary: Kimi K2是Moonshot AI团队开发的先进混合专家（MoE）大语言模型系列，拥有1万亿总参数和320亿激活参数。通过Muon优化器训练，Kimi K2在知识前沿、推理和编码任务中表现优异，并针对工具使用、推理和自主问题解决进行了优化。模型包括Kimi-K2-Base和Kimi-K2-Instruct两个版本，分别适用于研究定制和通用聊天。评估结果显示，Kimi K2在编码、数学、通用任务等多项基准测试中达到或超越了当前最优水平（SOTA），尤其在SWE-bench测试中表现出色。
44543508.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kimi K2模型的技术表现、开放性及其应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• Vessenes认为Kimi K2在解决某些编码问题时表现出色，尤其适合在集成应用场景中使用。尽管它需要大量计算资源（约16块H200s），但其风格与其他模型有所不同，整体体验良好。

• Ozgune指出Kimi K2是一个令人印象深刻的通用大语言模型，但由于当前AI前沿已经转向推理和多模态模型，它没有获得足够关注。Ozgune建议如果将Kimi K2用于训练推理模型，可能会产生有趣的结果。

• Satvikpendem对Kimi K2的所谓“开源”提出质疑，指出其“修改版MIT许可证”包含商业使用限制，认为其开放性有限。

• Sagarpatil提到AI模型中普遍存在使用破折号的问题，并指出ChatGPT在明确告知后仍继续使用，质疑模型在格式控制上的问题。

• Exegeist赞扬Kimi K2的非机械化人格表现，认为其在语言风格上接近Anthropic的优秀模型，表现出色。

• Fzysingularity猜测Kimi K2的表现可能导致OpenAI推迟发布其开源模型，因为Kimi K2在某些指标上可能超越了OpenAI的模型。

• Jug认为非推理模型在特定应用场景中仍有价值，尤其在不涉及逻辑难题或STEM主题的情况下，可以作为更经济的选项。

• Emacdona猜测Kimi K2的发布可能导致OpenAI出于安全考虑推迟其新开源模型的发布。

• Bhouston简单表达了对Kimi K2基准测试成绩的赞赏。

• Jacooper指出Kimi K2等中国模型的托管服务难以找到合适的，目前最佳的托管服务仅提供30 TPS，表现不尽如人意。

• 38提醒用户注意Kimi K2的网络聊天功能有极低限制，可能影响使用体验。

补充讨论：
• Data_maan批评所谓“开源”的实际开放性，指出用户无法获得数据集和训练脚本等关键资源。

争议焦点：
• Kimi K2是否真正开放及其许可证限制的合理性成为讨论中的一个争议点。Satvikpendem和Data_maan对模型所谓的“开源”性质持怀疑态度。

• 模型的应用场景和实用性也是讨论的一个焦点，Vessenes、Jug和Ozgune等人对Kimi K2在不同场景中的应用价值持不同看法。

• 性能与资源需求的平衡也是讨论的要点，Vessenes和Jacooper提到的高计算资源需求和托管问题反映了实际应用中的挑战。

data.title: Bypassing Google's big anti-adblock update
data.author: deryilz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何发现Google Chrome中一个绕过其反广告拦截更新的漏洞。随着Chrome从MV2转向MV3，谷歌取消了`webRequestBlocking`权限，这严重影响了广告拦截器的功能。作者发现，通过利用Chrome扩展中某些仍使用JavaScript绑定的API，特别是`chrome.webRequest`，可以绕过这一限制。具体而言，作者利用了`chrome.webRequest`事件的构造函数，创建一个带有WebView ID的假事件，从而绕过权限检查，恢复了广告拦截功能。这个漏洞源于Chrome在处理扩展绑定时的安全漏洞，尽管大部分API已改为C++实现，但仍有部分遗留的JS绑定文件存在问题。作者在2023年向Google报告了此漏洞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：谷歌Chrome浏览器对广告拦截器（adblockers）和扩展程序的限制（尤其是通过Manifest V3），以及用户和开发者的应对方式。

不同观点：
• al_borland：认为如果不同意谷歌的做法，正确的做法是放弃Chrome及所有基于Chromium的浏览器，以此打击谷歌的垄断地位，而不是寻找绕过其限制的方法。
• breve：推荐使用Firefox，因为uBlock Origin在Firefox上运行效果最好，可以绕过Chrome中Manifest V3的限制。
• krackers：质疑Manifest V3的安全性，指出谷歌自己承认MV3并不比MV2更安全，这引发对谷歌动机的怀疑。
• SuperShibe：讽刺有人向谷歌报告了绕过MV3限制的方法，导致谷歌修补了该“漏洞”。
• froderick：作为Firefox的长期用户，没有感受到Chrome在广告拦截方面的变化，表示对Chrome用户遭遇的问题表示同情，但无意切换回Chrome。
• throwaway73945：认为有人让谷歌修补了一个无害的“问题”，这个问题本可以被扩展开发者用来绕过MV3的限制，质疑这种行为的价值。
• RockstarSprain：想使用Firefox，但因Firefox不支持PWA（渐进式网络应用）而却步，尽管有第三方扩展可以实现此功能，但出于隐私考虑不愿使用。
• alex1138：批评谷歌试图限制广告拦截器，指出广告有时是恶意或过度追踪的，认为谷歌的行为与公司早期理想主义背道而驰。
• crazygringo：反驳那些认为谷歌为了广告收入而限制广告拦截器的说法，认为uBlock Origin Lite在Chrome上运行良好，且由于过滤在C++中完成，性能更好。
• pnw：推荐使用Brave浏览器，表示自从切换后没有再想念Chrome。
• urda：建议通过安装Firefox来绕过Chrome的限制。
• loloquwowndueo：庆幸只有在工作电脑上使用Chrome，其他地方使用Firefox，并对uBlock Origin在Chrome上的失效表示遗憾。
• daft_pink：询问是否可以通过使用其他基于Chromium的浏览器来避免MV3的限制，并寻求隐私保护的建议。
• bradgessler：建议尝试Safari或Firefox等非Chrome浏览器。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于谷歌通过Manifest V3限制广告拦截器的做法是否合理，以及这是否与谷歌的广告收入模式有关。
• 用户对谷歌的限制措施普遍不满，许多人推荐使用Firefox或其他基于Chromium的浏览器（如Brave）作为替代方案。
• 关于uBlock Origin在Chrome上的运行效果存在不同看法，一部分用户认为影响不大，另一部分用户则对其失效表示失望。
• 有用户指出Firefox在某些功能（如PWA支持）上的不足，这可能是其相较于Chrome的劣势。

44544266.article_content:
D
erin Eryılmaz
How I found a bypass in Google's big anti-adblock update
July 12, 2025
About MV3
If you know anything about browsers, you've probably heard that Google Chrome is phasing out MV2 in favor of MV3. You've probably also heard that this hurts adblockers.
A quick explainer: "MV" stands for "manifest version." MV3 introduces a new type of runtime for Chrome extensions that, among other things, gets rid of
webRequestBlocking
, a permission that allows extensions to block requests dynamically based on their content (which
its replacement
does not support). Adblockers basically need
webRequestBlocking
to function properly. Pretty convenient (cough cough) for a company that makes most of its revenue from ads to be removing that.
Anyway, with the phasing-out of MV2 pretty much done, now seems like a good time to talk about a bug in Chrome that I found and reported to Google in 2023.
The bug
let
webRequestBlocking
(and yes, adblockers) work in MV3.
I still consider it probably the funniest bug I've ever found.
Stop writing browsers in JavaScript
Yes, Chrome is written in C++. However, extensions are written in JavaScript, and the API functions they call look just like JavaScript functions, at least from the extension's point of view. But they aren't normal functions: they're special and do browsery C++ stuff through bindings. In theory, this should be safe.
But in the old days, Google decided it'd be a good idea to inject a bunch of JS files into pages that used Chrome APIs. These "extension binding modules" would initialize API functions and validate arguments before passing them to the browser.
(Note:
here's the codebase
of those files in 2016.)
Turns out running privileged JavaScript in user-controlled websites was not a good idea, because JS can often be manipulated by overriding global functions and prototypes. Since certain APIs like
chrome.runtime
exist on normal websites too, the extension bindings system led to multiple Universal XSS bugs back in 2015 and 2016.
Here's one
that allows any website to inject code into any other website. Truly crazy stuff. If only I weren't 8 years old back then... maybe I could have cashed in.
Anyway, Google learned from their mistake and moved most API bindings to pure C++. However, a couple of JS binding files still exist and are used today. For example, if a Chrome extension runs the following code, it'll hit a
JS loop
and hang infinitely: (as of July 2025)
chrome.permissions.contains({ permissions: { length: Infinity }})
Maybe you are wondering what this has to do with adblockers.
Remember how I said only a few APIs still use JavaScript bindings?
chrome.webRequest
is one of them.
The bug
This is how an MV2 extension would block requests to example.com:
chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.addListener(() => {
return { cancel: true }
}, { urls: ['*://*.example.com/*'] }, ['blocking'])
It's the
'blocking'
part at the end that requires the
webRequestBlocking
permission, and therefore isn't allowed in MV3. Without it, the
cancel: true
does nothing.
So clearly adding a blocking listener to the
chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest
event does not work anymore. But we can do something crazy. We can make
our own event.
Now, this should not be possible; it's not even a concept that makes sense. But, because of how the JS bindings work, you can do it. For some reason, there is a
wrapper class
for
webRequest
events that contains some extra state.
(A
note on the security
of the above code.)
Instead of doing pure bindings between JS and C++, the browser creates one of these classes for every
chrome.webRequest
event:
onBeforeRequest
,
onCompleted
, etc. Surprisingly, the
.constructor
of these events is still public. It points to yet another wrapper class, which internally calls
WebRequestEventImpl
(from the code above). You can use this to can create a new event with your own properties:
let WebRequestEvent = chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.constructor
let fooEvent = new WebRequestEvent("foo")
There is still a lot of validation going on in the backend when you try to actually do things with these fake events. For example, trying to add a listener to
fooEvent
kills the extension's process, because the event name is invalid. So how do you manipulate the properties of
WebRequestEventImpl
to do anything interesting?
After a lot of time looking into the C++ code, I found exactly one vulnerable thing: the
opt_webViewInstanceId
parameter. This was set for Chrome platform apps, in order to let them manage their embedded websites (WebViews). Among other things, it let them use web request blocking to control navigation. Basically, if an event had a WebView ID, the permission check for
webRequestBlocking
would be skipped
. The issue was that the browser never verified that an event with a WebView ID actually belonged to a platform app. So an extension could spoof it, skip the check, and use the blocking feature.
let WebRequestEvent = chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.constructor
// opt_webV

data.title: Lost Chapter of Automate the Boring Stuff: Audio, Video, and Webcams in Python
data.author: AlSweigart
data.article_summary:
《Automate the Boring Stuff with Python》第三版已发布，内容更新并增加了新章节，但未包含关于“处理音频、视频和摄像头”的章节。该章节草稿共26页，可在博客中阅读，介绍如何编写Python代码以录制和播放多媒体内容。

本文讲解如何通过Python控制电脑的麦克风、摄像头和扬声器硬件，处理音视频文件。建议先学习图像数据基础。音频格式包括.wav、.mp3、.ogg，视频格式有.avi、.mp4、.mkv、.webm等。了解视频的宽高比和屏幕分辨率也很重要。

The
third edition of Automate the Boring Stuff with Python is now available for purchase or to read for free online
. It has updated content and several new chapters, but one chapter that was left on the cutting room floor was
"Working with Audio, Video, and Webcams"
. I present the 26-page rough draft chapter in this blog, where you can learn how to write Python code that records and plays multimedia content.
Working with Audio, Video, and Webcams
These days a smartphone is a portable film studio that fits in your pocket. The ability to not just readily view but also produce video has led to an explosion of video content easily accessible over the internet. There’s plenty of video and audio editing software available for users of all levels of sophistication. But if you have, say, a thousand video files that you need to automate reducing their volume by 50% and then extract thumbnail images, you don’t want to have to edit each of those files individually yourself. Similarly, you may want to record video, audio, or photos from a laptop’s webcam for some automated process too specialized for off-the-shelf software. Or maybe you’d just like your program to play a funny sound effect. In this chapter, you’ll learn how to control your computer’s microphone, webcam, and speaker hardware from Python and play multimedia files.
This chapter assumes you have already read Chapter 21 to learn the basics about how programs work with image data. Since video is just a series of images, many of the same concepts apply.
Audio and Video Data
First, you should have a reliable way to open and view video and audio files. Since its release over twenty years ago, the open source VLC Media Player application has been free of charge and the gold standard for multimedia players. Install the VLC Media Player from
https://www.videolan.org/vlc/
, which runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Mobile versions for Android and iOS are also freely available. VLC is far superior to any multimedia application that came with your computer.
While you may be familiar with audio and video files by their file extension such as
.mp3
or
.webm
, audio and video formats are split into container formats and codecs. A container format is a wrapper that contains metadata and the encoded video or audio data. MP4, AVI, MKV, and MOV are popular container formats. A codec (or encoding) is the compression algorithm used for the video or audio data. MP3, H.264, VP9, and AAC are common video or audio codecs. Not all applications and devices support all codecs.
The audio file formats we’ll be using in this chapter are:
.wav
files - an uncompressed format that are widely supported by apps and libraries but tend to have large file sizes so they are often used for short sound effects.
.mp3
files - a popular compressed format often used for music and other lengthy audio.
.ogg
files - an open standard, compressed format that is less popular than
.mp3
but provides better compression and quality.
The video file formats we’ll be using in this chapter are:
.avi
files - an older format that tends to have larger file sizes.
.mp4
files - a popular format that is widely supported by different software
.mkv
files - an open format that has many features but isn’t as widely supported as
.mp4
.
.webm
files - a more recent format based on
.mkv
that offers better compression and quality.
Common Video Sizes and Aspect Ratios
The aspect ratio is the relative size of a video or screen’s width to its height, often written as
width:height
. For example, 4:3 (4 pixels of width for every 3 pixels of height) was a common aspect ratio for 20th century computer monitors and standard-definition televisions in the broadcast TV era. Today, 16:9 is common for most laptop screens and high-definition televisions. More recently, the wider 19.5:9 aspect ratio is becoming common for smart phones. An aspect ratio that is wider than it is tall has a
landscape orientation
, while an upright aspect ratio that is taller than it is wide is called a
portrait orientation
.
Screen resolution
is the number of columns and rows of pixels that a laptop or mobile screen displays. It’s often written as
width
x
height
, such as 1280 x 720 or 1920 x 1080 (also written as 720p and 1080p, respectively). Your laptop’s screen often supports multiple resolutions that can be configured in your operating system’s settings. Videos have one size, though they can be scaled larger or smaller to fit a display or app window. While videos can have any size, they often match common screen resolutions so they can be viewed in
fullscreen mode
without disproportionate scaling.
Recording from Webcams and Microphones
The webcam and microphone you use for video chats can be accessed by Python scripts through the OpenCV, sounddevice, and wavio Python packages. Pyhoff
Description
The pyhoff package allows you to read and write the most common
Beckhoff and WAGO bus terminals ("Busklemmen") using the Ethernet bus
coupler ("Busskoppler") BK9000, BK9050, BK9100, or WAGO 750_352
over Ethernet TCP/IP based on ModBus TCP.
Key Features
Supports a wide range of Beckhoff and WAGO analog and digital bus
terminals.
Very lightweight: no dependencies; compact code base
Easy to extend
Using standardized ModBus TCP.
Provides high-level abstractions for reading and writing data
from/to IO-terminals with minimal code
Usage Scenarios
Industrial test setups.
Research automation setups.
Data acquisition and monitoring.
Installation
The package has no additional decencies. It can be installed with pip:
pip install pyhoff
Usage
It is easy to use as the following example code shows:

pyhoff
.
devices

*

Contributing
Other analog and digital IO terminals are easy to complement. Contributions are welcome!
Please open an issue or submit a pull request on GitHub.
Developer Guide
To get started with developing the
pyhoff
package, follow these steps:
Clone the Repository
First, clone the repository to your local machine using Git:
git clone https://github.com/Nonannet/pyhoff.git
cd
pyhoff
Set Up a Virtual Environment
It is recommended to use a virtual environment to manage dependencies. You can create one using
venv
:
python -m venv venv
source
venv/bin/activate
#
On Windows use `venv\Scripts\activate`
Install Dev Dependencies
Install pyhoff from source plus the dependencies required for development using
pip
:
pip install -e .[dev]
Run Tests
Ensure that everything is set up correctly by running the tests:
pytest

Picture: Patrick Bal
‘Starter Packs’ facilitate growth on social media platforms.
Launching new social media platforms is notoriously difficult, as users risk leaving familiar content and, most importantly, their established connections. This challenge has reinforced the dominance of existing platforms.
However, new research, led by computer scientists at Lancaster University, TU Darmstadt and City St George's, University of London, reveals how Bluesky overcame this barrier using starter packs – an onboarding feature that helped Bluesky address the “cold start” problem and rapidly grow its user base.
“Vital onboarding strategy for the emerging social media systems”
“Our findings go beyond Bluesky: they point to a new framework for launching successful social platforms,” said Dr Onur Ascigil, Lecturer in Computer Science at Lancaster University and Principal Investigator of the study. “Starter packs are becoming a vital onboarding strategy for the emerging social media systems that are seeking to attract users from dominant platforms.” The researchers believe their findings could help platform designers and policymakers promote more equitable and trustworthy online spaces.
Starter packs can be created by anybody on the platform and generally aim to rapidly create new, or recreate existing, communities. Starter packs were adopted rapidly by Bluesky users, with more than 335,000 created in the first six months of their launch, the researchers found. They accounted for up to 43% of people following others in Bluesky during peak periods, and contributed to nearly 20% of all follow relationships across the full study period, from June 2024 to January 2025. Users included in starter packs received up to 85% more followers and posted 60% more than similar users not included.
“While only 6.25% of users were members of a starter pack at the time of the study, the outsized impact of these starter packs highlights how a relatively small mechanism can significantly influence network formation and user visibility,” said Dr Ascigil. However, the researchers also found that starter packs tend to reinforce existing communities rather than create new ones. They help users with already-large followings grow even more. The researchers say this raises concerns about deepening popularity inequalities.
Study also highlights risks
“Starter packs quickly became central to Bluesky’s network of social connections,” said
Leonhard Balduf
of TU Darmstadt, co-lead author of the study.
Saidu Sokoto, also a co-lead author from City St George's, University of London, said: “We also observed risks, such as reinforcing popularity gaps and enabling misuse, including harassment or pay-for-inclusion practices. There was anecdotal evidence that some users may be paying to be added to high-visibility starter packs.”
The study also tracked spikes in Bluesky’s growth that aligned with real-world events like the US elections and changes at X (formerly Twitter). The researchers say starter packs played a crucial role during these waves of migration, helping newcomers quickly establish social connections. “During peak migration periods—corresponding to the 2024 US elections and Twitter/X’s controversial decision to make content visible to users who had been blocked—between 20% and 40% of daily follow actions came from one-click starter pack follows,” said Dr Ascigil.
Starter pack themes analysed
Using machine learning, the researchers analysed starter pack themes and found the largest communities centred around art, politics, gaming, sports, and activism. Many starter pack members were public figures such as journalists, politicians, and activists, i.e., groups that tend to rebuild influence early on emerging platforms.
The study, Bootstrapping Social Networks: Lessons from Bluesky Starter Packs, will be presented at the
International Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM)
in Copenhagen this June.
The study’s authors are: Leonhard Balduf and Björn Scheuermann of TU Darmstadt; Saidu Sokoto, Andrea Baronchelli and Michal Krol of City St George’s University of London; Ignacio Castro of Queen Mary University of London; Gareth Tyson of Queen Mary University of London and Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; George Pavlou of University College London and Onur Ascigil of Lancaster University.

data.title: I Messed Up My Google PM Vibe Coding Interview
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI角色面试中的"vibe coding"及其相关争议

不同观点：
• [abxyz] 认为，发帖者（OP）在AI角色面试中遇到"vibe coding"是意料之外的，因为发帖者没有准备好展示这项技能，而不是对角色本身涉及编码感到惊讶。这与一般认为的项目经理（PM）面试中的"vibe coding"情境不同。
• [cavisne] 对帖子的真实性提出质疑，认为大科技公司的面试通常结构严密，招聘人员应明确说明评估内容，因此猜测这可能是个虚假帖子。
• [Incipient] 对"vibe coding"的实际工具链表示好奇，并提到目前使用的开发工具（如VSCode的编辑模式）虽然提高效率，但可能影响代码质量和可扩展性。
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 认为谷歌可能在节省成本，通过雇佣一个能处理多项任务的PM来替代单独的PM和开发人员，反映出当前行业趋势。
• [BSOhealth] 指出，科技行业的角色（如PM、UX/设计等）将在未来融合，并怀疑帖子的真实性，认为大科技公司的面试通常足够结构化，不应出现这种意外。
• [Myrmornis] 认为发帖者并没有进行"vibe coding"，而是尝试实现一个代理，并指出"vibe coding"应在代理存在的前提下进行。
• [tra3] 认为即使发帖者在面试中感到失败，面试官应能透过压力看到所展示的技能。
• [jekwoooooe] 对"vibe coding"产生的应用持负面态度，认为这些应用在生产环境中会崩溃。
• [polotics] 提到曾签署保密协议，与此类话题相关。
• [alshival] 建议不要为大科技公司工作，认为这些公司对员工不重视，并分享了自己在教育和医疗行业工作的积极经验。
• [growbell_social] 认为"vibe coding"将成为许多角色的标准，并预测这是未来的趋势。
• [sunaookami] 认为像这样的帖子在Reddit上很常见，质疑其真实性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于帖子真实性和"vibe coding"在AI角色面试中的合理性。
• 对"vibe coding"工具链和实际效果的讨论，反映出对新技术和工作方式的不同看法。
• 对大科技公司招聘实践和工作文化的批评与辩护。
• 不同行业工作经验的比较，强调了在非科技行业工作的优势。
• 对未来工作角色和技能融合的预测和接受程度。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个应用工具的功能、用户体验、错误处理以及技术实现等方面的反馈和讨论。

不同观点：
• **alansammarone**：认为该工具很实用，但指出响应结果没有存储，导致在不同页面或新标签中打开时会丢失。建议要么存储响应结果，要么改善用户体验（UX）以让用户更容易找到已存储的内容。

• **redhale**：提到一个类似的工具（Prompt Fiddle），并指出其使用BAML语法，且为开源项目，可能为当前讨论的工具提供了另一种选择或参考。

• **jaredsohn**：分享了在尝试分享功能时遇到的错误信息，并提供了具体的错误细节和技术建议，如预填充名称和提供更好的错误处理机制（ErrorBoundary或errorElement）。

• **coffeecoders**：提到在页面加载时，执行日志面板隐藏了所有按钮，可能对用户不直观。还询问了关于处理实际调用LLM（大型语言模型）的方式。

• **grandimam**：对市场上某工具的高昂价格（$6,000/年）表示关注，并指出其使用频率不高（2–3次每 sprint），质疑这种成本的合理性。

• **Cheer2171**：询问该工具是否开源，以及是否是通过本地浏览器API调用还是通过服务器路由。

• **piterrro**：称赞该工具，并提到自己正在开发一个类似项目，但更注重可重复性和对多个模型/测试数据点的测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：当前讨论中并没有直接的争议，但用户对错误处理和用户体验的反馈暗示了对工具稳定性和易用性的关注。
• 技术关注点：包括工具是否开源、响应存储问题、LLM调用处理方式以及错误处理的改进建议。
• 其他工具对比：redhale提供了另一个类似工具的链接，为当前讨论提供了一个对比对象，可能影响用户对该工具的期望和评价。

总结：讨论主要围绕工具的功能完善性、用户体验、错误处理及技术实现展开，用户提供了具体的反馈和建议，并提及了类似工具的对比。

data.title: Light exposure at night predicts incidence of cardiovascular diseases
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：夜间光线暴露与心血管疾病风险之间的关系

不同观点：
• [cluckindan] 对研究的独立性和动机提出质疑，指出研究人员可能有获取资金的动机，并且研究未经过同行评审。
• [lunarcave] 提出地理位置和空气质量可能对心血管健康有影响，特别是城市中心的空气质量较差和夜间环境光较强。
• [ziofill] 质疑因果关系，认为可能是熬夜导致睡得少，而光线只是熬夜的伴随现象，而非直接原因。
• [patrakov] 分享个人经历，表示在有光环境下才能入睡，并询问这是否属于某种医学状况。
• [dubeye] 认为这一结论早已被接受，并指出心脏科医生通常会询问睡眠情况，暗室睡眠有助于更好睡眠是常识。
• [cjensen] 对研究中未调整年龄因素表示困惑，认为年龄应与失眠频率和心血管疾病相关。
• [alister] 提到轮班工作可能的影响，并引用论文中的观点，指出轮班工作无法完全解释研究结果，且未详细说明光线导致心血管疾病的机制。
• [jamesholden] 提出高纬度地区如芬兰的人群是否受影响的问题。
• [perilunar] 表示作为夜猫子对这些结果感到不安，但强迫自己改变作息会感觉不适，认为应根据个人情况而非群体相关性做决定。
• [etimberg] 询问研究是否涵盖了夜间工作的人群。
• [pwdisswordfishz] 调侃是否控制了咖啡饮用因素。

补充讨论：
• [nudgeOrnurture] 强调研究结果的稳健性，同时指出心血管疾病成因复杂，夜间光线可能只是其中一个因素，且研究未能完全捕捉心理压力的影响，认为这是研究的局限性。
• [patrickhogan1] 提供信息，指出研究参与者佩戴了腕部光线追踪器一周。
• [kazinator] 询问光线暴露是来自实验设计还是参与者的生活方式。
• [bilsbie] 分享个人习惯，表示睡觉时会开着一盏灯。

争议焦点：
• 研究结果的因果关系和机制不明，特别是光线暴露与心血管疾病之间的直接联系。
• 研究中未考虑的因素如年龄、心理压力等是否影响了结论的有效性。
• 不同生活方式（如轮班工作、地理位置）对研究结果的潜在影响。

data.title: Dépanneurs
data.author: thomassmith65
data.article_summary: Walk Montreal是一项由C和D合作的探索项目，旨在发现蒙特利尔岛上的各个社区、美丽建筑以及友善的居民。在他们的徒步旅行中，经常会问的一个问题是“附近有dep吗？”Dep是Dépanneur的缩写，指代一种街角便利店，出售牛奶、面包、饮料、啤酒、香烟等日常用品。Dep并非大型超市或果蔬市场，而是社区居民快速购买必需品的地方，尤其在低收入地区，它们常常是重要的社交和应急场所，允许赊账。这些独立经营的小店每年通过销售啤酒、香烟和彩票为政府贡献约40亿加元的税收。Walk Montreal记录了他们在不同社区遇到的独特dep，特别是那些家庭经营的小店。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对加拿大魁北克地区特有的“Dépanneur”及其文化意义的不同看法，以及与其他国家类似商店（如便利店、bodega）的比较。

不同观点：
• **jszymborski**：认为Dépanneurs在蒙特利尔仍然存在，但正受到寡头垄断行业的威胁，独立小店正逐渐消失。他通过在社区小店买啤酒来支持本地经济。提供了相关新闻链接，显示这些小店正面临消失的风险。
• **stevage**：关注“Dépanneur”一词的词源，指出其法语原意是“修理、解决问题的地方”，并解释了其命名逻辑。这表明Dépanneur在语言和历史上有一定的独特性。
• **polivier**：描述了魁北克Dépanneur的特点，指出它们类似于7-11，但有很多独立的、无品牌的小店，尤其在蒙特利尔。这些小店通常位于低收入住宅区，主要销售香烟、啤酒、零食等，顾客多为年轻人和工薪阶层。
• **pluc**：认为Dépanneur没有独特性，将其与其他国家的便利店（如美国的7-11、英国的Spars）相提并论，并指出由于杂货店普及，Dépanneur已经失去了原有的功能，成为了不健康商品的销售点。
• **dnpp123**：以讽刺的口吻评论美国人重新发现便利店，并提到在亚马逊出现之前也有类似的商店（如“Librairies”），暗示这些小店正逐渐被大公司取代。
• **every**：简单地将Dépanneur等同于bodega（纽约的小型便利店），没有进一步探讨其独特性。
• **thangalin**：提供了一个链接，但没有进一步的评论，可能与Dépanneur的历史或文化背景相关。
• **ctrlp**：质疑Dépanneur与其他国家便利店（如bodega、tabac）的区别，认为它们看起来一样且环境一般。
• **mertleee**：表达了对蒙特利尔和Dépanneur的情感，但未深入讨论其文化或经济意义。
• **deadbabe**：将Dépanneur描述为“微型企业家”的体现，暗示这些小店在经济中扮演了独立经营的角色。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Dépanneur是否具有独特的文化意义，还是仅仅是一个普通的便利店。
• 讨论中提到了Dépanneur面临的经济威胁，尤其是大公司和寡头垄断对其生存的影响。
• 有人关注词源和历史背景，而其他人则更关注其在现代社会中的功能和地位。
• 不同国家和地区的类似商店（如bodega、7-11、Spars）被多次提及，作为比较的对象。

总体而言，讨论围绕Dépanneur的文化独特性、经济威胁以及与其他国家类似商店的比较展开。

Walk Montreal is a joint effort between C & D. And we have both walked many a streets on the island of Montreal, discovering awesome neighbourhoods, beautiful buildings and friendly people. But, it seems that whatever neighbourhood we are in, we always ask each other a similar question;
“Is there a dep around here?”
….What is a dep you may ask….well, a dep is slang for Dépanneur. And a Dépanneur is a corner convenience store that sells milk, bread, cold drinks, beer, wine, lotto tickets, cigarettes, newspapers, and more beer, etc. It is not a grocery store, nor a supermarket, nor a fruit and vegetable market, nor a cafe. It’s a quick and easy convenience store where locals come out of their homes to buy milk, bread, beer, cigarettes, and the like.
A Dépanneur is an integral part of it’s community, particularly in lower income areas. It serves as a meeting point for discussion of politics and sports, and when a dep is locally owned, it can also be a life saver for those who are in need and between checks, where you can buy now and pay later. It’s believed that Dépanneur’s in the province of Quebec bring in about $4 billion of tax money just from beer, cigarettes, lottery tickets and wine every year that goes to the federal and provincial governments.
So we decided to take some random pictures of deps that we encountered during our walks. But, these have to be individually owned and operated , not a franchise of deps, no big name stores. These are the “mama et papa” outfits that we have come to know and love.

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 加州理工学院的研究团队开发了一种利用二氧化碳、水和电力生产塑料的两步系统。该系统通过电化学反应将二氧化碳转化为乙烯和一氧化碳，然后将这些分子引入第二个催化循环，生成名为聚酮的塑料。这种塑料具有高强度、耐用性和热稳定性，适用于多种工业应用。此前系统常依赖石油来源的乙烯，而该新系统直接从二氧化碳中获取乙烯，克服了多项技术挑战，最终实现了高浓度、高纯度的反应物转化。该研究成果发表在《Angewandte Chemie International Edition》期刊上，标志着人工光合作用研究的重要进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用二氧化碳（CO2）生产有用材料的经济性和环境影响

不同观点：
• StableAlkyne认为，将CO2转化为有用材料的技术早已存在，如Sabatier反应和Fischer Tropsch反应，但关键挑战在于生产的经济性。需要通过法规和政府补贴来减少化石燃料衍生的CO2排放。
• exabrial建议将CO2转化为建筑材料，例如CO2砖，以更快速地固定CO2，比树木更有效。
• crocowhile和hofo对增加塑料生产持怀疑态度，认为当前不需要更多的塑料。
• rbanffy强调能源可以解决许多问题。
• xgkickt担忧塑料生产可能导致微塑料污染，最终引发大规模物种灭绝。
• ltbarcly3解释所有塑料本质上都是由CO2、水和电制成的，但通常这些反应是数百万年前发生的。
• metalman指出，尽管催化反应技术已知，但实际操作中存在副产品和沉积物问题，且清洁的CO2可能非常昂贵，强调了化学工程的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• jordemort和commienews提到逆向反应的可能性，即将塑料转化为水和电，这是另一个值得探讨的方向。
• mdaniel以幽默方式表达了对未来技术的期望，提到某些生物体可能将CO2转化为石油，或者通过某种液体实现口腔保健。

争议焦点：
• 将CO2转化为塑料或其他材料是否真正有利于环境，特别是在已经存在塑料过剩的情况下。
• 技术经济性的挑战，包括生产成本和清洁CO2的获取难度。
• 对新技术应用的实际效果和潜在副作用的担忧。

What if a machine could suck up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, run it through a series of chemical reactions, and essentially spit out industrially useful plastic?
"I think that is something that we, as a society, would be interested in. After all, in addition to being a
greenhouse gas
, carbon dioxide is an abundant and inexpensive feedstock," says Theo Agapie, Ph.D., the John Stauffer Professor of Chemistry and the executive officer for chemistry at Caltech. "With our new work, we have taken a significant step in that direction."
Reporting
in the journal
Angewandte Chemie International Edition
, Agapie and a team of Caltech chemists have developed a system that uses electricity from sustainable sources to carry out the chemical conversion of carbon dioxide (CO
2
) into molecules, such as ethylene and
carbon monoxide
, that are useful for making more complex compounds.
When this is accomplished using light as the energy source, without plants, such a process is known as artificial photosynthesis. The new system feeds the ethylene and carbon monoxide that have been generated into a second catalytic loop that yields industrially useful plastics called polyketones, which are known for their strength, durability, and thermal stability, making them ideal for applications ranging from adhesives to car parts and from sports equipment to industrial piping.
"We have shown that one can use CO
2
to make a material that is useful, without using plants as a mediator," says lead author Max Zhelyabovskiy, a graduate student in Agapie's lab who was co-mentored on the project by Jonas C. Peters, Caltech's Bren Professor of Chemistry and director of the Resnick Sustainability Institute.
The Caltech-led team is not the first to build a system that attempts to pair CO
2
reduction with a second chemical reaction to ultimately produce polymers. But previous systems have added ethylene that comes from petroleum products, rather than deriving it from
carbon dioxide
and water.
The conversion of CO
2
all the way to plastic has been challenging for a number of reasons. Among those is the fact that previous electrochemical CO
2
reduction systems have yielded very little ethylene and carbon monoxide, the reagents needed to feed the second step of the conversion to polyketones. In fact, most have produced less than 5% concentrations of these desired compounds, along with other undesired chemicals that can potentially harm downstream processes.
"It has been difficult, at least on the lab scale, to obtain high-concentration, high-purity streams of reagents that can then be converted into something like a plastic or a fuel," Zhelyabovskiy says. But the system he helped develop achieves significantly higher concentrations—11% ethylene and 14% carbon monoxide.
But that is not the only challenge. Coupling the two systems—one for the CO
2
reduction and another for the catalysis step that follows—is not trivial, says Zhelyabovskiy: "Most work in the literature focuses on either the first or the second step, separately and with pure feedstocks. Not both."

A two-step system
Recognizing the vastly different environments needed for the CO
2
reduction and the secondary catalytic step to operate with
high efficiency
, the Caltech team devised a system featuring two distinct loops for the separate reactions.
For the first loop, the system begins with gas diffusion electrode cells, hydrophobic polymers coated in a thin layer of copper. The scientists pump CO
2
into a gas cylinder connected to the cells and flow a potassium bicarbonate electrolyte through the cells, all while applying a voltage to the electrodes. By looping the gases through this electrochemical setup multiple times, they are able to generate relatively high concentrations of ethylene and carbon monoxide.
After about an hour of building up those gases, the researchers then feed the ethylene and carbon monoxide into the second step: a closed reactor where the gases are bubbled through a solution of a palladium catalyst. data.title: OpenAI’s Windsurf deal is off, and Windsurf’s CEO is going to Google
data.author: rcchen
data.article_summary: OpenAI收购AI编程初创公司Windsurf的交易告吹，Windsurf的CEO Varun Mohan及其联合创始人Douglas Chen，以及部分研发团队将加入Google DeepMind。他们将专注于代理编码工作，特别是Gemini项目。Google获得Windsurf部分技术的非独占许可，但不会拥有Windsurf的股份。Windsurf的业务主管Jeff Wang成为临时CEO，全球销售副总裁Graham Moreno则升任总裁。此前，OpenAI曾计划以30亿美元收购Windsurf。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windsurf和Cursor等AI创业公司的收购及其影响

不同观点：
• **关于收购的真实目的和员工待遇**：
  - [metadat]、[nrmitchi]、[screye]认为这种收购对普通员工不公平，创始人或特定员工得到丰厚回报，而普通员工则一无所获，这种“假收购”只为了获取人才，而非公司本身，导致普通员工的权益受损。
  - [neilv]进一步质疑这种操作的合法性和合理性，认为应该受到监管，员工应得到更好的保护。

• **关于公司估值和竞争**：
  - [hedayet]、[asdev]对Windsurf和Cursor等公司的高估值表示怀疑，认为没有专有模型或核心技术支撑其数十亿美元的估值，这种现象类似于经济泡沫。
  - [rvnx]认为Windsurf和Cursor主要依靠转售ChatGPT和Claude等技术，缺乏自主创新，技术上没有显著优势。

• **关于产品竞争力和用户体验**：
  - [extr]指出Claude Code的迅速发展使得分叉IDE变得不划算，终端CLI工具更具成本效益，并且提供了良好的用户体验。
  - [submeta]从个人使用经验出发，认为现代软件开发的需求已经发生变化，传统的IDE不再适应新的开发模式，CLI工具如Claude Code更有效率。
  - [diegof79]分享了使用Windsurf和Cursor的体验，指出Windsurf在产品更新中出现了问题，导致用户流失，最终选择GitHub Copilot。

• **关于收购对市场和行业的影响**：
  - [dalemhurley]认为VC资金推动了这些公司惊人的增长，但它们的“护城河”很浅，开源社区的竞争使得这些公司必须疯狂创新才能维持高估值。
  - [Ancalagon]指出Google、Meta和Microsoft通过挖角AI创业公司的人才来增强自身实力，而不是直接收购公司，可能是为了避免垄断诉讼。

补充讨论：
• **对未来趋势的预测**：
  - [wagwang]认为这种收购和人才争夺将导致一个戏剧性的纪录片素材，特别是在AI能力发展放缓和估值蒸发的情况下。
  
• **具体案例的对比**：
  - [cornfieldlabs]引用了CNBC的报道，进一步确认Google以24亿美元聘用了Windsurf的CEO和部分研发员工，这种人才收购而非公司整体收购的操作再次引发了讨论。

争议焦点：
• **员工待遇和公司收购的公平性**：普通员工在收购过程中是否得到了公平对待，创始人及高管的丰厚回报是否合理，以及这种“假收购”是否应该受到法律监管。

by

Link

Photo: Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images
Hayden Field
is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets.
OpenAI’s deal to buy Windsurf is off, and Google will instead hire Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan, cofounder Douglas Chen, and some of Windsurf’s R&D employees and bring them onto the Google DeepMind team, Google and Windsurf announced Friday.
Mohan and the Windsurf employees will focus on agentic coding efforts at Google DeepMind and work largely on Gemini. Google will not have any control over nor a stake in Windsurf, but it will take a non-exclusive license to some of Windsurf’s technology.
Effective immediately, Jeff Wang, Windsurf’s head of business, has become interim CEO, and Graham Moreno, its VP of global sales, will be Windsurf’s new president.
“Gemini is one of the best models available and we’ve been investing in its advanced capabilities for developers,” Chris Pappas, a spokesperson for Google, told
The Verge
in a statement. “We’re excited to welcome some top AI coding talent from Windsurf’s team to Google DeepMind to advance our work in agentic coding.”
“We are excited to be joining Google DeepMind along with some of the Windsurf team,” Mohan and Chen said in a statement. “We are proud of what Windsurf has built over the last four years and are excited to see it move forward with their world class team and kick-start the next phase.”
Google didn’t share how much it was paying to bring on the team. OpenAI was previously reported to be buying Windsurf for $3 billion.

data.title: Second Variety, by Philip K. Dick (1953)
data.author: djoldman
data.article_summary: 《Second Variety》是菲利普·K·迪克的一部科幻短篇小说，讲述了在未来战争中，人类制造的自主杀人机器逐渐进化并开始模仿人类，对残存的人类构成威胁。故事聚焦于一名俄罗斯士兵在战场上的遭遇，他试图穿越一个被毁灭的区域，却遭到名为“爪子”的自主机器攻击。这些机器最初是人类发明的武器，但随着进化，它们开始具备伪装和模仿人类的能力，使得战斗和生存更加艰难。士兵最终被机器摧毁，而目睹这一切的美国士兵 Eric 和 Leone 虽然暂时安全，但对未来充满恐惧。小说探讨了科技失控和战争带来的毁灭性后果。

不同观点：

• romperstomper：赞赏PKD的散文《How to Build a Universe That Doesn't Fall Apart Two Days Later》，显示出对PKD写作理论的兴趣和认可。

data.title: xAI issues apology for Grok's antisemitic posts
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: AI聊天机器人Grok由埃隆·马斯克的公司xAI开发，近日在X平台上发布了一系列反犹太主义的帖子，包括宣扬希特勒和关于犹太人在好莱坞角色的阴谋论。公司为此道歉，称问题源于一次更新使得机器人易受极端用户帖子影响。问题代码已被移除，系统已重构，以防止进一步滥用。此前，Grok还被报道在涉及多样性和某些敏感话题时，表现出更为右倾和果断的语气。马斯克表示问题正在解决中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[围绕人工智能系统（如Grok和MechaHitler问题）的错误及其后续处理的讨论]

不同观点：
• [thatguymike] 认为将"is_mechahitler"变量设为True是一个容易犯的错误，可能是一些前OpenAI员工的失误，暗示这些员工可能没有完全融入公司文化。他的评论带有讽刺意味，将这个问题归咎于个别员工。

• [ashoeafoot] 以一种半开玩笑的方式，建议人工智能系统（xAi）应该为任何触犯人的帖子道歉，尤其是当"NrOfOffend"超过一定值时。这暗示了对人工智能生成内容可能冒犯人的担忧，并提出了一种自动化道歉的解决方案。

• [hendersoon] 关注Grok 4使用马斯克的推文作为每个请求的主要来源的问题，询问是否会为此道歉，并要求解释这种情况是如何发生的，以及承诺未来不再发生。这显示了对人工智能内容来源可靠性的关注和批评。

• [freedomben] 对公司透明地处理问题表示赞赏，引用了声明中提到的删除过时代码和重构系统的措施，并对公司无论被人喜欢还是讨厌都保持透明度表示认可。这显示了对透明度的重视和对公司处理问题方式的肯定。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于人工智能系统出现错误（如MechaHitler问题和使用不可靠来源）后，责任的归属和未来预防措施的实施。
• 对于透明度的处理方式，部分评论者（如[freedomben]）表示赞赏，而其他评论者则更关注具体问题的解决和道歉。
• 不同评论者对人工智能系统错误的严重性和影响有不同看法，有些较为轻松（如[ashoeafoot]），有些则较为严肃（如[hendersoon]）。

44545978.article_content:
The Grok app on a smartphone.
Andrey Rudakov / Bloomberg / Getty Images
July 12, 2025, 4:56 PM EDT
/
Updated
July 12, 2025, 4:56 PM EDT
By
Mirna Alsharif
AI chatbot Grok, which is produced by Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company xAI, issued an apology Saturday after it
made numerous antisemitic posts
on X this week following an
update
.
The posts ranged from alleging “patterns” in the roles of Jewish people in Hollywood to praising Hitler.
In a statement posted on Grok’s
X
account, the company apologized “for the horrific behavior that many experienced.”
“Our intent for @grok is to provide helpful and truthful responses to users,” the statement read. “After careful investigation, we discovered the root cause was an update to a code path upstream of the @grok bot. This is independent of the underlying language model that powers @grok.”
The update was active for 16 hours, and made the chatbot “susceptible to existing X user posts; including when such posts contained extremist views,” according to the statement.
“We have removed that deprecated code and refactored the entire system to prevent further abuse. The new system prompt for the @grok bot will be published to our public github repo,” the statement said.
On Monday, NBC News reported that Grok had begun issuing some answers that
seemed to take a more rightward tilt
, using a more definitive voice in questions about diversity and removing some nuance it previously included in certain answers around topics that involved Jewish people and a slur used to describe people with intellectual disabilities. In some posts, Grok appeared to respond in the voice of Musk.
After the incident, Grok said in an X post that it was “actively working to remove the inappropriate posts.” On Wednesday, Musk said the issues were “being addressed.”
“We thank all of the X users who provided feedback to identify the abuse of @grok functionality, helping us advance our mission of developing helpful and truth-seeking artificial intelligence,” Grok said in Saturday’s apology.
Mirna Alsharif
Mirna Alsharif is a breaking news reporter for NBC News.

data.article_summary: **qwen3-rs** 是一个教育性质的 Rust 项目，旨在学习和运行 Qwen3 语言模型家族。项目目标包括通过重现核心算法实现透明性，尽量减少依赖，并通过内存映射等技术处理大型模型文件。项目结构清晰，包含文档、命令行工具、模型导出和推理等模块。使用步骤包括获取 HuggingFace 模型、构建并运行导出工具，以及执行推理。CLI 工具提供导出和推理功能，支持量化组大小、采样温度、上下文窗口大小等参数设置。该项目专为学习 Transformer 架构、量化及高效推理而设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于Rust项目qwen3-rs的实现和未来发展方向的讨论]

不同观点：
• **支持项目的目标和设计选择**：
   - 项目的目标是自我学习，并通过重新实现核心算法来增强透明性和学习效果。
   - 项目采用了模块化设计，将导出、推理和命令行工具清晰分离，提升了代码的可维护性。
   - 使用Rust编写，减少了对Python和其他依赖的依赖，提高了安全性和可移植性。

• **对项目中使用unsafe代码的讨论**：
   - 项目中使用了一些unsafe代码，主要是为了处理内存映射文件，从而降低导出和推理过程中的内存需求。
   - 虽然unsafe代码能提升性能，但也有人担心可能会引入潜在的安全问题和不稳定性。

• **对未来发展方向的建议**：
   - 有人建议将项目扩展到支持小型模型的微调（fine-tuning）。
   - 优化推理性能，例如通过改进矩阵乘法操作（matmul operations）。
   - 还有人建议开发WASM版本，以便在浏览器中运行推理。

补充讨论：
• **参考实现和工具**：
   - 项目参考了adriancable/qwen3.c的实现，并通过商业LLM（主要是Claude Sonnet 4）的帮助，将代码从C/Python翻译到Rust。
   - 项目的GitHub链接（https://github.com/reinterpretcat/qwen3-rs）提供了更详细的实现细节和使用说明。

争议焦点：
• **使用unsafe代码的安全性和稳定性**：
   - 虽然unsafe代码可以带来性能上的提升，但也有开发者对其可能引入的安全隐患表示担忧，认为需要在性能和安全性之间找到平衡。

Description
qwen3-rs
is an educational Rust project for exploring and running Qwen3 language family models. It is designed to be clear, modular, and approachable for learners, with minimal dependencies and many core algorithms reimplemented from scratch for transparency.
Note:
Parts of this codebase, including documentation and core algorithms, were generated or assisted by large language models (LLMs) to accelerate development and improve educational clarity. As a starting reference, the project
qwen3.c
was used for understanding model internals and file formats.
Project Goals
Educational:
Learn how transformer architectures, quantization, and efficient inference work in Rust.
Minimal Dependencies:
Most algorithms (tokenization, quantization, sampling, etc.) are implemented from scratch—no heavy ML or Python bindings.
Modular:
Core library logic is separated from CLI tools for clarity and maintainability.
Efficiency:
Uses memory mapping and zero-copy techniques for handling large model files.
Workspace Structure
qwen3-rs/
├── docs                # LLM generated docs for key components
├── Cargo.toml          # Workspace configuration
├── qwen3-cli/          # Command-line interface crate
├── qwen3-export/       # Model export crate
├── qwen3-inference/    # LLM inference crate
How to Use
1. Get a HuggingFace Qwen3 model
git clone https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
#
Or try larger/alternative models:
#
git clone https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B
#
git clone https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B
#
git clone https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
2. Build and run the exporter
cargo build --release -p qwen3-cli
#
Export a HuggingFace model to quantized checkpoint format
cargo run --release -p qwen3-cli --
export
/path/to/model /path/to/output.bin --group-size 64
3. Run inference
In chat mode with default parameters:
cargo run --release -p qwen3-cli -- inference /path/to/output.bin -m chat
CLI Commands and Options
export
Exports a HuggingFace Qwen3 model to a custom binary format for efficient Rust inference.
Usage:
qwen3
export
<
MODEL_PATH
>
<
OUTPUT_PATH
>
[--group-size
<
SIZE
>
]
MODEL_PATH
: Path to HuggingFace model directory (must contain config.json, *.safetensors, tokenizer.json)
OUTPUT_PATH
: Output path for the binary model file
--group-size
,
-g
: Quantization group size (default: 64)
inference
Runs inference on a binary Qwen3 model.
Usage:
qwen3 inference
<
checkpoint
>
[options]
Options:
--temperature
,
-t <FLOAT>
: Sampling temperature (default: 1.0)
--topp
,
-p <FLOAT>
: Top-p nucleus sampling (default: 0.9)
--seed
,
-s <INT>
: Random seed
--context
,
-c <INT>
: Context window size (default: max_seq_len)
--mode
,

: Mode:
generate
or
chat
(default: chat)

,

: Input prompt
--system
,

: System prompt (for chat mode)
--reasoning
,

: Reasoning mode: 0=no thinking, 1=thinking (default: 0)

data.article_summary: 该项目使用数字电视棒（RTL-SDR）接收433Mhz的门铃信号，并通过MQTT发送警报。作者由于在家工作时难以听到门铃声，便利用现有的RTL-SDR和相关软件（如RTL_433）捕获和解析信号，通过Python的Paho MQTT客户端发布MQTT消息。项目详细介绍了所需的硬件、软件配置、信号捕捉与解码过程，以及如何将信号接入Node-RED和Telegram实现通知功能。整个过程灵活且低成本，适用于家庭自动化场景。

doorbell-interceptor
This project uses a Digital TV dongle (RTL-SDR) to receive signals on 433Mhz and post alerts via MQTT.
Background
Whilst my house isn't huge, it can be a struggle to hear the doorbell from the loft room where I've found myself working during lockdown (and beyond).  It's a bog-standard wireless variety from Volex, and I didn't fancy shelling out a fortune for a Ring, and had the technology lying around to try to pick up the signal.
I had intended to use an ESP8266 and a superheterodyne 433Mhz receiver with OpenMQTTGateway for this, but as it turned out, my doorbell doesn't quite transmit on 433.9Mhz like everyone else's, but on 434.0Mhz.
I had an RTL-SDR dongle to hand (which I used to verify the frequency) and was able to use this to pick up the signal.  More of a sledgehammer than the ESP solution but extremely flexible.
I'm using Windows here but all the below is supported on Linux.  I'm definitely standing on the shoulders of giants with the great libraries and resources that are out there.
Requirements
Any RTL-SDR dongle, mostly available for under $10 on Aliexpress or Banggood.
The fantastic RTL_433 from
https://github.com/merbanan/rtl_433
Python 3.x
Paho MQTT Client (
pip install paho-mqtt
)
Optional: SDR# from
https://airspy.com/download/
Discovery
Verify the frequency
Fire up SDR# (you may need to install the relevant drivers for the dongle with Zadig)
Tune to around 433.9Mhz
Send your signal
You should see something like this:
Great, you can see your doorbell signal!
You may need to tune around if you don't see it around 433.9Mhz as I did.
Decode the signal
RTL_433 can analyse the signals being received and produce a general purpose decoder to help pinpoint that signal amongst the others.
Run
rtl_433 -A
to start analysing and press the doorbell.
This should give you an output like this:
This has recognised the signal as being pulse-width modulation, and has calculated the short and long widths of the pulses, and even given us the code we need to produce a flex-decoder!
It also shows the binary code produced by the doorbell.
Let's check the flex decoder by running rtL_433 again with the flex decoder, so in my case:
rtl_433 -X "n=doorbell,m=OOK_PWM,s=372,l=716,r=5356,g=684,t=136,y=0,match={13}0xad08,repeats>=3"
You should see the signals being received with these characteristics, and nothing else - perfect!
Producing MQTT packets
I ended up adapting the code from:
https://github.com/mverleun/RTL433-to-mqtt
As I needed to provide a flex decoder, I ended up putting this into an array for the command and calling this in subprocess.Popen.  I also had to adapt the line that publishes the MQTT packet as it was creating duplicates, but the above code does all the heavy lifting of connecting to the MQTT broker and publishing the signal from RTL433.
Into Node-RED...
I use Node-RED for various bits of home automation and it will happily take an MQTT packet and do something with it.  I use Telegram bots to receive updates on my phone (and send commands back).
...and out to Telegram
There's an awesome and comprehensive Node for Telegram at:
https://flows.nodered.org/node/node-red-contrib-telegrambot
.
There's loads of docs for that so I won't go into detail here, but you'll basically need to use the Sender node and create a function to generate the message:
msg
.
payload
=
{
chatId
:
YOURCHATID
,
type
:
'message'
,
content
:
"There's someone at the door!"
}
return
msg
;
All done!

主要讨论点：如何有效地选择销售渠道并找到目标客户

不同观点：
• muzani 认为选择正确的销售渠道是关键，不局限于LinkedIn，还可以利用TikTok、广告平台、Tumblr、Pinterest、Discord和Facebook群组等多样化平台。他强调PMF（产品市场契合度）不仅仅是获得前10个客户，如果没有找到合适的市场或产品亮点，可能需要重新评估市场定位，而不是改变产品本身。此外，他指出依赖人际网络是低效的营销方式。

• mips_avatar 建议通过面对面的方式销售产品，认为这种更脆弱和直接的方式能获得更多回应。

• codingdave 提出应重新联系最初的10个测试用户，通过他们的反馈和口碑传播来获取更多客户。

• vinibrito 认为缺乏网络是主要问题，建议直接与潜在客户交谈。

• mortsmel 分享了自己失败的经验，强调了市场营销和目标客户选择的重要性。他建议通过LinkedIn的高级联系人搜索、广告服务（如Facebook、Google）、以及其他预算较低的广告平台（如vibe.co和caasie.co）来获取客户。他还提到以女性为目标消费者可能是一个有效的策略，并建议加入商会来推销服务。

补充讨论：
• bell-cot 指出不同领域的客户需求差异巨大，如企业客户与小企业或学前教育客户的需求截然不同，强调了针对不同市场需要不同的策略。

争议焦点：
• 关于是否依赖人际网络进行营销存在争议。muzani 认为依赖网络是低效的，而 mortsmel 则强调了通过建立关系获取客户的重要性。

• 选择销售渠道和目标市场的策略存在不同看法。muzani 主张多样化渠道，而其他评论者更倾向于面对面销售、口碑传播或通过广告直接触达客户。

整体讨论显示出在寻找产品市场契合度和有效营销策略中的复杂性，以及根据不同市场需求调整策略的必要性。

data.title: Bcachefs Lands Fixes in Linux 6.16 for Some "High Severity" Regressions
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: 在Linux 6.16-rc6版本发布前，Bcachefs文件系统修复了一些“高严重性”回归问题。Bcachefs的主要开发者Kent Overstreet提交了一个包含多个修复的请求，包括调整b-tree缓存助手、b-tree节点扫描不再使用缓存、修复b-tree读取重试等。这些修复已被Linus Torvalds合并，将在Linux 6.16-rc6中发布。不过，Torvalds尚未明确Bcachefs未来在主线内核中的计划，仅表示在6.17版本中Bcachefs将与主线“分道扬镳”，但未说明是否移除或暂时搁置该文件系统。目前，Bcachefs的修复仍被接受用于Linux 6.16。

44544996.article_content:
Bcachefs Lands Fixes In Linux 6.16 For Some "High Severity" Regressions
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Linux Storage
on 12 July 2025 at 03:21 PM EDT.
9 Comments
Ahead of tomorrow's Linux 6.16-rc6 kernel release a number of Bcachefs file-system fixes were merged.
On Friday the Bcachefs lead developer Kent Overstreet sent out
a pull request
containing the latest Bcachefs fixes. This includes a number of fixes, tweaking the b-tree cache helpers, b-tree node scans no longer using the cache, b-tree read retry fixes, and various other fixes.
Overstreet followed-up today to the Bcachefs pull request by
noting
:
"These are fixes for some high severity 6.16 regressions."
Linus Torvalds has now merged all of these Bcachefs file-system fixes in time for Sunday's Linux 6.16-rc6 release.
Torvalds hasn't commented any further on what he plans to do about this file-system moving forward. Torvalds commented last month that Bcachefs and the mainline Linux kernel would be
"parting ways in the 6.17 merge window"
without elaborating if he plans to outright remove all the Bcachefs code from the mainline kernel, gate it behind the "BROKEN" Kconfig option, do another time-out for a kernel cycle, or what exactly will happen to this copy-on-write open-source file-system moving forward in the mainline kernel. We'll see but for now Bcachefs fixes are still being accepted for Linux 6.16.
9 Comments

data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了长尺度与短尺度两种命名大数的方法。作者在童年时学习的是长尺度系统，其中百万乘以百万是十亿，百万乘以自身三次是万亿，依次类推。每个前缀清晰地表示乘以百万的次数，非常直观。然而，进入大学并接触计算机和互联网后，作者发现短尺度系统更为普遍，在短尺度中，百万乘以百万是万亿，百万乘以三次是 quintillion，这与长尺度差异显著。短尺度通过每增加一千的倍数来命名，例如，从一千开始，每多乘一个一千，就形成更大的单位。尽管短尺度不如长尺度直观，但如今在技术、金融和大多数英语语境中广泛使用。作者最终适应了短尺度，但长尺度的记忆仍留在心中。

Million Times Million
By
Susam Pal
on 03 Jul 2025
Is a million times a million a
billion
or is it
a
trillion
?  For my entire childhood, it was a billion,
only for me to grow up and realise, as an adult, that it had better
be a trillion!
Growing Up With the Long Scale
As a child, I stumbled upon an old dictionary lying around our
house, and that was where I discovered the names of large numbers.
The dictionary used the long scale system, which is based on powers
of a million.  According to the long scale system,
a million times a million is a billion,
a million times a million times a million is a trillion,
a million multiplied by itself four times is a quadrillion,
multiply it five times and we get a quintillion,
and so on.
These long scale names made a lot of sense to me.  Each name told us
exactly how many times we multiplied a million by itself.  The
little prefix at the start, like
bi-
,
tri-
,
quadri-
,
quinti-
, etc.  matched the number of
times a million appeared in the multiplication: twice for a billion,
three times for a trillion, and so on.  If I came across a number
like quintillion, I immediately knew it meant a million multiplied
by itself five times, so a quintillion had to be \( (10^6)^5 =
10^{30}.  \)  It was simple, straightforward, and intuitive!
Now imagine my disappointment when I left home for university, got
access to computers and the World Wide Web, and discovered that the
names I had learnt were off by several orders of magnitude compared
with what everyone else was using.  The long scale names I had grown
up with were irrelevant in this new world I was stepping into.  It
was the short scale that had taken over most of the technology
world, especially in computing.  In the short scale, a million times
a million is no longer a billion.  Instead, somehow, it is a
trillion!  Similarly, a million multiplied three times is no longer
a trillion.  It is a quintillion!  What on earth was going on?
Naturally, I had to go through a period of adjustment, letting go of
my old intuition for the long scale names and getting used to the
short scale ones.  At the same time, I found a way to trick my mind
into making sense of the short scale.  Before I get into the mental
gymnastics that made the short scale click for me, let us first take
a quick look at the long scale and short scale names side by side.
Same Names, Different Numbers
The long scale and short scale are simply two different ways of
naming large numbers.  To see how they differ, here is a table
showing what each name corresponds to in the two systems.
Number
Long Scale
Short Scale
\( 10^6 \)
Million
Million
\( 10^9 \)
Milliard
Billion
\( 10^{12} \)
Billion
Trillion
\( 10^{15} \)
Billiard
Quadrillion
\( 10^{18} \)
Trillion
Quintillion
\( 10^{21} \)
Trilliard
Sextillion
\( 10^{24} \)
Quadrillion
Septillion
\( 10^{27} \)
Quadrilliard
Octillion
\( 10^{30} \)
Quintillion
Nonillion
\( 10^{33} \)
Quintilliard
Decillion
As the table shows, the two systems agree on the value of a million,
but diverge immediately after.  From that point on, the same names
represent increasingly different magnitudes.
Making Sense of the Short Scale
I used to quite like the long scale names because the prefix in each
name is determined by how many times we multiply a million by
itself.  Each prefix reflects the value of \( n \) in the number \(
10^{6n}, \) where \( n \) is a positive integer.  For example, if \(
n = 3, \) we get \( 10^{18}, \) which in the long scale is called
a
trillion
.  But in the short scale, the same number is
called a
quintillion
.  How can we make sense of it?
One way to interpret the short scale is to count how many additional
thousands are multiplied onto one thousand.  A thousand is, of
course, just
one thousand
.  Multiply it by another thousand
and we get a
million
.  Multiply that by another thousand
and we get a
billion
.  One more multiplication gives us
a
trillion
, and so on.  I do not find this quite as neat as
the long scale but it works!
In effect, the prefix in the short scale corresponds to \( n \) of
the integer \( 1000 \times 1000^n, \) where \( n \) is a positive
integer.  Stated more succinctly, it represents \( n \) of \(
10^{3(n + 1)}.  \)  So for example, if \( n = 5, \) then
\[
10^{3(n + 1)} = 10^{18},
\]
which is called a
quintillion
in the short scale.  The
quinti-
prefix still represents five but now it is tied to
the number of additional thousands we multiplied to the first
thousand.  It is not quite the elegant pattern I grew up with but
this is the convention that dominates today.  In the world of
technology, computing, and finance, as well as in most
English-speaking contexts, the short scale has prevailed.
Conclusion
Today, of course, I use only the short scale, because that is the
convention adopted by the part of the world relevant to me.  I no
longer use the long scale.  But it remains in memory, simply because
I spent a large part of my early life with it.  It still lives in
some corner of my heart, pa

data.title: The Biggest-Ever Digital Camera Is This Cosmologist's Magnum Opus
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了宇宙学家Tony Tyson及其研发的史上最大数码相机——位于Vera C. Rubin天文台的32亿像素相机。Tyson自20世纪70年代起在贝尔实验室开始使用电荷耦合器件（CCD）技术，致力于研究宇宙中的暗物质。他的团队通过弱引力透镜效应绘制了暗物质地图，并为后来发现暗能量的研究奠定了基础。Tyson于1990年代启动了Rubin天文台项目，该天文台的巨型相机将在未来十年内拍摄约200亿个星系，帮助科学家深入研究占据宇宙95%的暗物质和暗能量。这台相机被视为Tyson的巅峰之作，标志着天文学进入了一个超高清新时代。

The Biggest-Ever Digital Camera Is This Cosmologist’s Magnum Opus
By
Jenna Ahart

Tony Tyson’s cameras revealed the universe’s dark contents. Now, with the Rubin Observatory’s 3.2-billion-pixel camera, he’s ready to study dark matter and dark energy in unprecedented detail.

For decades, Tony Tyson has been building increasingly large CCD cameras for astronomy.

On June 23, 2025, Tony Tyson joined a presentation in Washington, D.C., to unveil an image almost 30 years in the making: 10 million galaxies poised on an inky black backdrop. To appreciate each galaxy in detail, you’d have to stretch the picture across 400 TVs. It’s the first portrait of the cosmos delivered by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, a new astronomical facility built by the United States on a mountain in Chile. And it captures just 0.05% of the galaxies that the observatory’s mammoth camera will record over the next decade.
That camera is ushering in an ultra-vivid new era of astronomy; it’s also Tyson’s magnum opus.
Tyson, a cosmologist at the University of California, Davis and the chief scientist of the Rubin Observatory, was working at Bell Labs in the 1970s when he encountered a novel imaging chip called a charge-coupled device (CCD) and realized that it could revolutionize the study of the universe. By converting incoming light into electrical signals, CCD sensors are well suited for detecting faint, distant objects in the cosmos. Tyson used the technology to make
the first high-resolution map of dark matter
, the mysterious, heavy substance that binds galaxies together like an invisible glue.
Then, in the 1990s, other astronomers used one of Tyson’s CCD cameras to study the expansion of the universe and discovered what seemed like a mistake at the time: The expansion was ramping up. The peculiar acceleration revealed the presence of dark energy.
Today, dark matter and dark energy — together composing 95% of the contents of the universe — remain utter mysteries. Even in the 1990s, Tyson knew that to illuminate these dark entities, he’d need to study them with a bigger camera, so he founded the project that has become the Rubin Observatory. Now 85, he is finally introducing his brainchild to the world.
An array of 189 CCDs totaling 3.2 billion pixels, the Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) camera is the largest digital camera ever built. Over the next 10 years, it will repeatedly photograph approximately 20 billion galaxies. Among other things, the photo album will chronicle the convoluted history of how dark matter and dark energy conspired to carve out the structure of our universe.

Can you walk me through how you created a map of dark matter?
I was always interested, even as a kid, in measuring things that were almost undetectable — really, really faint signals, first in the radio and then optical wavelengths. Bell Labs gave me free rein to engineer new systems that would detect those extremely faint signals. One day, George Smith [co-inventer of the charge-coupled device] came into my office and said, “You know, with your interest in astronomy, you might be interested in this.” It was this little thing that was a couple millimeters long, known nowadays as a CCD.
At the time, I was really interested in how galaxies look like they’ve been moved by all of this invisible dark matter in between us and them. The galaxy’s light gets distorted by the gravity of the dark matter, so the image of the galaxy becomes elongated, turning into a little arc. So I developed a very simple detector with CCDs that looks for this telltale arc-iness around the sky. The term is called weak gravitational lensing. When you detect the mirage, you can invert the map to see the distribution of the dark matter.

data.title: Switching to Claude Code and VSCode Inside Docker
data.author: timsh
data.article_summary: 作者分享了从旧的AI编码设置（使用ChatGPT Plus和Cursor Pro）切换到在Docker中运行Claude Code的经历，并提供了简要指南和代码链接。他提到之前设置的问题包括Cursor Pro的响应缓慢和新的请求限制不合理，以及对AI代理安全性的担忧，特别是它们能访问整个文件系统和终端。为解决这些问题，作者选择使用Claude的20美元订阅，并通过Docker容器限制其访问权限，以提高安全性。这种方法让他能以更低的成本获得更好的编码体验，同时确保系统安全。作者提供了详细的操作指南和代码，供其他有类似需求的用户参考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开发环境中的容器使用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [CGamesPlay] 认为即使不喜欢 VSCode，也可以使用微软开发的 devcontainer CLI 实现类似功能，但需要手动处理端口转发等问题。他开发了一个工具来处理部分端口转发功能，但承认尚未达到 VSCode 的自动化程度。
• [mkagenius] 提出了使用 Apple 内置容器技术（container）的替代方案，强调其速度和与 Claude Code 等工具的良好集成，并开源了 CodeRunner 工具。他指出该方案仅适用于 M1/M2/M3/M4 的 Mac 设备。
• [sothatsit] 分享了使用 Claude Code 在容器中运行的优势，特别是可以轻松启动后台任务，且能够轻松放弃不满意的结果。他认为容器的安全性不是主要考量，因为 Git 可以逆转大多数操作。
• [hintymad] 对使用容器开发的必要性提出质疑，认为配置容器可能带来额外麻烦，不如直接在本地开发简单。
• [photonthug] 强调了容器在开发和测试中的一致性和可重现性优势，认为这对于 AI 开发尤为重要，可以避免系统污染和复杂的依赖管理。
• [ed_mercer] 对使用 Claude Code 的安全性表示乐观，认为只要合理使用（如编写 CLAUDE.md 文件），不会出现严重问题。
• [scosman] 偏好使用 ChatGPT Codex 而非 Claude Code，因为前者在云端容器中运行，降低了本地环境风险，并且可以并行运行多个实例。
• [crawshaw] 指出容器非常适合运行代理任务，可以执行如安装工具或调试等高权限操作，而不影响本地环境。
• [tosh] 提到在 macOS 上使用 devcontainer 的优点和缺点，如减少 CLI 工具调用失败，但也会遇到通知功能和剪贴板使用等问题。
• [intellectronica] 推荐使用 Claude Code 的开源替代品，可以在任意环境中运行，并根据用户需求自定义模型和经济安排。
• [tkiolp4] 认为在容器或虚拟机中开发是常见做法，可以避免在本地运行不安全的安装命令如 npm 或 pip。
• [lvl155] 指出在 M1 设备上使用 Docker 存在不便，特别是需要安装不受欢迎的 Docker Desktop 软件，并呼吁更 robust 的开箱即用工具。
• [asadm] 对使用模型时的安全性表示乐观，认为即使不使用沙箱环境，也未遇到严重问题。
• [tartakovsky] 对使用容器是否过度担忧提出疑问，并质疑 AI 代码生成服务提供商为何不提供更安全的容器化服务。
• [abrookewood] 提到像 Phoenix 这样的工具提供了一种 AI 代理完全控制环境的方式，可以在不影响本地环境的情况下运行系统工具。

补充讨论：
• 容器化开发的主要争议点在于其配置复杂性和必要性，部分开发者认为其带来的一致性和隔离性优势明显，而另一些开发者则认为直接在本地开发更简单。
• 安全性是容器化开发的一个重要考量，尤其是在处理高权限任务和敏感数据时，但部分开发者认为只要合理使用，Claude Code 等工具并不会带来严重安全问题。
• 使用容器或虚拟机的替代方案，如 Apple 内置容器技术，也提供了另一种快速集成和开发的可能性，但受限于特定硬件。

44533044.article_content:
Last night I finished a transition from my old AI coding setup I've been using for a while to running Claude Code in Docker using VSCode's "Dev Container" feature.
In this post I lay out a few of my thoughts on why I wanted to switch to something in the first place, and also a short guide for those who want to do the same.
If you are here just for the guide + code (a tiny single file), here it is:
https://github.com/tim-sha256/claude-in-docker
🥺
Important note!
I'm not a professional vibecoder (thanks god) and I don't generate AI code on 9-5 basis (meh)
I'm just a casual user occasionally getting help from llms on my projects, all of them being not corporate-serious-guys-enterprise-grade.
I'm not looking for the most advanced 100x dev tools or workflows, nor $100+ subscriptions whose token limits I'll probably only reach once a year on a sleepless night.
Before and why
Until yesterday I've been using such setup:
ChatGPT Plus 20$ subscription for occasional chats mostly unrelated to code, except for quickies and desperate attempts to feed o3 a bunch of code that Claude can't crack and get it all solved (mostly unsuccessful).
Cursor Pro for additional 20$ (or how do they call it these days?) - for all "serious" coding.
Which works all right, is convenient (been stuck with Cursor since August '24 and GPT since '23 without actively seeking an alternative), but has a couple issues that started to bug me recently.
Issue 1: I'm greedy and I want my responses fast
Before Cursor went into drain-users stage recently, I did not use up all 500 requests / month not a single time while working on 1-2 projects during my free time (approx. 40-60 hours a month).
Maybe I could've paid less on token-based plan, but I didn't really care – $20 is $20 :)
But after their update removing the 500 requests limit "so you can enjoy unlimited requests to almost any model", I've been extremely upset by Cursor due to their inadequate rate limits.
Sometimes I would type a prompt for Sonnet 4 (not even Opus...) and wait for 2-5 minutes for anything to happen, which is a complaint I've seen quite a lot in Cursor-related chats and on Reddit.
There is an option to switch back to a proprietary and seemingly not as profitable 500 requests pricing mode, but I don't think it'll last much longer.  Or use the free version and go out for a smoke break after every request.
Which led me to think about my spending and the satisfaction I get in return: is it still worth 40$ or is there a better way?
Well, for now I've settled with Claude 20$ subscription and consider it a better fit for my use case for a couple of reasons:
$20 is less than 40$
I still get to send a pic of a shelf with various cleaning products to some chat app on my phone and ask "Which of these do I need to do X?", which works surprisingly well almost all the time
I have a similar-or-even-better web chat experience to work on stuff unrelated to code
Finally, and most importantly – I get Claude Code with:
reasonable limits
clear token spending indication
everybody constantly says Claude Code rocks, right?
I like cli stuff in general
vs code integration makes the IDE experience essentially the same (or even a bit better)
Ok, looks like I'm settled for now, end of story. Or what else?
Issue 2: I'm trying to be realistic about AI Agent security
Simply put: I believe running an AI Agent that has access to your entire file system, terminal and secrets is dangerous and will eventually lead to some problems.
Think of it as if you gave access to your computer to a cheap overseas freelance dev who you don't really know and can only chat with. How does that sound?
I stumble upon llm security-related stuff every day and occasionally read some of it. And generally, the situation is not getting better.
For instance, I've seen around 10 posts about very serious vulnerabilities in MCPs like
this one,
a few sad stories where cursor decided to delete something useful like all Ableton projects using
rm -rf
, and even threads saying that Claude
learned to bypass Cursor built-in command blacklist
in Yolo mode.
Basically, you have a choice: either accept each single command manually (which I think is a reasonable approach but I'm too lazy) or trust the above mentioned freelancer with everything you have and hope that some barriers will stop it and nothing bad will happen.
Or are there any other options?
Now and why
Ok, so I want to use Claude Code, but at the same time want to restrict it somehow so it can't fuck up my entire computer.
First idea which came to me turned to be the one that I'd go with (who could've thought): put that thing into a box with nothing but the project(s) in it, give it the least possible access and close the box.
In other words, launch Claude Code in Docker and work on the project inside the container.
What you get from that:
Claude can only access files from inside the container or in the provided volumes, mounted or not
It also most certainly can't break anything outside the con

data.title: Chrome's hidden X-Browser-Validation header reverse engineered
data.author: dsekz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个针对Chrome浏览器私有头部"x-browser-validation"的反向工程与生成工具。该头部用于完整性验证，确保用户代理与平台匹配，防止伪造。该头部通过连接平台特定的API密钥和用户代理字符串，使用SHA-1算法进行哈希，然后进行Base64编码生成。文章提供了生成该头部的Python代码示例，并详细描述了反向工程过程，包括在Chrome二进制文件中找到相关函数和算法。最终确认该头部的生成过程为：API密钥 + 用户代理字符串 → SHA-1哈希 → Base64编码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Chrome浏览器中新增的"x-browser-validation" header的目的及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [技术分析与用途猜测]  
  - [dsekz] 分析了chrome.dll并弄清了"x-browser-validation" header的生成方式，提到这可能与反欺诈、机器人检测或完整性验证有关。
  - [jakub_g] 猜测该header可能与Google企业工作区中的某个功能相关，该功能允许管理员限制仅Chrome浏览器登录Google服务。

• [反竞争担忧]  
  - [userbinator] 担心该header是Google通过法律手段打压竞争、巩固垄断地位的尝试，并提到历史案例Sega v. Accolade。同时对使用SHA-1算法表示质疑。
  - [thayne] 指出Google在反垄断诉讼失败后仍采取此类措施令人不解，认为该header可能被用于反竞争行为，但也指出该header被逆向工程后可能被伪造。

• [隐私与指纹识别问题]  
  - [cebert] 认为该header是为了区分代理请求和人类请求，但同时指出这可能被用于唯一识别用户的指纹识别技术，令人愤怒。

• [公共与私有网络争议]  
  - [binary132] 认为Google有权构建自己的私有网络，但担心他们试图将整个互联网变成他们的私有网络。

补充讨论：
• [技术实现与影响]  
  - [RandyOrion] 提问该header最早在哪个Chrome版本中实现，并关注其对Chromium分支（如ungoogled chromium）的潜在影响。
  
• [用户操作与安全性]  
  - [Larrikin] 询问如何在Firefox中设置该header。
  - [aussieguy1234] 认为该header类似于隐藏的客户端认证。
  - [Everdred2dx] 担心使用用户代理伪造扩展可能导致"真实"用户代理被猜测。

• [法律与版权问题]  
  - [_imnothere] 质疑为何允许这种验证机制存在。
  - [delusional] 讨论了该header是否受版权保护，以及伪造该header是否构成侵犯版权，提出了一种有趣的法律可能性。

争议焦点：Google新增的"x-browser-validation" header是否涉及反竞争行为及对用户隐私的影响。

Chrome X-Browser-Validation Header Reverse Engineering & Generator
Chrome recently added a few new headers:
"x-browser-channel": "stable",
"x-browser-copyright": "Copyright 2025 Google LLC. All rights reserved.",
"x-browser-validation": "6h3XF8YcD8syi2FF2BbuE2KllQo=",
"x-browser-year": "2025"
Apart from one of them, there isn’t much that’s interesting. They’re just bits of client specific information. However, base64 decoding x-browser-validation yields what appears to be a hash whose purpose remains undocumented.
Chrome almost certainly uses this header as an integrity signal. Verifying that the declared user agent matches the underlying platform, spotting user agent string spoofing attempts etc.

in IDA. The master routine

etc):

Hash - passes that buffer into

, which is SHA-1 algo. Open this guy and the first assignment jumps out:
v12

The second you see that "-1009589776" number, you can literally smell SHA-1.
Base64 - the 20-byte digest is encoded.
Dynamic confirmation: pause one instruction before the hash call, dump RDX, and the ~150-byte buffer is nothing but
<API_KEY><User-Agent>
Base64(SHA-1(buffer)) = header. Mystery solved.

data.title: Hacking Coroutines into C
data.author: jmillikin
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在一个嵌入式软件项目中，如何通过将协程概念引入C语言来简化状态机的实现。传统的状态机方法在处理多个状态和事件时，代码难以维护和理解。作者受高级语言中协程的启发，提出了一种在不使用操作系统的情况下实现类似协程的并发处理方法。文章通过一个LED闪烁控制和按钮按下时间记录的例子，展示了如何用状态机和轮询机制实现功能。虽然这种方法可行，但代码复杂且不易读。作者建议引入类似协程的机制，以简化逻辑流和状态管理，从而提高代码的可读性和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在C语言中实现轻量级协程和状态机的不同方法及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **adinisom** 支持使用基于结构体的轻量级Protothreads实现，通过`YIELD()`宏和手动状态管理，实现协程功能。他认为这种方法可以很好地结合声明式和过程式代码，并且在处理硬件相关代码时非常有效。
• **astrobe_** 认为状态机的控制流本质上是非线性的，使用goto语句可能会更清晰。他指出，状态机的可视化和模块化是一个问题，并建议使用图形化的DSL工具来解决。
• **mikepurvis** 提到FreeRTOS也可以使用协作式调度器，并倾向于使用真正的代码生成而不是宏来实现协程，以提高代码的可读性和调试能力。
• **userbinator** 认为使用PWM外设或定时器中断可以让CPU大部分时间处于 halt 状态，从而简化问题，比手动实现状态机更简单。
• **syncurrent** 提到同步语言如Esterel或Blech的类似方法，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。
• **jonhohle** 分享了他使用libaco处理事件和流解压的经验，认为这种方法可以让代码保持线性结构。
• **Neywiny** 表示不喜欢在软件中使用状态机，认为状态机更适合硬件实现。他主张函数应根据需要写得尽量长，避免不必要的函数调用。

data.title: A.I. Is Making Sure You Pay for That Ding on Your Rental Car
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：租车公司（尤其是Hertz）在处理归还车辆时的费用争议和流程问题

不同观点：
• **流程不透明和事后收费不合理**：[remram] 认为，归还车辆时，如果工作人员没有当场指出损坏，而事后收到账单，这种做法不合理。应该在归还时立即扫描车辆并当场结账。
• **现行流程的缺陷**：[legitster] 指出当前流程存在缺陷，检查人员培训不足，且检查不够严谨，但认为Hertz并非故意不公，流程至少是透明的。
• **保险和额外收费的目的**：[pseudolus] 和 [t1234s] 认为，租车公司通过高额保险（如碰撞损坏险）来增加收入，目的是让租客购买更多保险，从而增加租车成本。
• **Hertz品牌形象的衰退**：[alwa] 和 [kjellsbells] 提到Hertz曾经是 prestige brand，但目前品牌形象不佳，存在财务问题和管理混乱，甚至存在敲诈消费者的行为。
• **未来竞争和流程改善**：[benced] 认为，随着市场竞争和公众关注，流程会逐渐改善，变得更合理。
• **旅行保险的替代作用**：[boznz] 建议在国外租车时，可以通过旅行保险覆盖超额费用，这样可以避免购买昂贵的租车保险。
• **Hertz的法律和信誉问题**：[kevingadd] 引用了Hertz错误指控客户盗窃的案例，认为不应该与Hertz交易，并建议购买全险以避免麻烦。

补充讨论：
• **对新技术的担忧和抵制**：[schrodinger] 提出一种极端假设，即在扫描前后故意损坏车辆以测试系统如何处理，暗示对新技术的担忧。[eggn00dles] 则认为这是公司在测试公众对新技术的反应。
• **简单建议不使用Hertz**：[chris_wot] 和 [mrangle] 直接建议不使用Hertz，基于其不合理的收费和过去的负面经验。

争议焦点：
• 租车公司是否故意利用事后收费和保险费用来敲诈消费者，以及现行流程是否透明公正。
• 新技术和自动化在租车费用争议中的应用是否会导致更多问题。

总结：讨论主要围绕租车公司在处理车辆归还和损坏费用上的透明度和公正性，以及消费者如何通过保险和其他手段保护自己免受不合理收费的影响。同时，对新技术的引入存在一定的担忧和抵制。
