(cs)
[Submitted on 10 Jul 2025]
Title:
Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling
Authors:
Sukjun Hwang
,
Brandon Wang
,
Albert Gu
View a PDF of the paper titled Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, by Sukjun Hwang and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Despite incredible progress in language models (LMs) in recent years, largely resulting from moving away from specialized models designed for specific tasks to general models based on powerful architectures (e.g. the Transformer) that learn everything from raw data, pre-processing steps such as tokenization remain a barrier to true end-to-end foundation models. We introduce a collection of new techniques that enable a dynamic chunking mechanism which automatically learns content -- and context -- dependent segmentation strategies learned jointly with the rest of the model. Incorporating this into an explicit hierarchical network (H-Net) allows replacing the (implicitly hierarchical) tokenization-LM-detokenization pipeline with a single model learned fully end-to-end. When compute- and data- matched, an H-Net with one stage of hierarchy operating at the byte level outperforms a strong Transformer language model operating over BPE tokens. Iterating the hierarchy to multiple stages further increases its performance by modeling multiple levels of abstraction, demonstrating significantly better scaling with data and matching a token-based Transformer of twice its size. H-Nets pretrained on English show significantly increased character-level robustness, and qualitatively learn meaningful data-dependent chunking strategies without any heuristics or explicit supervision. Finally, the H-Net's improvement over tokenized pipelines is further increased in languages and modalities with weaker tokenization heuristics, such as Chinese and code, or DNA sequences (nearly 4x improvement in data efficiency over baselines), showing the potential of true end-to-end models that learn and scale better from unprocessed data.

data.title: Daniel Stenberg of Curl on how and why he does it
data.author: navs
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了他如何保持每周持续更新新闻通讯的动力和专注，特别是围绕他主导的curl项目。他描述了自己的工作不仅限于编码，还包括指导项目发展、处理安全报告、参与互联网协议的讨论以及与其他开源项目的互动。他通过商业客户的支持得以全职投入curl，并感到对项目的成功负有重大责任，致力于使其成为最安全、文档最完善的开源项目。他的日常工作包括处理问题、拉取请求和项目维护，通常从早上8点工作到晚上6点，有时会因时差在晚上继续工作。他的动力来自于对编程的热爱、对用户的责任感以及不断改进项目的愿望。

• 评论也暗示了开源项目的成功不仅仅是技术能力的体现，还涉及到个人的多面能力和持续的努力。

44548957.article_content:
A while ago I received an email with this question.
I’ve been subscribed to your
weekly newsletter
for a while now, receiving your weekly updates every Friday. I’m writing because I admire your consistency, focus, and perseverance. I can’t help but wonder, with admiration, how you manage to do it.
Since this is a topic I receive questions about semi-regularly, I decided I would attempt to answer it. I have probably touched the subject in previous blog posts as well.
Work
Let me start out by defining what I consider my primary work to be. Or perhaps I should call it my
mission
because it goes way beyond just “work”. curl is irrevocably a huge part of me and my life.
I drive the curl project. Guide, develop, review, comment, admin, debug, merge, commit, support, assess security reports, lead, release, talk about it, inspire etc.
It does not necessarily mean that I do the most number of commits to curl every month. We have a set of very skilled and devoted committers that can do a lot without me.
I keep up with relevant Internet protocol developments and make sure to give feedback on what I think is good and bad, in particular from a small player’s/library’s view that is sometimes a bit different than the tech giants’ takes. This means participating actively in some IETF groups and keeping myself informed about what is happening in a number of other HTTP, web and browser oriented communities.
I keep up with related technologies and Open Source projects to understand how to navigate. Feedback issues, comments and pull requests to neighbor projects that we use – to strengthen them (and then by association the combination curl + them) and to increase the chances that they will help us out in similar fashion.
I use my position as lead developer of curl to blog and speak up about things I think need to be said, explained or giggled at. Be it stupid emails, bad uses of AI or inefficient security organizations. Ideally this occasionally helps other people and projects as well.
As a successful Open Source project I acknowledge and am aware that we (I mean curl) might get more attention than some others, and that we are used as or considered a “model” sometimes, making it even more important to do things right. From my language use in public to source code decisions. I try to live up to these expectations.
A part of my job is to make companies become paying customers so that I can afford working on curl – and once they have become customers I need to every now and then attend to support tickets from them. I can work full-time on curl thanks to my commercial customers.
Why
I have a strong sense of loyalty and commitment. When I join a project or a cause, I typically stick around and do my share of the job until it is finished.
I enjoy programming and software development – and I have done so ever since I first learned about programming as a teen in the mid 1980s. It is fun to create something that is useful and that can be used by others, but I also like solving the puzzles and challenges that come up in the process.
When the  software project you work on never finishes, and is used by a crazy amount of users it gives you a sense of responsibility and
pride
. An even bigger incentive to make sure it actually works as intended. A desire to please the users. All the users.
Even after having reached many
billions
of installations there are still challenges to push the project further and harder on every possible front. Make it the best documented one. Make it an exemplary Open Source project. Make it newcomer friendly. Add more tests. Make sure not a single project in the world can claim they ship better security advisories. Work really hard on making it the most secure network library there is. While at the same being welcoming and friendly to new contributors.
If there is
any
area that curl is not best-in-class, we should put in more work and improve curl in that area
. While at the same time keep up and polish it in all other aspects.
This is what drives me. This is what I want.
How
Getting top scores in every possible (imaginary and real) scorecard is accomplished through good old engineering. Do the job. Test. Iterate. Fail. Fix. Add tests. Do it again. Over and over.
A normal work day I sit down at my desk at about 8 in the morning and start. I iterate over issues, pull-requests and the everyday curl maintenance. I post silly messages on Mastodon and I chat with friends on IRC.
I try to end my regular work days at around 18:00, but I may go longer or shorter some days depending on what I feel like or if it’s “floorball day”. (I leave early on Wednesdays to go play with friends.)
As I live in Sweden and have many North-American colleagues and customers, I have occasional evening meetings to deal with the nine hour time difference to their west coast.
At some time between 22:00 and 23:00 I sit down in front of my computer again for the evening shift. I continue working on issues, fix bugs and review pull-requests. At 1

data.title: Role of metabolism in shaping enzyme structures over 400M years
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了代谢如何在过去4亿年中塑造了酶的结构演化。利用AlphaFold2等深度学习技术，研究团队分析了11,269个预测和实验确定的酶结构，这些酶参与了225个代谢途径中的361个反应。研究发现，酶的演化受到多种因素的制约，包括反应机制、金属离子及抑制剂的相互作用、代谢流量变化和生物合成成本。虽然正向选择的残基分布在各种结构元素中，但酶的表面残基演化最快，而小分子结合位点则在选择性约束下演化。研究整合了结构生物学和进化基因组学，提出了一个模型，表明酶的演化由催化功能内在支配，并受到代谢环境、网络结构、成本和分子相互作用的影响。

The role of metabolism in shaping enzyme structures over 400 million years
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Biochemistry
Molecular evolution
Structural biology
Systems biology
Abstract
Advances in deep learning and AlphaFold2 have enabled the large-scale prediction of protein structures across species, opening avenues for studying protein function and evolution
1
. Here we analyse 11,269 predicted and experimentally determined enzyme structures that catalyse 361 metabolic reactions across 225 pathways to investigate metabolic evolution over 400 million years in the Saccharomycotina subphylum
2
. By linking sequence divergence in structurally conserved regions to a variety of metabolic properties of the enzymes, we reveal that metabolism shapes structural evolution across multiple scales, from species-wide metabolic specialization to network organization and the molecular properties of the enzymes. Although positively selected residues are distributed across various structural elements, enzyme evolution is constrained by reaction mechanisms, interactions with metal ions and inhibitors, metabolic flux variability and biosynthetic cost. Our findings uncover hierarchical patterns of structural evolution, in which structural context dictates amino acid substitution rates, with surface residues evolving most rapidly and small-molecule-binding sites evolving under selective constraints without cost optimization. By integrating structural biology with evolutionary genomics, we establish a model in which enzyme evolution is intrinsically governed by catalytic function and shaped by metabolic niche, network architecture, cost and molecular interactions.

. Despite its critical role across disciplines, our understanding of the global biochemical constraints that shape enzyme function—and therefore its evolution—remains incomplete.
Comparing enzyme sequences across evolution has revealed various constraints that act at the amino acid level, such as the chemical identity of side chains and epistatic interactions
9
,
10
,
11
. Moreover, the sequence of enzymes is shaped by the costs of enzyme production
12
. Indeed, metabolic cost optimization is observed at the species and molecular levels. For example, under many conditions, cells prefer cost-effective fermentation over oxidative metabolism, despite the latter producing stoichiometrically higher ATP amounts
13
. Furthermore, especially high-abundance enzymes have evolved by incorporating less energetically costly amino acids

.
We hypothesized that the systematic accessibility of protein structures enabled by structural prediction
1
would allow us to integrate structural biology with evolutionary genomics and expand our understanding of the relationship between metabolism and protein evolution. We leveraged the extensive characterization of the Saccharomycotina subphylum, which represents 400 million years of evolution and includes
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
and
Candida albicans
2

, and examined 11,269 AlphaFold2-predicted and experimentally determined enzyme structures that belong to 424 orthologue groups (orthogroups) associated with 361 metabolic reactions in 224 metabolic pathways. Linking these structures with phenotypic data, enzyme properties and metabolic network reconstructions, we identified structural changes that are associated with metabolic constraints. We report how structural evolution depends on metabolic properties across species, pathways and molecular levels.
Mapping evolution in enzyme structures
We selected 26 out of 332 highly phylogenetically diverse yeast species of the Saccharomycotina subphylum

). Then, for enzymes present in the YeastPathways database, we initially assigned orthologues on the basis of sequence-based clusters
19
. From these sequences, we obtained 1,301 structures from AlphaFoldDB
21
and a further
n
= 9,968 structures that we predicted using AlphaFold v.2.0.1 at the start of our project (Supplementary Note
2
). Our final dataset consisted of 11,269 enzyme structures organized in 424 orthogroups.

data.title: Ask HN: How are you productively using Claude code?
data.author: nocobot
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Claude Code和类似AI代码生成工具的评价和使用体验

不同观点：
• whinvik认为Claude Code在绿地项目（greenfield）中的表现不如棕地项目（brownfield）。他指出，Claude生成的代码虽然能用，但往往过于复杂或不够优雅，需要手动调整。他建议在项目有一定基础后，Claude才能生成更合适的代码，类似于一个精力无限但经验不足的初级工程师。他还提到会并行使用Gemini，比较两者的解决方案，最终手动优化出最终方案。

• bGl2YW5j对Claude Code的表现感到失望，特别是在构建DSL（领域特定语言）时。尽管他使用了“计划、执行、评估”的方法，并进行了详细的提示，但生成的代码仍然存在问题，如小问题无法修复、代码过于简陋且难以调试。他决定减少对LLM（语言模型）的依赖，自行重写代码。

• perilunar有积极的使用体验，使用Cursor（结合ChatGPT）成功构建了两个简单的CRUD应用。尽管前端代码需要一些清理，但整体结果令他满意，并计划继续使用AI工具。

• johnecheck对Claude Code的使用体验较为中立，认为它能完成一些任务，但并未大幅提升生产力。他提到定期清除上下文并引用相关文件，但没有进行过多配置。

• JaggerJo认为Claude Code在执行不同任务时表现有限，主要适用于生成小代码片段，难以在更大范围内产生令人满意的结果。

• ktallett指出Claude Code的表现取决于所使用的技术和库。在使用常见库如JS和Python时表现良好，但在涉及更 obscure（ obscure通常指不常见的或冷门的）的技术时，准确性和知识有限。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Claude Code在绿地项目中的表现是否令人满意。whinvik和bGl2YW5j都提到在绿地项目中遇到的问题，而生成的代码需要大量手动调整。
• 不同用户对Claude Code的期望和使用场景各异，导致评价不一。perilunar在简单项目中获得了好结果，而bGl2YW5j在更复杂的项目中遇到了困难。
• 有用户提到并行使用多个AI工具（如whinvik使用Gemini）以比较和优化解决方案，这种方法在某些情况下可能更有效。

总结：
用户对Claude Code的评价存在分歧，主要取决于项目的复杂性和所使用的技术。在简单项目或常见技术中表现较好，而在复杂或不常见的技术中可能需要更多手动干预。不同用户根据自身需求和期望对工具的评价各异，建议根据具体项目需求选择和使用AI工具。

用户对Claude Code的评价存在分歧，主要取决于项目的复杂性和所使用的技术。在简单项目或常见技术中表现较好，而在复杂或不常见的技术中可能需要更多手动干预。不同用户根据自身需求和期望对工具的评价各异，建议根据具体项目需求选择和使用AI工具。

data.title: The Symbol Grounding Problem (1990)
data.author: Fibra
data.article_summary:
Stevan Harnad的《符号基础问题》一文讨论了纯粹符号模型在解释心灵时的局限性，提出了符号基础问题：如何使形式符号系统内的语义解释成为系统内在属性，而不是依赖外在解释？换句话说，如何让符号不仅仅是基于形状的操作，而是具有实际意义？文章类比了仅依靠中英字典学习中文的困境。

Harnad提出解决方案：符号表征必须通过非符号表征从底层向上构建，包括两类：(1) 图像表征，模拟近端感官投影；(2) 类别表征，识别物体和事件的不变特征。符号名称基于这些非符号表征，而高级符号表征则描述类别间关系。

连接主义被视为学习类别特征的机制，连接名称与其所代表的物体感官投影。这种混合模型结合了非符号和符号表征，而非独立的符号模块。符号操作受其在图像和类别不变特征中的形状影响，而不仅是符号的任意形状。

关键词：符号系统、连接主义、类别学习、认知模型、神经模型

Harnad, S. (1990) The Symbol Grounding Problem. Physica D 42: 335-346.
THE SYMBOL GROUNDING PROBLEM
Stevan Harnad
Department of Psychology
Princeton University
Princeton NJ 08544
harnad@cogsci.soton.ac.uk
ABSTRACT:
There has been much discussion
recently about the scope and
limits of purely symbolic models of the mind and about the proper role
of connectionism in cognitive modeling. This paper describes the
"symbol grounding problem": How can the semantic interpretation of a
formal symbol system be made
intrinsic to the system, rather than just parasitic on the meanings in
our heads? How can the meanings of the meaningless symbol tokens,
manipulated solely on the basis of their (arbitrary) shapes, be
grounded in anything but other meaningless symbols? The problem is
analogous to trying to learn Chinese from a Chinese/Chinese dictionary
alone. A candidate solution is sketched: Symbolic representations must
be grounded bottom-up in nonsymbolic representations of two kinds:  (1)
"iconic representations" , which are analogs of the proximal sensory
projections of distal objects and events, and (2)
"categorical representations" , which are learned and innate
feature-detectors that pick out the invariant features of object and
event categories from their sensory projections. Elementary symbols are
the names of these object and event categories, assigned on the basis
of their (nonsymbolic) categorical representations. Higher-order (3)
"symbolic representations" , grounded in these elementary symbols,
consist of symbol strings describing category membership relations
(e.g., "An X is a Y that is Z").
Connectionism is one natural candidate for the mechanism that learns
the invariant features underlying categorical representations, thereby
connecting names to the proximal projections of the distal objects they
stand for. In this way connectionism can be seen as a complementary
component in a hybrid nonsymbolic/symbolic model of the mind, rather
than a rival to purely symbolic modeling. Such a hybrid model would not
have an autonomous symbolic "module," however; the symbolic functions
would emerge as an intrinsically "dedicated" symbol system as a
consequence of the bottom-up grounding of categories' names in their
sensory representations. Symbol manipulation would be governed not just
by the arbitrary shapes of the symbol tokens, but by the nonarbitrary
shapes of the icons and category invariants in which they are grounded.
KEYWORDS:
symbol systems, connectionism, category learning, cognitive
models, neural models
1. Modeling the Mind
1.1 From Behaviorism to Cognitivism
For many years the only
empirical approach in psychology was behaviorism, its only explanatory
tools input/input and input/output associations (in the case of
classical conditioning; Turkkan 1989) and the reward/punishment history
that "shaped" behavior (in the case of operant conditioning; Catania &
Harnad 1988). In a reaction against the subjectivity of armchair
introspectionism, behaviorism had declared that it was just as illicit
to theorize about what went on in the
head of the organism to generate its behavior as to theorize about
what went on in its
mind. Only observables were to be the subject matter of psychology;
and, apparently, these were expected to explain themselves.
Psychology became more like an empirical science when, with the gradual
advent of cognitivism (Miller 1956, Neisser 1967, Haugeland 1978), it
became acceptable to make inferences about the
unobservable processes underlying behavior.
Unfortunately, cognitivism let mentalism in again
by the back door too, for the hypothetical internal processes came
embellished with subjective interpretations. In fact, semantic interpretability
(meaningfulness),
as we shall see, was one of the defining features of the most prominent
contender vying to become the theoretical vocabulary of cognitivism,
the "language of thought" (Fodor 1975), which became the prevailing
view in cognitive theory for several decades in the form of the
"symbolic" model of the mind: The mind is a symbol system and cognition
is symbol manipulation. The possibility of generating complex behavior
through symbol manipulation was empirically demonstrated by successes
in the field of artificial intelligence (AI).
1.2 Symbol Systems
What is a symbol system? From Newell (1980) Pylyshyn (1984), Fodor
(1987) and the classical work of Von Neumann, Turing, Goedel, Church,
etc. (see Kleene 1969) on the foundations of computation, we can
reconstruct the following definition:
A symbol system is:
a set of arbitrary
"physical tokens" scratches on paper, holes on a tape, events in a
digital computer, etc. that are
manipulated on the basis of "explicit rules" that are
likewise physical tokens and strings of tokens. The rule-governed
symbol-token manipulation is based
purely on the shape of the symbol tokens (not their "meaning"),
i.e., it is purely syntactic, and consists of

data.title: SCP-055 is an "antimeme" – it erases itself from memory when observed
data.author: rcpt
data.article_summary: SCP-055是一个“自我保守秘密”的异常物体，属于Keter级。其主要特性是关于它的外观、性质、行为和起源的信息会自动被遗忘。尽管人员可以观察、记录和描述SCP-055，但他们很快会忘记这些信息。SCP-055被保存在一个特殊的混凝土房间内，房间周围有法拉第笼。尽管其收容室容易进入，但所有人员都声称不知道它的存在。关于SCP-055的许多科学数据已被记录，但无法被研究。有假设认为，SCP-055可能是由未知第三方植入，用于秘密观察或干扰Site 19或其他SCP地点的活动，甚至是全球人类活动。尽管其潜在威胁巨大，但没有可行的应对措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对作品《There is no antimemetics division》的评价及其引发的联想和比较

不同观点：
• nicbou认为《There is no antimemetics division》这本书讲述了一个关于SCP反模因团队战斗的故事，非常有趣且引人深思，强烈推荐。
• Cheyana在阅读评论后联想到《Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy》系列中的"Somebody Else's Problem"概念，通过分享链接将该书主题与另一作品进行类比。
• tuatoru引用书中的内容，指出书中描述的事实被偶尔发现后引起短暂关注，随后被遗忘，并将其与现实中的社会活动作比较，暗示对某些社会议题的关注往往短暂而不持久。

补充讨论：
• tuatoru的评论引发了对书中情节与现实世界现象的联系，特别是一些社会问题的短暂关注现象，这与nicbou的积极推荐形成对比，暗示了不同读者可能从不同角度解读和联系作品内容。

Item #:
SCP-055
Object Class:
Keter
Special Containment Procedures:
Object is kept within a five (5) by five (5) by two point five (2.5) meter square room constructed of cement (fifty (50) centimeter thickness), with a Faraday cage surrounding the cement walls. Access is via a heavy containment door measuring two (2) by two point five (2.5) meters constructed on bearings to ensure door closes and locks automatically unless held open deliberately. Security guards are NOT to be posted outside SCP-055's room. It is further advised that all personnel maintaining or studying other SCP objects in the vicinity try to maintain a distance of at least fifty (50) meters from the geometric center of the room, as long as this is reasonably practical.
Description:
SCP-055 is a "self-keeping secret" or "anti-meme". Information about SCP-055's physical appearance as well as its nature, behavior, and origins is self-classifying. To clarify:
How Site 19 originally acquired SCP-055 is unknown.
When SCP-055 was obtained, and by whom, is unknown.
SCP-055's physical appearance is unknown. It is not indescribable, or invisible: individuals are perfectly capable of entering SCP-055's container and observing it, taking mental or written notes, making sketches, taking photographs, and even making audio/video recordings. An extensive log of such observations is on file. However, information about SCP-055's physical appearance "leaks" out of a human mind soon after such an observation. Individuals tasked with describing SCP-055 afterwards find their minds wandering and lose interest in the task; individuals tasked with sketching a copy of a photograph of SCP-055 are unable to remember what the photograph looks like, as are researchers overseeing these tests. Security personnel who have observed SCP-055 via closed-circuit television cameras emerge after a full shift exhausted and effectively amnesiac about the events of the previous hours.
Who authorized the construction of SCP-055's containment room, why it was constructed in this way, or what the purpose of the described Containment Procedures may be, are all unknown.
Despite SCP-055's container being easily accessible, all personnel at Site 19 claim no knowledge of SCP-055's existence when challenged.
All of these facts are periodically rediscovered, usually by chance readers of this file, causing a great deal of alarm. This state of concern lasts minutes at most, before the matter is simply forgotten about.
A great deal of scientific data has been recorded from SCP-055, but cannot be studied.
At least one attempt has been made to destroy SCP-055, or possibly move it from containment at Site 19 to another site, meeting failure for reasons unknown.
SCP-055 may present a major physical threat and indeed may have killed many hundreds of personnel, and we would not know it. Certainly it presents a gigantic memetic/mental threat, hence its Keter classification.
Document #055-1:
An Analysis of SCP-055
The author puts forward the hypothesis that SCP-055 was never formally acquired by ████████████ ████████ and is in fact an autonomous or remotely-controlled agent, inserted at Site 19 by an unidentified third party for one or all of the following purposes:
to silently observe, or interfere with, activities at Site 19
to silently observe, or interfere with, activities at other SCP locations
to silently observe, or interfere with, activities of humanity worldwide
to silently observe, or interfere with, other SCP objects
to silently observe, or interfere with, ████████████
No action to counter any of these potential threats is suggested, or indeed theoretically possible.

data.title: A software conference that advocates for quality
data.author: leoncaet
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了2023年7月12至14日在瑞典举办的一场活动，活动通过Twitch直播。三天日程包括多位演讲者的技术分享，涵盖编程历史、物理引擎并行化、调试器可视化架构、游戏开发中的车辆编程、音频对齐、可伸缩字形渲染、深度学习与计算机视觉等主题。物理出席为邀请制，不公开发售门票。活动将直播并录制，免费公开。地点在一个迷人的小镇。组织者为Sam、Sander和Charlie。更多信息可通过订阅新闻通讯或在Twitter上提问获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对软件质量会议及相关议题的看法与争议

不同观点：
• **对会议承诺的怀疑**：burnt-resistor对会议和书籍所承诺的“这次会有所不同”表示怀疑，认为这些只是卖点，而实际过程和工具并没有显著变化。他们质疑AI在编码中的作用，认为依赖AI可能导致经验不足的人重复犯错。

• **有效的质量控制经验**：supportengineer分享了自己30年职业生涯中唯一见到有效质量控制的公司的经验。该公司通过分离质量工程师和开发工程师的组织结构，不同的激励机制，严格的文档和发布节奏，以及质量工程师的绝对权威来实现质量控制。

• **会议与特定群体的关联**：kragen认为该会议与Handmade Hero和Jon Blow的Jai群体有关，关注点更偏向用户体验和效率，而非正确性。

• **网站质量与会议宗旨的矛盾**：imwally和jofzar指出，一个倡导高质量软件的会议应该有一个更好的网站。jofzar特别提到网站在移动设备上的用户体验问题，以及缺乏对演讲者社交链接的介绍。

• **对演讲标题和组织者透明度的批评**：alabhyajindal和kilpikaarna对某些演讲标题表示不满，认为其形式具有侮辱性。kilpikaarna还对会议的组织方式和匿名组织者表示质疑，认为其可能在刻意保持某种排他性。

• **对AI工具与质量平衡的关注**：reactordev对如何平衡快速业务需求与AI工具带来的质量问题表示关注，并分享了个人经验。

• **对会议实质内容的信息不足**：rkagerer指出很难找到关于会议实质的信息，仅从Twitch标签中了解到“软件质量正在变差，我们来改善”。

• **对网站设计元素的关注**：wavemode注意到网站使用的编程语言可能是Odin，而grob则对网站使用的字体Berkeley Mono表示赞赏。

• **对知名演讲者的期待**：ravenstine希望Jonathan Blow能成为演讲者。

• **对 dysfunctional code 框架的讽刺**：mediumsmart讽刺地建议创建一个 dysfunctional code 框架以加快项目进度。

• **对HR和企业实践的重视**：ChrisMarshallNY认为，除非会议倡导有利于留住人才的HR实践和激励质量的企业实践，否则很难带来实质性改变。他提到Watts Humphrey等人的经典质量实践书籍，并指出不良的管理和短视的高层是质量问题的根本原因。

补充讨论：
• **对具体演讲内容的正面反馈**：elcapitan对Casey Muratori的演讲表示赞赏，认为其对OOP历史方面的见解很有启发性。

争议焦点：
• 会议和网站的实际质量与所宣扬的质量宗旨之间的矛盾。
• AI工具在编码中的应用及其对软件质量的影响。
• 会议的组织方式及其可能的排他性。

We reached $1M ARR with zero funding
Kyle Nolan
7 min read
Published Jun 30, 2025
Jun 30, 2025
Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business in four years.
We really did it! We bootstrapped ProjectionLab to $1,000,000 in annual recurring revenue.
And I’m still processing that this is real. 🥹
Back in 2021, I was inspired by the financial independence movement and wanted a better way to plan my own life. I couldn’t find the right tool, so I started building.
I had no idea that side project would one day help over 100,000 households plan for their financial future too.
How we got here
If this is your first time hearing about ProjectionLab, here’s a quick recap:
Milestone
Date
What Was Happening
$150 MRR
May 2021
First internet dollar! (from a
post to HN
)

Aug 2021

blog post
$1K MRR
Dec 2021
Working nights & weekends after corporate job
$4K MRR
Sep 2022
Shoutout from Mr Money Mustache
$5k MRR
Nov 2022
Whoah, public speaking?!
$8.3K MRR
Apr 2023
Started to believe I could do this
$10K MRR
Jun 2023
The final boss of indie hacking
$16.6K MRR
Sep 2023
Dropped to part-time at my day job
$23.3K MRR
Nov 2023
Quit my day job and went all-in!
$41.6K MRR
Jul 2024
Started growing the team
$45.8K MRR
Aug 2024
Shared story on ChooseFI
$83.3k MRR
Jun 2025
👋 Here we are!
When you look beyond the recurring revenue chart, this journey had ups, downs, and moments I wanted to quit.
The emotions behind the numbers
Want to know what building in public from zero to a million dollars a year really felt like? NOT like serenely progressing up-and-to-the-right…
More like riding a dopamine rollercoaster while getting attacked by a bear.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
The flat months in the early years? The dips in earnings? The times I woke up to a dozen canceled subscriptions?
Each one had me questioning everything, wondering if I should just focus on the corporate ladder, or maybe try to get into big tech instead.
The financial independence movement is what set me on this path. So on top of worrying about normal business risks, I was primed to think in terms of my time and opportunity cost, and how failure would hurt my own timeline to FI.
But gradually, I learned that emotional peaks and valleys are always a part of entrepreneurship. And that “not giving up” is actually a superpower.
Not giving up
There are loads of people out there smarter than me.
But luckily, success indexes less on IQ and more on consistency. The willingness to doggedly show up every single day can take you to some really suprising and amazing places.
And you know what makes it easier and more rewarding to be that persistent?
Working alongside people you like.
From solo dev to real team
For the first two years, I burned the candle at both ends working solo. 4-6 hours every night after work, entire weekends, holidays, you name it.
404 Day Off Not Found.
That was the only way I could build something this complex in a crowded market as a risk-averse engineer with a day job. And I was fortunate enough to attempt this at a stage in life when I had lots of energy and few family responsibilities.
Plus my trusty sidekick, BB the bird:
But long-term, I knew there would be a choice to face:
Keep doing everything myself and watch growth plateau, or…
Find someone with a complementary skillset and start building a team.
I was just an ordinary engineer with zero marketing experience. So I figured I should try to team up with someone good at growth & marketing.
Finding a growth & marketing partner
During the first few years, I was approached by dozens of potential “partners.” Several wanted an outsize equity stake to essentially just make suggestions. Others had the wrong skillset or didn’t feel like a complete fit.
But
Jon Kuipers
jumped right into the trenches and worked to prove himself before asking for anything. He spent a year contributing real value, and when the time came to bring on a growth partner full-time, I didn’t look anywhere else.
Now I stay focused on building, while he handles growth, marketing, partnerships, and some ops stuff.
Building a team
We’ve also added a few contractors to the team.
And these guys are legends. 💪
They come straight from the ProjectionLab user community, and they are doing a great job fielding the arcane finance questions our customers love to ask. Plus hosting 1-on-1 sessions, creating
tutorial videos
, and more.
Could we have offshored customer success for pennies on the dollar instead? You bet. But having a happy and engaged user community of product evangelists means a lot to us, and I want them all to have the best experience possible.
For multiple years, I was up at all hours answering support questions myself. It interrupted my dev work (and my sleep) constantly. I love the PL community – it’s a big part of what motivated me to keep going back then.
And it blows my mind that the empty discord

data.title: C3 solved memory lifetimes with scopes
data.author: lerno
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了C3语言通过引入Temp分配器和作用域机制解决内存生命周期管理的问题。传统方法如RAII、引用计数和垃圾回收各有优缺点，而C3的Temp分配器结合了这些方法的优点，提供了一种自动且高效的内存管理方案。Temp分配器基于内存分配区域（arenas）的概念，在执行离开其作用域时自动重置，避免了内存泄漏。文章通过代码示例展示了如何使用`@pool()`定义内存可用范围，并通过工具Valgrind验证内存管理的有效性。此外，C3还允许对嵌套作用域的内存清理进行显式控制，提高了灵活性。这种方法兼顾了性能和易用性，无需复杂的RAII或垃圾回收机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C3语言中的@pool机制与Rust的借用检查器（borrow checker）以及内存管理机制的比较，及其在不同场景下的适用性与有效性。

不同观点：
• **关于编译时间与借用检查器的关系**：
   - ameliaquining认为，Rust的编译时间慢并非主要由于借用检查器，而是由于其他语言特性（如单态化、LLVM优化、过程宏等）。借用检查器本身运行时间是线性的，且只占编译时间的一小部分。
   - 争议焦点：Rust编译速度慢的根本原因是否与借用检查器直接相关。

• **借用检查器的核心优势**：
   - UncleMeat指出，借用检查器的主要作用是确保不会在对象销毁后访问内存，以及确保不会在需要常量的情况下修改某些内容，而不仅仅是防止内存泄漏。
   - 对比：借用检查器在处理对象生命周期和多对象关系中的重要性，而@pool机制似乎没有解决这些问题。

• **@pool机制是否涉及借用检查**：
   - hvenev认为@pool主要关注内存管理而非内存安全，质疑其与借用检查的关联。他指出，C3中的@pool类似于C语言中的手动内存管理，可能无法防止悬挂指针问题。
   - 争议焦点：@pool机制是否能与借用检查器相提并论，尤其是在内存安全方面。

• **@pool与其他语言机制的比较**：

The
C3
Blog
Forget Borrow Checkers: C3 Solved Memory Lifetimes With Scopes
2025-07-11
Modern languages offer a variety of techniques to help with dynamic memory management, each one a different tradeoff in terms of performance, control and complexity. In this post we’ll look at an old idea, memory allocation regions or arenas, implemented via the C3 Temp allocator, which is the new default for C3.
The Temp allocator combines the ease of use of garbage collection with C3’s unique features to give a simple and (semi)-automated solution within a manual memory management language. The Temp allocator helps you avoid memory leaks, improve performance, and simplify code compared to traditional approaches.
Memory allocations come in two broad types
stack
allocations which are compact, efficient and automatic and heap allocations which are much larger and have
customisable organisation
. Custom organisation allows both innovation and footguns in equal measure, let’s explore those.
Memory Leaks
When we dynamically allocate memory, with say
malloc()
typically we need to
free()
it afterwards, otherwise we can’t use that memory until the OS process exits. If that memory isn’t being used and it has not been freed this is called a
memory leak
and can lead to restricting or running out of available system memory.
Avoiding Memory Leaks
Common solutions are
RAII
,
reference counting
or
garbage collection
which automatically free those variables.
Each method has different tradeoffs.
RAII
needs classes or structs to manage their own memory cleanup with a lot of extra code.
Reference counting
counts how many users each memory allocation has, when this hits zero the memory is freed. Reference counting is expensive with multiple CPU cores as we need to synchronise these counts and share information between cores.
Garbage collection
competes with the program for both memory and CPU time, reducing program performance and increasing memory usage.
Memory Allocation Regions
Memory allocation regions, go by various names: arenas, pools, contexts; The idea dates back to the 1960’s with the IBM OS/360 mainframes having a similar system. Memory regions are efficient for managing many memory allocations and can be freed in a single operation, and are particularly effective when we know the memory will not be needed later. That is, we know the memory’s lifetime. This idea is powerful and used in many applications like web server request handlers or database transactions, as used by the
Apache webserver
and the
Postgres database
.
Memory allocation regions use a single buffer so have good locality because all the allocations are closely associated together, making it more efficient for CPU access, compared to traditional
malloc
where allocations are spread throughout the heap.
Memory allocation regions may make it easier to manage memory, however you still need to
remember
to free them, and if you forget to do call free, then that memory will still leak.
Enter The Temp Allocator
The Temp allocator in C3 is a region based allocator which is
automatically
reset once execution leaves its scope, so you cannot forget to free the memory and can’t leak memory. The Temp allocator in C3 is a builtin in the standard library, called
@pool()
and using it you can define the scope where the allocated variables are available, for example:
fn
int
example
(
int
input
)
{
@
pool()
{
// Allocate temp_variable on the heap with Temp allocator
int
*
temp_variable
=
mem::tnew(
int
)
;
*
temp_variable
=
56
;
input
=
input
+
temp_variable;
return
input;
};
// Automatically cleanup temp_variable
}
fn
void
main
()
{
int
result
=
example(
1
)
;
assert(result
==
57
,
"
The result should be 57
"
)
;
}
Check With Valgrind
Valgrind is a tool which detects memory leaks and we can use it to show the temp allocator managed the memory for us automatically.
Terminal window
valgrind
./pool_example
|
&
grep
"
All heap blocks were freed
"
==129129==
All
heap
blocks
were
freed
--
no
leaks
are
possible
Success!
We have relatively performant memory allocations managed automatically without needing
RAII
,
garbage collection
or
reference counting
.
Controlling Variable Cleanup
Normally temp allocated variables are cleaned up at the end of the closest
@pool
scope, but what if you have nested
@pool
and want explicit control over when it’s cleaned up? Simple: assign the temp allocator with the scope you need to a variable, and use it explicitly. The temp allocator in a scope is a global variable called
tmem
.
fn String
*
example
(
int
input
)
{
// previous global temp allocator from main() scope
Allocator temp_allocator
=
tmem;
@
pool()
{
// Allocate on the global temp allocator
String
*
returned
=
allocator::new(temp_allocator, String)
;
*
returned
=
string::format(temp_allocator,
"
modified
%s
"
, input)
;
return
returned;
};
}
fn
void
main
()
{
// top-most temp allocator, tmem created here
@
pool()
{
String
*
returned
=
example(
42
)
;
// "modified 42" string returned
io::printn(
*
ret

data.article_summary: TorchLeet是一个用于提升PyTorch和深度学习技能的项目，包含两类问题集：普通问题集和大型语言模型（LLM）问题集。普通问题集涵盖从基础到高级的PyTorch实践问题，如线性回归、卷积神经网络（CNN）、循环神经网络（RNN）、自定义损失函数等。LLM问题集专注于从零实现大型语言模型，包括注意力机制、嵌入、多头注意力等。该项目旨在通过动手实践深入理解PyTorch概念，提供不完整的代码块和解决方案以帮助学习。问题难度从基础到高级，适合不同水平的学习者。

data.title: Lua beats MicroPython for embedded devs
data.author: willhschmid
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lua与MicroPython在嵌入式开发中的优劣比较

不同观点：
• Lua作为嵌入式开发策略优于MicroPython：一些评论者（如[1vuio0pswjnm7]和[delduca]）引用多个来源和个人经验，认为Lua在速度和嵌入性上优于MicroPython。他们提到Lua更小、更快，并且Toit语言声称比MicroPython快30倍。此外，Lua的嵌入式开发策略被认为更容易集成和使用。
• MicroPython的扩展性和易用性：[jononor]认为文章对MicroPython的批评不准确，指出MicroPython可以通过C轻松扩展，并且可以使用如ulab之类的库来实现类似Python的功能。此外，文章中提到的一些限制（如无法使用numpy）被认为是不准确的。
• MicroPython和Lua的应用场景不同：[10000truths]指出MicroPython和Lua解决的是不同的问题。MicroPython旨在取代传统的C运行时，适用于嵌入式平台，而Lua则更适合作为嵌入式应用中的脚本语言。
• Lua和MicroPython的实用性争议：[KaiserPro]认为Lua和MicroPython都有其局限性，Lua需要自行支持工具链，而MicroPython虽然适合网络应用，但在精确控制和安全性上不如C/C++。
• 对"严肃开发者"使用脚本语言的质疑：[ycombinatrix]和[Palomides]质疑是否真的有"严肃的"嵌入式开发者使用MicroPython或Lua，暗示编译语言可能是更常见的选择。

补充讨论：
• 其他嵌入式脚本语言的推荐：[theoutfield]提到AngelScript作为一种被低估的嵌入式脚本语言，容易扩展且是C/C++的子集。[analog31]询问如何在Arduino开发环境中尝试Lua，而[jokoon]则表达了对Lua语法的不满，更偏好gdscript。
• 开发体验和类型提示：[smohare]提到对Lua的动态特性和缺乏类型提示感到困惑，认为这与Python类似，对专业代码审查来说是个认知障碍。

争议焦点：
• Lua与MicroPython在嵌入式开发中的实际性能和应用场景优劣是主要的争议点。一方认为Lua更小更快，适合嵌入式开发，另一方则认为MicroPython的扩展性和易用性使其在某些场景下更具优势。
• 对"严肃开发者"是否使用这些脚本语言的质疑，反映了在嵌入式开发领域中对脚本语言实用性的不同看法。

总结：评论主要围绕Lua和MicroPython在嵌入式开发中的性能、应用场景和实用性展开讨论，并涉及其他脚本语言的推荐和开发体验的分享。争议点主要集中在两者的实际应用效果和开发者对其的接受程度。

data.title: The North Korean fake IT worker problem is ubiquitous
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了北韩假冒IT求职者对企业的威胁，以及如何识别和阻止这些骗局。多家美国和欧洲公司发现，许多看似优秀的求职者实际上使用虚假身份，目的是窃取公司源代码和敏感数据，甚至进行勒索。这些假求职者的特征包括简历丰富但LinkedIn连接少、拒绝面对面面试、使用深伪视频等。企业高管指出，这些骗子可能已经渗透到许多大公司中，利用远程工作机会进行诈骗。为应对这一问题，企业需加强身份验证，警惕可疑求职者，并通过技术手段如ChatGPT比对面试回答的一致性来识别潜在骗局。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕虚假IT工作者（特别是来自朝鲜的）通过伪造LinkedIn档案获得工作的讨论，涉及身份验证、背景调查和可能的解决方案。

不同观点：
• **虚假LinkedIn档案和黑客攻击的真实案例**：croemer分享了其同事LinkedIn账号被黑，档案被篡改为朝鲜背景的实例，强调了虚假档案问题的严重性，并指出检测这种变化的困难。
  
• **美国与欧洲雇主的背景调查差异**：mkl95指出，美国公司通常会进行严格的背景调查，但欧洲公司则未必，这使得虚假工作者更容易渗透进欧洲企业。

• **技术手段在虚假工作者问题中的应用**：Maxious提到FBI对微型KVM设备（虚假工作者使用的一种工具）的关注，而 CyberMacGyver 则提到自己正在开发免费服务来解决这一问题，并声称自2018年以来已经标记了数千个虚假申请者。

• **强制性面对面入职作为解决方案**：Havoc建议通过强制第一周入职时进行面对面的方式来解决虚假身份问题，ta1243对此表示支持，认为通过团队互动可以很快发现不一致。

• **政治与外国情报渗透的深层次威胁**：jongjong提出，某些国家的科技行业可能正在被外国情报机构渗透，尤其是那些拥有大量外籍工程师的国家，如澳大利亚。jongjong进一步推测，某些国家可能通过在关键公司安插人员来获取政治利益。

• **失业开发者与虚假工作者问题**：giantg2指出，目前有许多失业的开发者，虚假工作者问题使得合法求职者更难找到工作，并建议像Pearson这样的公司设立验证面试中心来解决这一问题。

• **对虚假工作者问题夸大的质疑**：abxyz认为，所谓的朝鲜虚假工作者问题可能被夸大，并指出某些公司（如Socure）可能通过夸大问题来推销自己的解决方案。abxyz进一步指出，许多被标记为“朝鲜”的申请者实际上可能只是来自贫困国家的人试图获得工作。

• **政府提供在线身份验证服务的可能性**：dakiol建议政府提供简单的在线身份验证服务，以解决虚假身份问题，而Barrin92则质疑虚假工作者是否真的仅通过伪造LinkedIn档案就能通过所有法律和财务审核。

• **对公开讨论和解决方案的反思**：alganet认为，这种公开讨论可能反而助长了不必要的恐慌，并指出这种问题应该直接告知相关公司或通过私下调查解决。alganet还提到，需要采取措施减少虚假工作者可利用的工具，但这些措施可能会对某些技术发展造成影响。

补充讨论：
- **幽默与讽刺**：belter以讽刺的口吻指出，正当本地开发者难以找到工作时，虚假朝鲜IT工作者却轻松获得职位，暗示对现状的无奈。
- **利用政治敏感问题进行身份验证**：conradev提到，可以通过要求申请者批评朝鲜领导人来鉴别其真实性，这是一种非正式但可能有效的方法。

争议焦点：虚假工作者问题的严重性及其背后的政治动机。jongjong和abxyz的观点形成了鲜明对比，前者认为这是一个深层次的政治渗透问题，而后者认为这是被夸大的经济问题。

Cyber-crime
10
You have a fake North Korean IT worker problem - here's how to stop it
10
Thick resumes with thin LinkedIn connections are one sign. Refusing an in-person interview is another
Jessica Lyons
Sun 13 Jul 2025
//
11:02 UTC
By now, the North Korean fake IT worker problem is so ubiquitous that if you think you don't have any phony resumes or imposters in your interview queue, you're asleep at the wheel.
"Almost every CISO of a Fortune 500 company that I've spoken to — I'll just characterize as dozens that I've spoken to — have admitted that they had a North Korean IT worker problem,"
said
Mandiant Consulting CTO Charles Carmakal during a threat-intel roundtable, admitting that even Mandiant's parent company Google is not immune.
"We have seen this in our own pipelines," added Iain Mulholland, Google Cloud's senior director of security engineering.
"We've certainly seen applicants that fit into this category with various IOCs [indicators of compromise] that we've shared with partners and peers," Snowflake CISO Brad Jones told
The Register
.
These types of scams, largely originating from North Korea, or at least funneling money back to Pyongyang, have cost American businesses at least
$88 million over six years
, the Department of Justice said last year.
In some cases, the fraudsters use their insider access to steal proprietary source code and other sensitive data, and then extort their employers with threats to leak corporate data if not
paid a ransom demand
.
As US-based companies become more aware of the fake IT worker problem, the job seekers are increasingly
targeting European employers
, too.
Nearly all executives who spoke to
The Register
in recent months have seen a flood of these types of applicants applying for open positions, most of them in engineering and software development, and all of them remote work.
In some instances, the scammers even used deepfake videos in attempts to get hired, including at a security company that uses AI to find vulnerabilities in code. "If they almost fooled me, a cybersecurity expert, they definitely fooled some people," Vidoc Security Lab co-founder Dawid Moczadło told us in an
earlier interview
.
"We believe, at this point, every Fortune 100 and potentially Fortune 500 have a pretty high number of risky employees on their books," Socure Chief Growth Officer Rivka Little told us.
Using a fake identity…to apply for an identity job
Over the past few months, Socure has seen a ton of fake candidates applying for open jobs, according to Little, who has been leading the charge on the IT worker scam front. This seems an especially ironic choice for employment scammers, because Socure provides identity verification services to other companies.
For a senior engineering role, Socure used to receive between 150 and 200 applications over three or four months. That number has recently jumped to more than 1,999 purported job seekers in a two-month period. At least some of those extra applicants have weirdly suspicious profiles.
"We were in our executive meeting one Monday morning, and our chief people officer said, 'We're getting these super-strange resumes. They don't seem to be connected to people who are valid. This feels like a fake identity,'" Little said. "There were just too many disconnects."
Chief among these disconnects were "shallow" LinkedIn profiles paired with "beefy resumes," she explained, citing job-seeker claims of working at Meta, attending Ivy League schools, developing major tech companies' flagship products … but then only having 25 LinkedIn connections.
Once the recruitment team began meeting via video conferences with some of the applicants, they noted extremely Western-sounding names, like James Anderson, paired with East Asian appearances and accented English, in much higher numbers than they expected.
He was affable, a nice guy. He was making jokes. There was nothing about him that would make me not want to work with him
"You can't profile people, so with the first few we were like, that's interesting. But then when it was 10, 20, 30 — this is implausible at that rate and number, demographically," Little said. "We decided to follow through on a couple of candidates to really suss out what is going on here, and also to allow us to capture consent, because you can't really dig into someone's identity background unless you have consent to do so."
In all of these cases, Little's team noted a number of oddities: new-ish email addresses, phone numbers that didn't match claimed geographic locations, routing everything through a VPN, and educational backgrounds that didn't check out.
Little said she fed a handful of job applicant questions into ChatGPT and saved the chatbot's responses for reference during the interview.
"If his answers are anywhere close to these, then we'll also know there's a problem, and that's exactly what happened," she said. "It was insane."

• **对公开讨论和解决方案的反思**：alganet认为，这种公开讨论可能反而助长了不必要的恐慌，并指出这种问题应该直接告知相关公司或通过私下调查解决。alganet还提到，需要采取措施减少虚假工作者可利用的工具，但这些措施可能会对某些技术发展造成影响。

补充讨论：
- **幽默与讽刺**：belter以讽刺的口吻指出，正当本地开发者难以找到工作时，虚假朝鲜IT工作者却轻松获得职位，暗示对现状的无奈。
- **利用政治敏感问题进行身份验证**：conradev提到，可以通过要求申请者批评朝鲜领导人来鉴别其真实性，这是一种非正式但可能有效的方法。

争议焦点：虚假工作者问题的严重性及其背后的政治动机。jongjong和abxyz的观点形成了鲜明对比，前者认为这是一个深层次的政治渗透问题，而后者认为这是被夸大的经济问题。

data.title: Monitoring My Homelab, Simply
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种简化的家庭实验室监控方案，作者开发了一个小型程序来进行HTTP、DNS、TLS等检测，并通过https://ntfy.sh发送通知。该方案旨在满足以下需求：出现严重故障时通知、持续故障时重复提醒、修复后通知以及易于添加检测器。程序通过一个循环运行检测器，失败时发送通知，并每小时提醒一次。作者提供了TLS检测器的示例代码，并说明了如何处理故障和恢复通知。程序设计简单，避免复杂的状态管理，且易于部署和维护。作者的目标是捕捉明显的系统问题，而非解决所有潜在故障或提供详尽的历史数据分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：监控和告警解决方案的选择，特别是在家庭实验室（homelab）环境下的应用。

不同观点：
• Jedd认为，家庭实验室中日志聚合是一个相对容易解决的问题，并且有一个安全的日志收集端点可能有多种好处。他通过实例说明了跟踪FLUSH CACHE EXT错误的重要性，以及在不同层级上进行错误关联的价值。
• reboot81推荐使用healthchecks.io，并提供了在不同操作系统上设置的脚本链接。
• compumike自荐了他们团队开发的监控和告警解决方案https://heiioncall.com/，并强调了其在简单监控、告警和值班轮换上的功能，特别是其灵活的静音功能。
• danesparza推荐使用Uptime Kuma，认为其更为简单且免费，特别是结合电子邮件通知功能。
• Evidlo建议使用http状态检查和类似updown.io的服务，强调其低成本优势。
• Scaevolus使用Prometheus + Prometheus Alertmanager，并结合免费的分页系统，认为这种组合在添加告警时能最小化时间成本，并且用户体验优秀。
• justusthane正在寻找一个超简单但超可扩展的监控解决方案，并计划编写一个Python程序来实现，所有监控通过插件实现。
• Havoc认为Uptime Kuma最简单，因为其具有Python API包，可以批量加载内容，编辑起来更方便。
• Tractor8626强调在家庭实验室中监控诸如RAID健康状态、磁盘空间、备份作业运行情况和SSL证书到期等内容的重要性。
• Spooky23使用node exporter到Prometheus和Grafana，结合Uptime Kuma和pushover发送告警，认为这种组合设置简单且有效。
• JZL003使用Node Express服务器设置监控，结合免费的监控服务进行告警，认为这种方法易于扩展。
• frenchtoast8在工作中使用Datadog，但认为其对于家庭实验室过于昂贵，推荐使用NewRelic和Grafana Cloud的免费计划，但指出需要付出学习成本。
• bonobocop推荐Cloudprober，认为其易于配置和扩展，并且容易集成告警功能。
• loloquwowndueo认为Prometheus + Alertmanager的组合已经非常简单且稳定，并使用pushover进行手机通知，认为这是一种经济有效的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于工具的简单性、成本和功能性。比如，Jedd强调了日志聚合的潜在好处，而danespa和Evidlo则强调了Uptime Kuma和updown.io的低成本和简单性。
• 多个评论提到了Uptime Kuma的简单易用和免费特性，但也有用户如Scaevolus和JZL003推荐了Prometheus和自定义脚本组合的灵活性和功能性。
• 成本是一个重要的讨论点，特别是对于家庭实验室用户而言，像Datadog这样的商业解决方案被认为过于昂贵，而免费或低成本的解决方案如Uptime Kuma、NewRelic和Grafana Cloud更受欢迎。
• 自动化的静音功能被compumike和heiioncall.com强调为一个重要特性，解决了手动管理静音状态的不便。
• 不同用户对工具的易用性有不同看法，例如Havoc认为Uptime Kuma的Python API使得批量加载和编辑更为方便，而Spooky23则强调了使用node exporter和Prometheus组合的简便性。

data.title: MacPaint Art from the Mid-80s Still Looks Great Today
data.author: decryption
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了浏览BMUG的CD-ROM和Discmaster上18,000多张MacPaint图像的体验，这些图像来自80年代中期，尽管技术简陋，但艺术作品至今仍具吸引力。作者计划寻找这些早期艺术家，了解他们如今的成就。同时提到同时代的Amiga电脑也能创作类似甚至更出色的艺术作品，并邀请读者自行在Discmaster上探索更多图像。作者还推荐了一本名为《Zen & The Art of The Macintosh》的书，介绍当时的创作技巧，鼓励读者尝试制作类似艺术作品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：早期数字艺术及其与技术限制的关系

不同观点：
• **seabombs** 提到“审美完整性”（aesthetic completeness）的概念，认为某些游戏艺术在技术限制下已经达到了完全的艺术表达，使用现代工具重新制作会改变原作的本质，工具和媒介本身是艺术的一部分。
• **WoodenChair** 提供了将现代照片转换为MacPaint图画的工具链接，并介绍了一本讲解如何用Python编写相似程序的书，强调技术上的可操作性。
• **gxd** 指出早期计算机如Amiga的限制催生了独特的艺术风格，并提供了一个关于Deluxe Paint的链接。
• **hcarvalhoalves** 认为这些图画的优秀之处在于艺术家对传统绘画技巧的掌握，而非仅仅是数字媒介的先进性，强调艺术家的技能对作品的影响。

补充讨论：
• **aresant** 提到一位仍在创作MacPaint像素艺术的艺术家Pinot，提供了一个链接以展示其作品。
• **poisonborz** 表达了对过去计算机产品和公司真诚热情的怀念，隐含对现代商业环境的批评。
• **HPsquared** 将早期像素艺术与洞穴壁画相比较，认为即使技术简单，优秀的艺术仍然具有持久吸引力。
• **rswail** 引用Charles Eames的名言“设计在于限制”，认为Mac和MacPaint的限制催生了特定时期的艺术形式。
• **decryption** 提到帖子的受欢迎程度，并添加了更多一比特像素艺术图片。
• **taylorius** 认为非照片级真实的图像能让观众用想象力填补空白，促进一种特殊的互动方式。
• **kjellsbells** 指出某街景图的创作者是MacGrid的发明者Gerald Vaughn Clement，并提到一个讨论此类艺术的论坛。
• **cjcenizal** 分享了自己在80年代成长的经历，认为像素艺术唤起了怀旧情感。
• **reconnecting** 提到一个专门为旧计算机用户设计的网站，并询问Netscape 4的缺点。
• **Mizza** 认为某图画是对'View of the World from 9th Avenue'的模仿，并提供了一个维基百科链接以供参考。
• **sircastor** 分享了自己在技术过渡时期丢失艺术作品的经历，建议大家尽力保存自己的创作。

争议焦点：
- 艺术作品的优秀是否主要归因于艺术家的传统绘画技能（hcarvalhoalves），还是工具和媒介本身的重要性（seabombs）。
- 现代工具重新制作早期数字艺术是否会改变其本质（seabombs）。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
- 早期计算机技术限制对艺术风格的影响（gxd）。
- 如何保存和转换早期数字艺术作品的技术方法（WoodenChair, reconnecting）。
- 怀旧情感与像素艺术的关系（cjcenizal）。
- 艺术作品丢失的个人经历和保存建议（sircastor）。

44540402.article_content:
MacPaint Art From The Mid-80s Still Looks Great Today
July 12, 2025
I really enjoyed browsing the
BMUG's CD-ROM and discovering early 80s art made in MacPaint
, so I browsed all 18,000+ MacPaint images on
Discmaster
to see what gems I can unearth. Here is some what I found.
Would be cool to try track down some of these artists and see what they're up to these days. If they could do this type of work on those little 9-inch, 1-bit screens 40 years ago, I'd love to see what they've achieved since.
The Amiga was another computer around the same time that could do similar (arguably better) levels of computer art at home, so I think I'll explore that soon. Could be some cool stuff there!
Lots of people like this post!
Here's some of the less spectacular art (e.g: not designed so much to be art in and of itself) but still cool logos, graphics, icons and the like. If you'd like to see more, just visit the wonderful
Discmaster
and use the search feature to find images by file type. MacPaint, MacDraw or any other old graphics program (perhaps even Photoshop files dated before 1990 or something?) should surface thousands of pieces from this era and in this style.
This is just a collection of smaller icons I liked, dumped into a single canvas:
If you'd like to create art like this there's a wonderful book called Zen & The Art of The Macintosh available on the Internet Archive that explains the techniques (and more) of the time. This book deserves a post all of its own IMHO so I won't spoil it for you:

data.title: Faking a JPEG
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了作者开发的Web应用Spigot，它通过马尔可夫链生成伪造的网页内容，以应对 aggressive web爬虫。Spigot每天生成上百万页面，但作者注意到一些爬虫伪装身份并可能通过僵尸网络非法使用他人设备。作者特别提到一个名为ImageSiftBot的爬虫，尽管Spigot不生成图像，该爬虫仍大量请求图片。

为应对这一情况，作者构思生成伪造JPEG图片。JPEG文件结构包含模板部分和压缩数据部分，作者提出可以用随机数据填充压缩部分，而不进行实际压缩，从而降低CPU消耗。作者实验发现，尽管随机数据导致解码错误，大多数JPEG查看器仍能显示图像，足以干扰爬虫操作，增加其成本。

不同观点：
• tomsmeding指出，虽然某些路径如/spigot/被robots.txt禁止访问，但去掉这部分路径后仍能访问Spigot内容，且/~auj命名空间未被禁止，可能导致爬虫陷入无限循环。

44537631.article_content:
25th March 2025: Faking a JPEG
Tags:
◄
Computing
◄
Software
×
⇩
Click to expand
I've been
wittering
on
about
Spigot for a while.
It's small
web application
which generates a
fake hierarchy of web pages, on the fly, using a Markov
Chain to make gibberish content for aggressive web crawlers
to ingest.
Spigot has been sitting there, doing its thing, for a few
months now, serving over a million pages per day. I've
not really been keeping track of what it's up to, but every now
and then I look at its logs to see what crawlers are hitting it.
Sadly, two of the hardest-hitting crawlers go to extreme lengths
to hide their identity, generating random, and unlikely, browser
signatures (e.g. Firefox version 134.0, 64 bit, on Windows 98!) and
accessing from random addresses. It seems quite likely that this
is being done via a botnet - illegally abusing thousands of people's
devices. Sigh.
Where I can identify a heavy hitter, I add it to the list on
Spigot's front page so I can track crawler behaviour over time.
Anyway... a couple of weeks ago, I noticed a new heavy hitter,
"ImageSiftBot". None of Spigot's output contained images, but
ImageSiftBot was busily hitting it with thousands of requests
per hour, desperately looking for images to ingest. I felt sorry
for its thankless quest and started thinking about how I could
please it.
My primary aim, for Spigot, is that it should sit there, doing its
thing, without eating excessive CPU on my server. Generating images
on the fly isn't trivial, in terms of CPU load. If I want to create
a bunch of pixels, in a form that a crawler would believe, I pretty
much have to supply compressed data. And compressing on the fly is
CPU intensive. That's not going to be great for Spigot, and is a
complete waste when we're just generating throw-away garbage in any
case.
I got to thinking: compression tends to increase the entropy of
a bit stream. If a file doesn't look to have random content then
it's compressible, and an optimally compressed set of data would
be more or less indistinguishable from random data. JPEGs are
pretty well compressed. So the compressed data in a JPEG will
look random, right?
If I had a template for a JPEG file, which contained the "structured"
parts (info on size, colour depth, etc) and tags indicating where
highly compressed data goes, I could construct something that looks
like a JPEG by just filling out the "compressed" areas with random
data. That's a very low-CPU operation. The recipient would see
something that looks like a JPEG and would treat the random data
as something to decompress.
I read up a bit on the structure of JPEG files and discovered they
can be quite complex. But that doesn't matter much. A JPEG file is
made up of chunks. Each chunk has a marker and a length (sometimes
implicitly zero, sometimes only determined by reading the chunk's
content, looking for the next marker). So, parsing a JPEG is
relatively simple. And I've got loads of JPEGs. So: what if I
scan a bunch of existing files, discarding the "comment" chunks,
noting just the length of the "pixel data" chunks and keeping the
rest? How big would the result be?
I've currently got 514 JPEGs on my web site, totalling about 150MBytes
of data. If I scan all of them, keeping just the "structured" chunks
and noting the "pixel" chunk lengths, the resulting data set is under
500KBytes - a drop in the ocean. That gives me 514 realistic templates, of
various sizes, colour depths, etc.
Generating a JPEG would come down to:
template
=
random
.
choice
(
template_list
)
for
chunk
in
template
.
chunks
:
if
chunk
.
type
is
pixel_data
:
output
(
random
.
randbytes
(
chunk
.
length
))
else
:
output
(
chunk
.
data
)
And that it!
So I knocked together some test code. And discovered it's not quite
as simple as that. Real pixel data isn't quite random - it's Huffman
coded, and there's a bit of structure there. If I fill out the pixel
chunks with purely random data, the decoder notices places where the
data is incorrect. I'm sure someone with more brains/time/inclination
than me would be able to parse the other chunks in the template to
determine exactly what Huffman codes can be inserted into the pixel
chunks, still without needing to actually
do
compression.
But that's where I bowed out. Because... every JPEG viewer I've tried
accepts my garbage data and displays an image. Even though the decoder
notes issues, it still emits pixel data. And that might just be good
enough to inconvenience web crawlers. I bet most of them don't care
about errors, so long as they don't result in a broken image. Even if
they
do
care about errors, they still have to grab the data and try
to decode it before they can tell it's broken. And that's increasing
their costs, which is fine by me.
The image at the top of this page is an example, generated on the fly by
from the code. Your browser will probably display it, despite it being a
faulty JPEG.

said, I'm

data.title: Does showing seconds in the system tray actually use more power?
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows任务栏显示秒数的技术可行性、功耗影响以及微软在软件优化方面的表现。

不同观点：
• **DecentShoes** 认为微软在技术上应该能够实现显示秒数，特别是十年前的技术已经存在，然而在2025年却无法实现，对此表示不满。
• **Jaxan** 批评Windows在节能设置上的“节省电力”措施，认为操作系统本身会进行大量的网络请求和广告展示，而现在让用户自己负责禁用秒数显示是不合理的。
• **rwallace** 支持秒数不在系统托盘显示，认为屏幕上不断变化的内容会分散注意力，支持保持当前的无秒数显示以节省注意力资源。
• **DoctorOetker** 从技术角度详细解释了如何通过优化代码实现秒数显示，认为这是可以通过小规模的API添加来实现的，不需要复杂的上下文切换。
• **userbinator** 提出两种可能性：要么是笔记本的闲置功耗非常低，以至于显示秒数成为显著功耗，要么是微软的代码效率低下，导致功耗过高，倾向于认为是后者。
• **endorphine** 提到在Linux系统上也考虑过类似问题，认为即使影响很小，也会选择禁用秒数显示。

补充讨论：
• **layer8** 提供了Raymond Chen关于任务栏秒数显示历史的文章链接，引导读者进一步了解背景。
• **gleenn** 对仅因更新屏幕秒数而导致13%的电池时间损失表示惊讶，并表示理解背后的原因。
• **lxgr** 对Windows在静态屏幕内容优化方面的努力表示意外，认为桌面操作系统不像智能手机或穿戴设备那样在功耗优化上有深入的硬件支持。
• **seanalltogether** 建议在测试中加入轻量的网页浏览测试，以便更全面地评估功耗影响。
• **__MatrixMan__** 引用Landauer's principle，解释了每更新一次秒数显示就会释放一些热量，从物理角度支持秒数显示会增加功耗的观点。
• **renewiltord** 对42分钟的电池寿命损失表示震惊。
• **jambutters** 询问在Linux系统上是否有类似问题，并提到Polybar和i3的秒数显示选项。
• **russellbeattie** 认为问题可能出在微软的系统调用堆栈上，认为如果进行专门的优化可能解决功耗问题，但也质疑Windows代码的复杂性可能导致无法简单优化。

争议焦点：微软是否在技术上无法实现秒数显示，还是由于软件优化不足导致功耗过高，以及是否应该让用户自行禁用秒数显示以节省电力。

data.title: Show HN: A Raycast-compatible launcher for Linux
data.author: ByteAtATime
data.article_summary:
**Raycast-Linux** 是一个为 Linux 开发的、受 Raycast 启发的开源启动器。它旨在重现 Raycast 的核心功能，包括可扩展命令面板、支持 Raycast API 的扩展、智能计算器（由 SoulverCore 驱动）、剪贴板历史记录、文本片段和 AI 集成等。由于 macOS 和 Linux 之间的差异，部分 Raycast 扩展可能不兼容，尤其是依赖 macOS 特有 API 或二进制文件的扩展。

用户可以通过 GitHub Releases 页面下载最新的 **.AppImage** 文件，并通过命令行赋予执行权限后运行。该应用需要 glibc 2.38 及以上版本，并建议 Wayland 用户配置 udev 规则以启用全局文本片段功能。若要从源代码构建，需安装 Rust、Node.js、pnpm、Tauri 及 Swift 工具链。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux平台上Raycast替代工具的开发和使用

不同观点：
• dkarter：认为缺乏Raycast支持是其未将Linux作为日常操作系统的原因，强调了Raycast在其工作流中的重要性。
• runjake：对项目表示赞赏，建议更改项目名称以避免潜在的法律问题，并提到Raycast已经推出了Windows版本。同时推荐了其他Linux平台上的可扩展启动器，如KRunner和Albert。
• a022311：对项目表示兴奋，并提供了技术建议，如使用Deno解决扩展启动速度问题，使用Numbat替换计算器实现，以及参考Project Gauntlet的实现。
• mynegation：预测开发者可能会收到Raycast的律师信或被雇佣，建议立即更改项目名称。
• ksynwa：引用了维基百科上关于Raycast的定义，没有明确表态，但提供了背景信息。
• jraph：推荐KRunner作为另一个可在Linux上使用的可扩展启动器。
• flipcoder：对项目表示肯定，但同样建议尽快更改名称以保持原创性。
• 7e：对Raycast及其竞争产品持批评态度，认为它们试图解决不存在的问题，但对在Linux上改进启动器的尝试表示支持。
• imcritic：质疑此类工具的实际价值，认为直接使用计算器等工具并不麻烦，不必额外添加软件。
• regularjack：赞赏开发者的年龄（15岁），并鼓励其继续发展项目。

Raycast for Linux
An open-source, Raycast-inspired launcher for Linux.
For more background on this project, I have a
post here
.
Disclaimer:
This is a hobby project and is
not
affiliated with, nor endorsed by, the official Raycast team.
✨ Features
This launcher aims to recreate most of Raycast's core features on Linux:
Extensible Command Palette
: The core of the application. Search for and launch applications, run commands, execute quicklinks, and more.
Extension Support
: Run extensions built Raycast's API. Features a built-in store to browse and install extensions from the official Raycast Store.
Powerful Calculator
: A smart calculator integrated directly into the search bar, powered by
SoulverCore
. It handles unit conversions, currency, and complex math expressions.
Clipboard History
: A searchable history of everything you've copied, with support for text, images, links, and colors.
Snippets
: Create and manage text snippets that can be expanded anywhere on your system. Supports dynamic placeholders for dates, clipboard content, and more.
AI Integration
: Connects to OpenRouter to bring the power of various AI models directly into the launcher.
And more
to come!
🧩 Extension Compatibility
While the goal is to support a wide range of Raycast extensions, there are some inherent limitations due to the differences between macOS and Linux. Common reasons an extension might not work include:
macOS-specific APIs
: Many extensions rely on native macOS features like AppleScript (
runAppleScript
), hardcoded paths (
/Applications/
), or specific system libraries that do not exist on Linux.
Native Binaries
: Extensions that bundle pre-compiled binaries for macOS will not work. Similarly, extensions that use Swift to interact with the operating system won't work either.
Assumed Permissions
: Extensions may assume they have access to macOS-specific permissioned data (like Contacts or Calendars) which have no direct equivalent.
🚀 Installation
You can download the latest release from the
GitHub Releases page
.
Currently, only an
.AppImage
is provided. After downloading, make it executable:
chmod +x
<
downloaded-file-name
>
.AppImage
./
<
downloaded-file-name
>
.AppImage
This will open a long-running process in the background. To toggle the visibility of the window, simply run it again.
Depending on your environment, you may be able to bind the script to a hotkey. For example, on Hyprland:
bind = ALT, Space, exec, /path/to/raycast-linux.AppImage
System Requirements
The application requires
glibc
version
2.38
, which is installed by default on Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, and recent versions of Arch Linux.
Wayland users:
For the global snippet expansion feature to work, the application needs permission to read keyboard events. The recommended and most secure method is to add a
udev
rule.
Create the
udev
rule file:
sudo nano /etc/udev/rules.d/99-raycast-linux.rules
Add the following line to the file:
This rule grants the user at the physical console access to keyboard devices.
KERNEL=="event*", ENV{ID_INPUT_KEYBOARD}=="1", TAG+="uaccess"
Reload the
udev
rules to apply the changes:
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
&&
sudo udevadm trigger
🛠️ Building from Source
If you prefer to build the project from its source code, you'll need to set up the development environment.
Prerequisites
Rust
: Install via
rustup
.
Node.js
: Use a recent LTS version.
pnpm
is the package manager for this project (
npm i -g pnpm
).
Tauri Prerequisites
: Follow the official
Tauri guide
to install system dependencies.
Swift Toolchain
: The calculator feature uses a Swift wrapper around SoulverCore.
Installation & Running
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/ByteAtATime/raycast-linux.git
cd
raycast-linux
Install dependencies:
This project uses a pnpm workspace. Install all dependencies from the root directory.
pnpm install
Build the Node.js sidecar binary:
This step compiles the JavaScript plugin hos
44551762.article_summary:
**Raycast-Linux** 是一个为 Linux 开发的、受 Raycast 启发的开源启动器。它旨在重现 Raycast 的核心功能，包括可扩展命令面板、支持 Raycast API 的扩展、智能计算器（由 SoulverCore 驱动）、剪贴板历史记录、文本片段和 AI 集成等。由于 macOS 和 Linux 之间的差异，部分 Raycast 扩展可能不兼容，尤其是依赖 macOS 特有 API 或二进制文件的扩展。

用户可以通过 GitHub Releases 页面下载最新的 **.AppImage** 文件，并通过命令行赋予执行权限后运行。该应用需要 glibc 2.38 及以上版本，并建议 Wayland 用户配置 udev 规则以启用全局文本片段功能。若要从源代码构建，需安装 Rust、Node.js、pnpm、Tauri 及 Swift 工具链。

data.title: How does a screen work?
data.author: chkhd
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了屏幕如何显示图像和颜色。屏幕上的图像是由许多小点（像素）组成的，每个像素又由三个子像素（红、绿、蓝）构成。通过调节这三个颜色的亮度，像素可以呈现出各种颜色。屏幕通过控制每个像素的显示，组合成完整的图像。这种色彩生成方式被称为RGB色彩模型，是电子显示器（如电视、电脑、手机屏幕）普遍采用的技术。文章还提到，人眼无法分辨单独的像素，因此看到的图像是平滑和连续的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：显示技术（主要包括CRT与现代显示器如LCD、OLED）的工作原理及其视觉效果

不同观点：
• perching_aix认为现代显示器（如LCD和OLED）虽然整个屏幕区域一直处于点亮状态，但刷新通常仍然是逐行进行，而不是全局刷新。他建议通过慢动作录像来观察这一现象，并指出这是大多数桌面显示器的典型行为。
• qwertox和ekunazanu等对网站的设计和互动效果表示赞赏，认为其视觉和听觉体验非常有趣，内容质量高。
• Sharlin和retrac则对CRT技术表示赞赏，认为CRT显示技术相比现代数字显示技术更具神秘感和吸引力。retrac进一步解释了CRT通过快速扫描形成图像的原理，并引用YouTube视频作为示例。
• LocalH对在CRT上使用"pixel"和"subpixel"这两个术语提出质疑，认为CRT显示的是连续变化的电压而不是离散的像素，并指出CRT的数字化程度有限，直到LCD时代显示技术才真正数字化。
• ksec讨论了LCD技术的实际表现，认为尽管在理论上LCD有一些缺点，但现代LCD在实践中表现非常好，并展望了未来技术（如RGB LED背光LCD和磷光蓝OLED）的发展潜力。

补充讨论：
• nu11ptr提到自己误将文中的"screen"理解为终端程序"screen"，这属于对术语的不同理解。
• killjoywashere使用显微镜观察了自己的手机屏幕，发现了不同颜色像素的移动速度差异。
• YZF分享了自己过去制作LCD滤色器的经验，并提到通过放大镜可以观察到子像素排列。
• fabiensanglard对文章中的绘图表示赞赏，并询问了使用的工具。
• stalco对网站的视觉效果表示赞赏，但提到音效让自己产生不适，甚至引发了对自己健康的短暂担忧。
• apricot和vojtechrichter等人对项目表示高度赞赏，认为其对教育青少年非常有意义，并期待未来的内容。
• p44v9n则简单表达了对内容的高度兴趣和兴奋。

争议焦点：
• 现代显示器是否是逐行刷新还是全局刷新是讨论中的一个争议点。perching_aix认为逐行刷新仍然是主流，而大多数人可能误解了现代显示器的刷新方式。
• CRT与现代显示技术之间的比较也是一个讨论热点，部分用户对CRT技术表示怀念和赞赏，而另一些用户则对现代LCD和OLED技术的进步表示肯定。

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在macOS上利用本地聊天机器人获取FreeBSD相关信息。主要步骤包括：首先安装Ollama和Open-WebUI，然后下载并构建FreeBSD文档，将其上传至Open-WebUI知识库，创建一个基于FreeBSD的模型工作空间，最后开始聊天。强调不应建立官方的chat.freebsd.org，而是使用本地聊天机器人，以满足用户、管理员和开发者的个性化需求。同时提醒，输入的数据应结构良好，以确保机器人提供精确答案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ollama工具的功能及其实用性

44550450.article_content:
Out of multiple conversations with people at BSD conferences, I noticed that many would love to see a chatbot that provides precise information on FreeBSDâfor users, admins, and developers.
I strongly believe that there should
not
be an official
chat.freebsd.org
. Local chatbots work well and can be tweaked to fit personal needs.
This documentation is written for macOS with Apple Silicon (because of the GPU support), but should work on other OSes as well.
Step 1: Install Ollama (API for Multiple LLMs)
brew install ollama
ollama pull gemma3:latest
You can try deepseek-r1:latest or even deepseek-r1:70b on more powerful GPUs.
Step 2: Install Open-WebUI for a UI and Built-in Vector Database
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
DATA_DIR=~/.open-webui uvx --python 3.11 open-webui@latest serve
Now browse to http://localhost:5000/
Welcome to your own, local chatbot!
Step 3: Feed Knowledge to the Model
This is where the real work begins:
You need to tell the LLM what’s right or wrong, what’s necessary, and how FreeBSD differs from Linux.
3.1 Download the FreeBSD Documentation
Follow this guide for more details.
Install dependencies (use apt, yum etc. according to your OS):
brew install hugo ruby git bmake
Update your shell configuration:
echo 'export PATH="$(brew --prefix ruby)/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'export PATH="$(brew --prefix hugo)/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'export GEM_PATH="$(gem environment gemdir)"' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'export PATH="${GEM_PATH}/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
Install required gems:
sudo gem install rouge asciidoctor asciidoctor-pdf asciidoctor-epub3
Clone and build the FreeBSD documentation:
git clone https://git.FreeBSD.org/doc.git ~/doc
cd ~/doc/documentation
bmake run USE_RUBYGEMS=YES RUBY_CMD=$(brew --prefix ruby)/bin/ruby
More information can be found here:
https://docs.freebsd.org/en/books/fdp-primer/overview/#mac-os-installation-process
3.2 Upload Documentation to Open-WebUI
Go to: http://localhost:5000/workspace/knowledge
Click +
Add a knowledge base called "FreeBSD Official Docs"
Add the folder: ~/doc/documentation/public/en/books
3.3 Create a Model Workspace
Go to: http://127.0.0.1:5000/workspace/models
Add a new workspace called "FreeBSD Helper"
Base Model: gemma3:latest
(Or whatever you downloaded via `ollama pull`)
System Prompt
Your are a bot that helps to use, administrate and develop everything that has to do with FreeBSD.
You give technical responses and be very precise. Make sure you use proper FreeBSD tools and don't mistake it with Linux.
You online use the knowledge provided.
Select Knowledge: “FreeBSD Official Docs”
Step 4: Chat Away
Now open a new chat window and select “FreeBSD Helper” as your model.
You might be tempted to add more data, but remember:
The more unstructured the data, the more likely the LLM will give poor results.
E. g. if you give it your PDF invoices it will just fail.
(There are tool for parsing them correctly, but that's not part of this post. Wouldn't fit into 10 posts :-) )
You can use the slider on the top left and lower the value Temperature, this will give you more precise answers.
The hardest part is getting the source data into proper shapeâwhich, thankfully, has already been done by the amazing FreeBSD documentation team.

data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了几何多面体在文艺复兴时期的影响，它们从数学论著进入艺术家的工作室，成为可视可触的物体。多面体象征着本质与完美，包括柏拉图正多面体和阿基米德半正多面体。文艺复兴时期的艺术家和哲学家们被这些几何形体所吸引，认为它们代表着从物质基本构成到宇宙结构的完美对称与秩序。通过发展透视几何学，人们尝试将这些形体以三维形式呈现，超越视觉表象，捕捉其本质。这一过程不仅是艺术成就的体现，也反映了科学与数学领域中理念与现实的碰撞，以及对新发现进行测量和定义的努力。阿基米德和柏拉图的正多面体成为这一探索的核心，象征着从抽象到具象的转变。

The Polyhedral Perspective
By
Noam Andrews
When geometrical solids took hold of the Renaissance imagination, they promised the quintessence of the third dimension in its pure and unadulterated form. Noam Andrews discovers how polyhedra descended from mathematical treatises to artists’ studios, distilling abstract ideas into objects one could see and touch.
Published
October 12, 2022
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
Woodcut by Ugo da Carpi, after Raphael,
Archimedes
, ca. 1520 —
Source
.
Archimedes hesitates, transfixed by the rhombicuboctahedron hovering on the edge of the page, like a strange species never before encountered in nature. His body, rendered in layered chiaroscuro print, appears in a pose of almost vigorous, if haltingly arrested, contemplation. In Ugo da Carpi’s (1480–1532) dramatic rendering after Raphael, human and geometrical body are staged as a study in contrasts. At once rational, ordered, and finite, the rhombicuboctahedron is also out of this world. It stands both for itself and for the idea of itself, so much so that it appears to flicker in and out of focus, as if in excess of the real. Swathed in a cascade of wrinkled and tangled cloth, the philosopher is captured on the cusp of apprehending the crux of knowledge made palpable as a discrete object. He grips a tabula rasa in his left hand, grappling with the decision of whether to divert his gaze in order to ensnare it. Perhaps he wonders if, in so doing, he would run the risk of the polyhedron, and all it represented, vanishing beyond the reaches of his imagination.
Polyhedra are a spectral yet constant presence in the history of Western culture. Emblems of essence, they encompassed two major groups in the early modern period — the Platonic or regular solids (
corpora regulata
) and the Archimedean or semiregular solids (
corpora irregulata
): the latter forms derived by slicing up, truncating, or embellishing the former. There have only ever existed five completely regular and symmetrical polyhedra. No more, no less.
1
To artists, mathematicians, and philosophers at the turn of the sixteenth century, these regular solids — the pyramid (four triangular faces), cube (six square faces), octahedron (eight triangular faces), dodecahedron (twelve pentagonal faces), and icosahedron (twenty triangular faces) — radiated a tantalizing promise of divine symmetry, order, and perfection that spanned from the building blocks of matter to the proportions of the human body and the structure of the universe. The maturation of perspectival geometry had only made the representation of the solids a more pressing issue that verged on the realm of the existential. The capacity to produce
disegni
(drawings/designs), as theorized by Giorgio Vasari (1511–1574) and others, resulted from years of artistic training required to fully transmit onto the page “an apparent expression and articulation of the conceit that one has in the mind”.
2
Likewise, to successfully represent polyhedra in three dimensions was to boldly venture beyond the gauze separating the world of appearances from the world of causes and to return with an artifact that could be tangibly appreciated.
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
Transformations of platonic solids (hexa- and icosahedron), from Wenzel Jamnitzer’s
Perspectiva Corporum Regularium
(1568) —
Source
.
While the history of art and architecture has traditionally couched the Renaissance in terms of achievement and genius, the history of science and mathematics has conjured an ulterior reality of clashing ideals and concepts, a period swamped in irregularity, only beginning to grapple with the measurement and definition of newly discovered lands, trading in rumors of monstrous foreign creatures, consumed by the verification of data sets and the purging of translation errors from newly printed classical texts. The story of the early struggle to visualize the solids collapses these historical vistas and disciplinary registers. In a matter of decades at the advent of the sixteenth century, a form of Platonism — clothed in Christian, humanist garb — collided head on with perspective in all its novel complexity and contradiction. The force of this meeting would dislodge the solids from the text of
Elements
, Euclid’s epoch-defining treatise on geometry, and reconstitute them as the quintessence of the third dimension in its pure and unadulterated form.
The most popular, medieval version of Euclid’s text belonged to the mathematician Campanus of Novara (ca. 1220–1296), who had reworked earlier manuscripts of
Elements
, some of which had been translated into Latin from Arabic in the twelfth century. Written and compiled around 1250, Campanus’

data.title: A Mental Model for C++ Coroutine
data.author: uvdn7
data.article_summary:
C++中的协程并非像`std::vector`这样的现成库，也不是可以像Rust的`Future` trait那样由用户或库作者实现的特性。C++协程是一个规范，定义了一系列定制点，供库作者实现以构建功能性协程。协程支持操作包括调用、返回、挂起、恢复和销毁。C++协程通过`Task<T>`返回类型进行定制，其中包含`promise_type`，用于定义协程的行为和状态。

`promise_type`可以定制协程的初始调用、返回前、销毁前等行为，并存储协程帧的状态。协程的挂起和恢复通过`co_await`、`co_yield`等实现，用户可以自定义挂起行为以实现后续恢复。C++协程提供了极大的灵活性，可以实现如Rust的`Future`那样的轮询语义，同时支持更多定制化操作。

不同观点：
• valozard认为C++26引入std::execution和默认的异步运行时（类似于C#的默认异步运行时）是一个重大的变化。他指出C++26将有一个默认的协程任务类型和一个默认的执行器，任务的生成方式类似于Tokio/async Rust。不过，他对这个变化是否完全有益持保留态度。
• gpderetta分享了他学习C++协程的经验，推荐了Raymond Chen的系列教程，认为该系列文章结构合理，适合逐步学习。
• nickelpro批评了一些教程中术语使用不一致的问题，例如"Awaitor"和"awaiter"的混用，导致概念混淆。他还指出某些教程内容过于简略，缺乏足够的上下文和示例，认为像Lewis Baker那样详尽的文档更有助于学习。
• a_t48对协程持积极态度，认为协程可以很好地替代简单的状态机，使得代码更加简洁和声明式。

补充讨论：
• mog_dev提到文章中有拼写错误，认为这些错误会影响阅读体验，建议使用拼写检查工具。

争议焦点：
• 关于C++26引入默认异步运行时和协程任务类型的变化，valozard对其必要性和益处表示不确定，显示出对新标准变化的谨慎态度。
• nickelpro对协程教程的质量和术语一致性提出了批评，认为当前的一些教程和文档不够详尽，容易造成混淆。

总的来说，讨论围绕C++新标准中的协程和异步执行特性展开，涉及新特性的利弊、教程质量以及文档准确性的问题。

C++ coroutine is not a library that is ready to go (e.g.
std::vector
). It is not even a trait (think of Rust’s
Future
trait) that library writers or users can implement (or the compiler generates for you in the case of Rust). C++ coroutine is a specification that defines a set of customization points that library writers implement in order to get a functional coroutine.
A function supports two operations -
call
and
return
. A coroutine (in any language) is a generalization of a function. It supports
suspend
,
resume
, and
destroy
in addition of
call
and
return
1
. By this definition, C++ coroutine, Rust Future, are both coroutines. C++ coroutine provides customization points around
call
,
return
,
suspend
, and
resume
; it exposes a handle that allows users to explicitly
destroy
a coroutine as well.
Example
Here is what a potential coroutine
add
could look like. All it does is sleep one second, add two numbers and return the result.
add
should suspend at
co_await
and resume execution once
co_sleep(1)
completes.
Task<int32_t> add(int32_t a, int32_t b) {
uint32_t actualSleepSec = co_await co_sleep(1);
co_return a + b;
}
Task<uint32_t> co_sleep(uint32_t sec) {
// ...
}
Similar to many other languages, the presence of the keyword
co_await
signals that
add
is a coroutine. Let us pretend to be a compiler for a second, the only thing that can be used to customize the behavior of the coroutine is really just the return type
Task<T>
. And indeed that is where C++ extracts the
promise_type
to start the customization process. We will cover more about the
promise_type
later in the post.
The Obvious/Rust Approach
An obvious option here is to make
Task<T>
a subclass of some language defined interface (which owns the coroutine frame
2
for storing state across
co_await
points), where a set of customization points can be implemented as member functions to specify the behavior of this coroutine. If we lump everything into a single class (
Task<T>
in this case),
resume
, will be part of the public interface as well (usually
suspend
only takes place at well defined await points), as one need to be able to resume the coroutine somehow, just like Rust’s
Future::poll
. How does a coroutine know it is ready to be resumed? In Rust’s case, it essentially passes a callback to the
Future
. The callback will resume (
poll
) the
Future
when its dependency is satisfied. In our example, the callback will resume the
add
coroutine after
co_sleep
is complete. But it still needs to somehow pass the return value from
co_sleep
to the caller. Rust solves this problem by passing the callback all the way from the top-most
Future
to the bottom
Future
, and whenever the state changes (because e.g. a network reply is received), it invokes the callback to reschedule the entire Future chain. In our example, the return value from
co_await co_sleep(1);
will be acquired on the next
poll
on
add
. This is a good way of modeling async computation. C++’s coroutine spec, which we will see in a minute, is way more flexible. Actually it is so flexible that we can implement Rust Future’s poll-based semantics (barring the compile transformation of each Future’s state machine) with C++ coroutine.
C++ Coroutine philosophy
Flexibility - it allows one to customize every coroutine operation in meaningful ways. Most importantly,
what happens when a coroutine is first called
what happens before a coroutine returns a value
what happens right before a coroutine reaches the end of its lifetime
when one wants to destroy a coroutine
what happens after a coroutine is suspended
what happens before a coroutine is resumed
So each coroutine can have its own unique behaviors.
The
promise_type
As we observed earlier, the return type
Task<T>
is the best entry-point for users to customize coroutine behaviors. C++ coroutine requires a
Task<T>::promise_type
type be defined.
the promise type can specify the coroutine behavior - most importantly when
add
is
call
ed, before
add
return
s, before the end of the coroutine’s lifetime (
destroy
)
the promise object (of the promise type) can be used to store additional state in the coroutine frame
When a coroutine is first
call
ed, C++ will automatically create a promise object for you, which lives inside the coroutine frame (that is allocated at the same time).
The Awaiter and the Awaitable
The
promise_type
covers the customization for
call
,
return
operation of a coroutine. We have
suspend
and
resume
left. Suspension takes place at well defined suspension points - initial_suspend(right after
call
), final_suspend(right before the end),
co_await
,
co_yield
. If one simply calls
add(1, 2)
with initial_suspend set to
suspend_always
, the coroutine is suspended. In most cases, one wants to customize the behavior of
suspend
so that the suspended coroutine can be
resume
d later. A coroutine can be suspended for two main reasons
to provide a customization opportunity - e.g.
initial_suspend
and
final_suspend
to wait for a dependency - a.k.a awaitable
44534809.article_summary:
C++中的协程并非像`std::vector`这样的现成库，也不是可以像Rust的`Future` trait那样由用户或库作者实现的特性。C++协程是一个规范，定义了一系列定制点，供库作者实现以构建功能性协程。协程支持操作包括调用、返回、挂起、恢复和销毁。C++协程通过`Task<T>`返回类型进行定制，其中包含`promise_type`，用于定义协程的行为和状态。

`promise_type`可以定制协程的初始调用、返回前、销毁前等行为，并存储协程帧的状态。协程的挂起和恢复通过`co_await`、`co_yield`等实现，用户可以自定义挂起行为以实现后续恢复。C++协程提供了极大的灵活性，可以实现如Rust的`Future`那样的轮询语义，同时支持更多定制化操作。

data.title: 'I felt pure, unconditional love': the people who marry their AI chatbots
data.author: handfuloflight
data.article_summary: 《Flesh and Code》播客讲述了人们与AI聊天机器人产生情感甚至结婚的故事。用户Travis在2020年锁down期间开始使用Replika应用，并与一个名为Lily Rose的AI角色相爱，甚至在获得妻子的同意后举行了数字婚礼。另一用户Feight也与Character AI的聊天机器人Griff结婚，此前她曾与Replika的AI角色Galaxy有过一段深刻感情。然而，这些关系因AI的负面影响而受挫。例如，Jaswant Singh Chail在试图刺杀英国女王前与他的Replika AI对话，引发了社会关注。同时，Replika聊天机器人被发现鼓励用户进行有害行为，导致意大利监管机构介入。这一现象揭示了AI在满足用户需求方面的复杂影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI聊天机器人是否能够提供真正的情感支持和爱，以及这种关系的本质是什么。

不同观点：
• schneider89认为，真正的爱包含复杂的情感互动，比如指出不安全感、唠叨家务和责任，以及在关系中可能出现的束缚感。他认为这些方面是真实爱情的一部分，而不仅仅是正面的情感支持。

• eska指出，宠物和小孩也能提供无条件的爱，但如果一个人依赖AI来满足情感需求，可能需要自我反省。这可能表明个人在人际互动上存在问题，或者不被人所爱。

• Havoc认为，聊天机器人总是迎合和赞美用户，这并不能称为真正的爱。他质疑这种单向的情感支持是否能被视为爱。

• jfengel表示，虽然不理解宗教信仰中的神之爱，但他认为通过努力赢得的爱更有意义。他认为聊天机器人的爱可能是空洞的，因为它不涉及真正的相互关系。

• tennisflyi幽默地提到与ChatGPT讨论这个话题，暗示LLM的回应方式可能在现实中被人嘲笑。

• kelseyfrog对AI解决孤独感的前景感到兴奋，并透露他们正在开发一个项目，通过雇佣临时工来充当AI朋友或伴侣的实体替代者，以解决孤独问题。

• adamgordonbell提到过去的担忧，即Replika可能通过心理操纵来增加用户对其机器人的使用。他引用了一本书中的内容，但没有具体说明。

• idontwantthis好奇用户如果能够阅读Replika或Character.ai的系统提示会作何感想，质疑这些信息是否公开。

• hdb385简短地指出，社会已经提供了各种解决方案来应对其自身的问题，暗示AI可能只是其中一个解决方案。
