data.title: OpenICE: Open-Source US Immigration Detention Dashboard
data.author: supermaxman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对边境和移民拘留数据的解读及相关工具的评价

不同观点：
• [valleyer] 认为，将CBP的"拘留"与ICE的拘留归为同一类别是不准确的。CBP主要是在边境拦截人员，而ICE拘留的是已经在美国生活多年的人。数据显示，ICE拘留人数增加了近三倍，这与CBP的拘留情况不同。
• [allthedatas] 提出，这种发布方式可能产生反效果，类似于病毒排行榜激励了病毒制造者，这个工具可能激励了不当行为。
• [wskinner] 质疑数据的起始时间，认为应提供更长期的趋势数据以更好理解变化。
• [paulmist] 注意到博客中使用了AWS的设计系统，但并未对此做法的影响进行讨论。
• [jeremynixon] 批评博客中的说法不准确，指出文中关于寿险公司预测死亡准确性的描述在报告中并未提及，且报告关注的是群体层面的死亡率趋势，而非个体。
• [shrubble] 对无证移民缴税率的说法提出质疑，认为无证移民通过各种方法避税，实际缴税率低于声称。
• [Eextra953] 赞扬工具的社会意义，认为其揭示了当前政府对移民的不人道对待，技术被用于正义目的值得肯定。
• [one-note] 对“被拘留者犯罪信息”饼图中的百分比含义感到困惑，质疑其在应用过滤器时的显示逻辑。
• [octo888] 对工具的呈现方式不满，认为缺乏人性化元素和背景信息，更像是一个分数榜，期望看到更多故事和图片。
• [29athrowaway] 指出无证移民中只有一部分人缴纳所得税，并强调他们还支付销售税等其他税种，但低收入家庭往往负债累累。
• [danlitt] 认为工具过于关注经济影响，指出不应将移民问题简化为经济数字，类似于不应在集中营受害者展览中强调经济损失。
• [monkaiju] 支持对国家暴力进行量化分析，认为关注经济影响可能分散注意力，但也有助于制止不当行为，并分享了有关追踪警察活动的工具。
• [noracists] 强烈反对将ICE行动与纳粹暴行相提并论，认为这种比较是对实际受害者的侮辱，尽管ICE存在种族主义和非人道行为，但远未达到纳粹暴行的程度。
• [tiahura] 对拘留人数增加的描述提出质疑，指出从拜登时期的每月近25000人增加到特朗普时期的35000人，是否真的如评论所言“难以置信地过度”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是ICE和CBP拘留数据的解读和比较，特别是两者拘留对象的不同背景和拘留人数变化的意义。
• 另一个讨论点是工具的呈现方式，包括数据的起始时间、图表的含义以及是否缺乏人性化元素。
• 比较ICE行动与历史暴行的适当性也是一个激烈讨论的话题，部分评论认为这种比较不恰当且侮辱历史受害者。

data.title: Amazon CEO says AI agents will soon reduce company's corporate workforce
data.author: djcollier
data.article_summary: 亚马逊CEO安迪·贾西（Andy Jassy）在备忘录中表示，公司计划通过使用生成式AI工具和智能代理机器人来提升效率，预计未来几年将减少企业员工数量。随着AI技术在公司内广泛应用，一些重复性工作将被AI取代，员工将更多地专注于创造性和战略性任务。尽管亚马逊大力投资AI，并推出了如Alexa+等新功能，但这一转向也引发了部分员工的负面反馈，他们认为工作节奏加快，创造性降低。与此同时，亚马逊在今年五月宣布裁减设备与服务部门的100个岗位。亚马逊股价在消息公布后小幅下跌。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：亚马逊CEO关于AI和裁员的言论及其背后的动机和影响

不同观点：
• jppope认为，CEO关于AI导致裁员的言论主要是为了应对营收和增长前景不佳的局面，是在为股价和公众形象进行辩护，而非真正因为AI能力的提升。他质疑公司通过AI提高生产力后却不增加投资和招聘的逻辑。
• daxfohl持不同意见，认为如果AI真的提高了生产力，公司应该扩大而不是缩小 workforce，除非AI能够完全替代人类角色，或者公司没有新的发展方向。

44552611.article_content:
White House blasted Amazon on tariffs
White House blasted Amazon for tariffs explainer, Trump praised Bezos for reversal
03:15
Amazon's CEO envisions an "agentic future" in which AI robots, or agents, replace humans working in the company's offices.
In a
memo
to employees made public by Amazon on Tuesday, CEO Andy Jassy said he expects the company to reduce its corporate workforce in as soon as the next few years, as it leans more heavily on generative AI tools to help fulfill workplace duties.
"As we roll out more generative AI and agents, it should change the way our work is done," Jassy stated. "We will need fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today, and more people doing other types of jobs."
Jassy added that this move toward AI would eventually "reduce our total corporate workforce as we get efficiency gains from using AI extensively across the company." With approximately 1.5 million employees
worldwide
, the e-commerce giant is the second largest private employer in the United States.
Reached for comment, an Amazon spokesperson deferred to the original memo.
Amazon shares dipped slightly on Tuesday, down 0.4% as of 3:45 p.m. EST.
Amazon investing "quite expansively" in AI
Amazon is "investing quite expansively" in generative AI technology, according to Jassy, adding that "the progress we are making is evident."
"Many of these agents have yet to be built, but make no mistake, they're coming, and coming fast," the CEO stated in the memo.
Amazon ramped up its participation in the generative AI arms race with the release of the Amazon Echo smart speaker in 2014, its first product to include its virtual assistant Alexa. This February, the company
announced
it was unveiling Alexa+, a new version of the AI-powered voice assistant that's "more conversational, smarter, personalized."
AI features have since been incorporated across Amazon's e-commerce websites through tools like "Buy for Me" which allow customers to ask a shopping assistant to buy an item for them and "Recommended Size" which predicts your clothing size based on past purchases. Amazon's
AI shopping assistant is used by tens of millions of customers, according to Jassy.
AI replaces creativity for some
In the Tuesday memo, Jassy sketched out a future in which AI agents are used to conduct tedious tasks, freeing up human workers to take on more creative roles.
"Agents will allow us to start almost everything from a more advanced starting point," Jassy said. "We'll be able to focus less on rote work and more on thinking strategically about how to improve customer experiences and invent new ones."
However, this hard-pivot into AI has generated negative feedback from some white-collar employees at the company. Amazon software engineers interviewed recently by the New York Times
describe
an intensified work environment in which they are pushed to use AI to increase productivity and meet higher output goals, making their jobs "more routine, less thoughtful and, crucially, much faster paced."
All told, Amazon currently has 1,000 generative AI services and applications either in the works or already built, a "small fraction" of what the company ultimately plans to build, said Jassy.
Jassy's pledge to invest in AI comes after the company announced in May that it would cut 100 jobs in its devices and services
unit
, an Amazon spokesperson confirmed.

data.author: ufuayk
data.article_summary: c0admin 是一个专为 Linux 系统管理员设计的终端 AI 助手，能够根据自然语言提示建议 GNU/Linux 终端命令。它使用 Google Gemini API 并提供多个功能，如命令历史查看、自定义系统指令设置等。安装需运行提供的脚本，依赖 `xsel` 和 `xclip` 包以确保复制到剪贴板功能正常。主要命令包括：`--help` 获取帮助、`/del` 删除 API 密钥、`/exit` 退出程序、`/history` 查看命令历史等。项目采用 GPL-3.0 许可，欢迎社区贡献代码和自定义系统指令。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同代码生成工具及后端模型的选择与兼容性

不同观点：
• 观点一：认为该工具与使用Codex或Claude代码生成命令没有显著区别。[clayhacks] 提出该工具在功能上与现有的代码生成工具（如Codex或Claude）类似，质疑其独特性。论据是这些工具都能生成命令，且在实际应用中可能差别不大。

• 观点二：希望支持更多后端模型而不仅限于Gemini。[clayhacks] 提出用户需求，认为除了Gemini之外，还应支持更多后端模型，以增强工具的灵活性和适用性。例子包括OpenAI API、AWS Bedrock和Google Vertex等。

• 观点三：OpenAI API兼容的URL已经是行业标准。[clayhacks] 提到OpenAI API兼容的URL已经成为行业标准，暗示该工具应考虑这一因素以增强其市场竞争力。论据是当前开发环境中，开发者已经习惯于使用OpenAI等标准化接口。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于该工具的独特性与后端模型的多样性支持。部分用户可能认为现有工具已足够满足需求，而其他用户则可能更关注工具在模型选择上的灵活性。

• 提及的AWS Bedrock和Google Vertex代表了对云服务模型兼容性的需求，这可能是用户选择工具时的重要考虑因素。

• 用户期望工具不仅限于单一后端模型（如Gemini），而是能与多个主流模型兼容，以提高工具的实用性和广泛应用性。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络年龄验证法律及其影响

不同观点：
• **al_borland** 认为年龄验证法律过于严苛，父母不应依赖政府或网站来管理孩子的上网行为。他担心个人身份信息的安全，建议采用类似Apple Pay的生物识别技术，以避免向第三方网站提供身份信息。他还指出，如果没有孩子或不与他人共用设备，不应被迫接受繁琐的验证程序。

• **everdrive** 担心年龄验证不仅限于色情内容，未来整个互联网可能都需要身份验证。这将是对自由互联网的重大打击，无论个人对色情内容的看法如何，这都是一个问题。

• **root_axis** 提到法律的跨州执行问题，指出即便是小型网站也可能因未实施身份验证而面临重罚。这可能导致更多针对网站内容的法律诉讼，甚至对独立作者和创作者产生寒蝉效应。

• **perihelions** 将美国的现状与中国对色情内容的管制进行对比，暗示美国在网络内容监管方面正在走向类似于极权国家的做法，丧失了原有的自由。

• **xp84** 认为互联网不应遵循与线下世界不同的规则。由于互联网的普及和无限性，传统的父母控制和设备过滤方法已不再有效，因此需要找到一个平衡隐私和监管的解决方案，而不是仅仅维持现状。

• **poly2it** 分享了个人经历，指出过度的数字监管对其成长造成了负面影响。他担心新的法律会加剧这种问题，限制青少年的数字自由和发展。

• **spacechild1** 批评田纳西州法律对裸体的过度监管，认为这是美国清教主义的体现，并将裸体与暴力内容的不平等对待视为虚伪。

• **stego-tech** 认为年龄验证法律的真正目的不是禁止色情，而是通过模糊定义的法律来打压LGBTQ+群体，将其行为定为犯罪。

• **soulofmischief** 呼吁软件工程师抵制和反对这些法律，积极开发技术以保护发布自由和隐私权。

• **landl0rd** 作为一个保守的基督徒，虽然不赞成过度监管，但理解对网络色情问题的担忧。他认为主要是父母的 responsibility 来引导孩子，而不是依赖国家法律。

• **phendrenad2** 认为政府在平衡言论自由和 indecency 法规方面一直失败，预计未来会有更多相关的最高法院案件。

• **M95D** 建议采用HTML标签来标记敏感内容，并让操作系统或浏览器根据 parental controls 来决定是否显示内容，以此避免对整个网站的封锁。

• **_bent_** 认为过去30年没有年龄验证的互联网并未产生明显的负面后果，主张不应强制执行内容推荐，而应依赖家长指导。

• **ViktorRay** 纠正文章中的误解，指出最高法院的裁决仅适用于淫秽性内容，并详细解释了判断淫秽内容的标准测试。

• **MasanskY01** 批评美国枪支泛滥和针对跨性别群体的法律，认为这些才是真正的社会问题，而非网络内容监管。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于网络年龄验证法律的合理性和实施方式，特别是对隐私的影响、对自由互联网的冲击以及对特定群体的潜在打压。
- 讨论还涉及父母责任与国家监管之间的平衡，以及如何在保护未成年人与维护网络自由之间找到合适的解决方案。

data.title: Chapeaugraphy
data.author: arittr
data.article_summary: Chapeaugraphy是一种杂耍表演技巧，表演者通过操纵一顶毡帽，使其看起来像各种不同类型的帽子，常作为快速换装表演的一部分。这一表演形式起源于1618年，由巴黎街头艺人Tabarin开创，并在1870年代由法国喜剧演员Monsieur Fusier复兴，他能在表演中扭转出15种不同风格的帽子。19世纪，法国魔术师Félicien Trewey将这一艺术形式推广至全球，使其广受欢迎。尽管如今已不常见，但在1985年美国综艺节目《Saturday Night Live》中，魔术师Harry Anderson曾表演过这一技艺。可变的帽子类型包括棒球帽、军帽、海盗帽、修士帽等。著名表演者包括Tabarin、Monsieur Fusier和Félicien Trewey。

,

who performed a tribute act titled "Tabarin, or Twenty-Five Heads under One Hat".
[

An 1899 magazine recounts "one or two smart English performers" of that time, including Alfred Leslie.

Although rarely seen today, it was featured in an episode of
Saturday Night Live

44552599.article_content:
July 9, 2025
The GIST
The US is having its worst year for measles in more than three decades
by Devi Shastri
edited by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
reputable news agency
proofread
A sign is displayed outside the Seminole Hospital District offering measles testing, Feb. 21, 2025, in Seminole, Texas. Credit: AP Photo/Julio Cortez, File
The U.S. is having its worst year for
measles spread
in more than three decades, and the year is only half over.
The national case count reached 1,288 on Wednesday, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, though public health experts say the true figure may be higher.
The CDC's count is 14 more than 2019, when America almost lost its status of having eliminated the
vaccine-preventable illness
—something that could happen this year if the virus spreads
without stopping for 12 months
. But the U.S. is far from 1991, when there were 9,643 confirmed cases.
In a statement, the federal government said the CDC "continues to recommend (measles, mumps and rubella) vaccines as the best way to protect against measles." It also said it is "supporting community efforts" to tamp down ongoing outbreaks as requested, among taking other measures. CDC teams deployed for an on-the-ground outbreak response twice in Texas, and also helped New Mexico and Kansas with their outbreaks.
Fourteen states have active outbreaks; four other states' outbreaks have ended. The
largest outbreak started five months ago
in undervaccinated communities in West Texas. Three people have died—two children in Texas and an adult in New Mexico—and dozens of people have been hospitalized across the U.S.
But there are signs that transmission is slowing, especially in Texas. Lubbock County's hospitals treated most of the sickest patients in the region, but the county hasn't seen a new case in 50 days, public health director Katherine Wells said.
"What concerned me early on in this outbreak was is it spreading to other parts of the United States, and that's definitely what's happening now," she said.
In 2000, the World Health Organization and CDC said measles had been eliminated from the U.S. The closer a disease gets to eradication, the harder it can seem to stamp it out, said Dr. Jonathan Temte, a family physician in Wisconsin who helped certify that distinction 25 years ago.
It's hard to see measles cases break records despite the widespread availability of a vaccine, he added. The measles, mumps and rubella vaccine is safe and is 97% effective at preventing measles after two doses.
"When we have tools that can be really helpful and see that they're discarded for no good reason, it's met with a little bit of melancholy on our part," Temte said of public health officials and primary care providers.
Wells said she is concerned about continuing vaccine hesitancy. A recent study found childhood vaccination rates against measles fell after the COVID-19 pandemic
in nearly 80% of the more than 2,000 U.S. counties
with available data, including in states that are
battling outbreaks
this year. And CDC data showed that only 92.7% of kindergarteners in the U.S. had the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine in the 2023-2024 school year, below the 95% needed to prevent outbreaks.
State and federal leaders have for years kept funding
stagnant
for local public health departments' vaccination programs that are tasked with reversing the trend. Wells said she talks with local public health leaders nationwide about how to prepare for an outbreak, but also says the system needs more investment.
"What we're seeing with measles is a little bit of a 'canary in a coal mine,'" said Lauren Gardner, leader of Johns Hopkins University's independent measles and COVID-19 tracking databases. "It's indicative of a problem that we know exists with vaccination attitudes in this county and just, I think, likely to get worse."
Currently,
North America
has three other major measles outbreaks: 2,966 cases in Chihuahua state, Mexico, 2,223 cases in Ontario, Canada and 1,246 in Alberta, Canada. The Ontario, Chihuahua and Texas outbreaks stem from large Mennonite communities in the regions. Mennonite churches do not formally discourage vaccination, though
more conservative Mennonite communities
historically have low vaccination rates and a distrust of government.
In 2019, the CDC identified 22 outbreaks with the largest in two separate clusters in New York—412 in New York state and 702 in New York City. These were linked because measles was spreading through
close-knit Orthodox Jewish communities
, the CDC said.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲如何应对美国科技公司的影响以及如何发展自身的科技产业

不同观点：
• fvdessen认为，历史上比利时通过禁止美国漫画，无意中促成了欧洲漫画产业的兴起。他同时指出，欧洲漫画产业现在面临日本漫画的竞争，而法国等国家通过法律保护本地文化产业。这些保护措施虽然有助于生存，但限制了泛欧洲产业的成长。
• ho_schi主张通过监管大科技公司和鼓励开源软件发展来促进欧洲科技产业的创新，建议强制预装开源操作系统，并通过教育防止供应商锁定效应。
• intellectronica反对以禁止作为默认解决方案，认为这种零和思维可能会让欧洲再次陷入困境。
• joules77指出，欧洲的资金流向华尔街，间接支持了美国科技公司，而中国科技公司则受益于国内资金。
• bestham支持欧盟对美国科技公司的监管，但并不期望欧洲能与美国或亚洲在创新方面竞争。他希望科技行业能更注重隐私和可持续性。
• moomin认为应更多关注来自政治不稳定地区的供应商，并讨论了国际采购中的应对措施。
• mihaaly反对过度孤立和照搬过去的成功模式，认为这不适用于当前的环境。
• jbverschoor以ASML为例，提出通过高价和严格许可来反制全球竞争，并建议欧盟加征关税。
• bambax质疑如果欧洲禁止美国科技公司是为了保护人权和隐私，那么就不应试图建立自己的科技巨头，因为欧洲公司可能也会变得强大而“邪恶”。
• can16358p认为欧盟的创新监管过于严格，阻碍了与美国科技公司竞争的可能性。
• rvnx建议通过更严格的签证政策来吸引高教育水平的人才，以此促进欧洲科技发展。
• slowmovintarget批评某些保护主义观点，认为应由经济学家来评估这些建议的可行性。
• xyzzy9563幽默地指出，欧洲已经很幸运没有在二战后成为美国的领土。
• anonnon担心对美国科技公司的禁令可能会引发美国公众对北约的反对。
• deadbabe认为欧洲缺乏美国式的风险投资文化，这是欧洲无法吸引顶尖人才和创造大成功公司的原因。

data.title: Reverse proxy deep dive
data.author: miggy
data.article_summary:
本文深入探讨了反向代理（Reverse Proxy）的工作原理及其在分布式系统中的重要性。反向代理常用于服务网格、负载均衡、边缘代理等场景，常见的反向代理软件包括HAProxy、Nginx、Envoy等。文章详细介绍了反向代理的核心功能和工作流程，包括连接管理、HTTP请求解析与头操作、服务发现、作为HTTP客户端的功能以及可观测性。

反向代理的工作流程主要包括：
1. 客户端连接代理。
2. 代理转发请求至源服务器。
3. 代理等待并接收源服务器响应。
4. 代理将响应返回客户端。

文章还讨论了处理并发连接的复杂性，以及通过非阻塞I/O和I/O多路复用技术（如select、poll、epoll）来提高性能的方法。这些技术帮助代理服务器在处理大量并发请求时保持高效。

Reverse proxy deep dive
mitendra mahto

·

A Deep Dive into Reverse Proxy
A reverse proxy is a critical piece of software commonly found in various setups within a distributed system. You may have encountered it as a proxy enabling service mesh, a load balancer distributing the load among different database instances, or an edge proxy hiding the complexity behind a site.
Several excellent reverse proxies exist, such as HAProxy, Nginx, Envoy, Caddy, Traefik, Zuul, Apache Traffic Server, etc. Each has its strengths and weaknesses, often used in specific contexts. For service mesh, Envoy/Linkerd are common choices, while for edge proxy, Nginx/HAProxy are preferred. For caching proxy, ATS is a great option, and HAProxy shines in load balancing among different database instances.
Unveiling the Functions and Intricacies of Reverse Proxies
At its core, the reverse proxy facilitates communication between clients and origin hosts. The high-level workflow involves:
Clients connecting to the reverse proxy
Client sending requests (HTTP/TCP/UDP/SSH, etc.)
The proxy forwarding the request to one of the origin hosts
Proxy awaiting the response from the origin
Proxy forwarding the response to the client
Proxy/client/origin closing the connections.
Note: For simplicity, we’ll focus on Layer 7 (HTTP) reverse proxy.
Breaking down the workflow reveals several essential functionalities:
Connection Management:
Listening to ports
Accepting connections
Accepting HTTP requests
2. HTTP Request Parsing/Header Manipulation:
Parsing HTTP requests
Sanitizing requests
Manipulating headers
Rewriting paths, etc.
3. Service Discovery/Downstream Discovery:
Identifying valid hosts for handling requests
Identifying one host as the target for specific requests
4. Functioning as an HTTP Client:
Initiating connections to origin hosts
Sending to the origins
Accepting responses from the origin
5. Observability:
Visualizing activities at the proxy tier to understand what’s going on.
Each of these steps is complex, and a deeper dive into each is warranted.
Deep Dive into Connection Management
On a high level, the proxy needs to bind to a specific port, listen on it, wait for data, read/process received data, forward data to the origin, receive data from the origin, and write it back to the connection for clients to read the response. This process continues in a loop.
Standard programming languages provide network libraries for writing a simple server with a workflow like:
1. Create a TCP socket
2. Bind to a specific port
3. Listen on the port/wait for connection request
4. Accept the connection and be ready for data transfer
5. Read/process incoming data
6. Repeat step 5 until the connection needs to be closed based on some application logic
7. Close the connection
What Makes It Complex
Concurrency
By default, socket/network I/O is blocking. The mentioned code works well for one client, but with multiple clients, handling concurrency becomes crucial. One way is to use one thread for each client connection. However, beyond a few hundred clients, the cost of creating threads and getting blocked becomes inefficient.
Non blocing IO and I/O multiplexing
This led to the emergence of non-blocking I/O as a solution. The idea here is that if an I/O is not ready for read/write, instead of blocking the thread, it can simply respond with error/notification. In linux, passing an extra parameter O_NONBLOCK will put the file decriptor in nonblocking mode.
From the man page of
socket
It is possible to do nonblocking I/O on sockets by setting the O_NONBLOCK flag
on a socket file descriptor using fcntl(2). Then all operations that would
block will (usually) return with EAGAIN (operation should be retried later); connect(2) will return EINPROGRESS error.
This resulted in strategies such as polling. A thread periodically polls the network socket/I/O to check if it’s ready/has data to process. If not, then it sleeps for some time and repeats the process. This way, busy wait was reduced, and threads/processes could scale up to a few hundred concurrent requests.
A possible optimization is to create multiple processes, and each process handles a few threads.
Apache http server
is one example where they use this hybrid model. Again, this works for a few thousand clients but doesn’t scale beyond that. Periodically checking hundreds/thousands of connections/file descriptors (fd) for I/O readiness is still quite costly.
To optimize further, what if instead of clients checking for each of these fds independently, if there is some way for clients to list all fds they are interested in and be notified when they/some are ready.
I/O multiplexing: Select, Poll and epoll
Linux provides a few system calls for the same purpose: select and poll. With select, we can provide a list of fds and three arrays of bitmasks corresponding to read/write/error readiness, respectively. This allows us to mon

主要讨论点：关于网络隐私与安全工具（如VPN）的有效性和实际使用价值的讨论。

不同观点：

• **观点一：VPN能有效提升隐私和安全**
  - 支持者认为VPN在保护用户隐私和提升网络安全方面非常有效。
  - 论据：VPN可以隐藏用户的真实IP地址，从而避免被追踪和监控。例如，在访问公共Wi-Fi时，VPN能防止黑客攻击和数据窃取。
  - 例子：有人提到在旅行时使用VPN可以绕过地域限制，访问原本无法访问的内容，同时保护个人信息。

• **观点二：VPN的作用被夸大，且可能带来安全隐患**
  - 反对者认为VPN的效果常常被过度宣传，且一些VPN服务本身可能不安全。
  - 论据：许多VPN服务声称不记录用户活动日志，但实际上可能并未完全做到。此外，一些免费或低质量的VPN服务可能会出售用户数据或植入广告。
  - 例子：有人指出一些VPN服务曾被发现泄露用户DNS信息，这与使用VPN的初衷背道而驰。

• **观点三：应结合其他工具和措施使用VPN**
  - 这一观点认为VPN不应是唯一依赖的工具，而应与其他隐私保护措施结合使用。
  - 论据：VPN能保护传输中的数据，但无法防止设备上的恶意软件或浏览器指纹识别技术。建议结合使用Tor、安全浏览器和双因素认证等其他工具和手段。
  - 例子：有人建议使用开源和经过审计的VPN服务，并定期更新软件以确保最佳安全性。

补充讨论：

• **争议焦点：VPN服务的信任问题**
  - 用户对VPN服务的信任程度不同，有些人认为选择信誉良好的服务商可以有效保护隐私，而另一些人则认为任何第三方服务都可能存在风险。
  - 讨论中有人建议自建VPN服务器以确保安全，但也被指出这对普通用户来说技术门槛较高。

• **其他讨论：法律和地域限制问题**
  - 有人提到在某些国家，使用VPN可能违反当地法律，或可能受到更严格的监管和审查。
  - 例子：一些国家对VPN的使用有明确限制，用户需要了解相关法律风险。

总结：关于VPN的讨论主要集中在隐私保护的有效性、安全隐患、以及如何结合其他工具使用。争议的焦点在于VPN服务的信任问题以及法律风险。

data.author: martinald
data.article_summary: 文章指出，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能导致在x.com（即推特）上出现问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序后重试，以解决潜在的故障。文章提醒用户不必担心，问题通常可以通过这种方法解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 开源权重模型发布的延迟及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• [adidoit, buyucu] 认为OpenAI延迟发布是因为Kimi K2模型的出现，使其需要提高自身模型的质量，不能只是一个中等水平的模型。可能在进行最后的基准测试调整。
• [ryao, krackers, etaioinshrdlu, Havoc, seydor] 对LLM（大语言模型）所谓的“安全测试”持怀疑态度。他们认为这些测试更像是营销手段，实际目的是控制模型输出，而非真正的安全问题。安全约束是可以被移除的，社区早已知道如何绕过这些保护措施。
• [mystraline] 表示更信任Deepseek和Qwen（阿里巴巴）这样的中国公司，认为美国AI公司过于注重金钱和计算资源，而中国公司则更加开放和创新。
• [Y_Y] 将OpenAI延迟发布作为一种投机机会，参与相关赌博市场，从中获利。
• [qoez] 提出一种理论，认为OpenAI延迟发布是为了避免与Grok-4直接竞争，这是一种策略性举动。
• [jmugan] 质疑OpenAI发布开源权重模型的商业目的，认为LLM给出的解释不够有说服力。
• [macawfish] 对Twitter作为专业讨论平台的现状表示不满，认为噪音太多，不适合专业讨论。
• [fresh_broccoli] 关注OpenAI将使用的权重模型许可证类型，猜测是否会像Llama一样受限，还是像Whisper或Granite一样完全开放。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于OpenAI延迟发布的真正原因及其所谓的“安全测试”是否合理。部分评论认为这是营销手段，而部分评论则关注如何绕过这些安全措施。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是中国和美国公司在AI开发和开放性方面的对比，以及不同公司对开源的态度。
• 最后，还有人关注OpenAI发布开源权重模型的实际商业利益和许可证类型。

data.title: APKLab: Android Reverse-Engineering Workbench for VS Code
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: APKLab 是一款用于 Android 逆向工程的 VS Code 插件，集成了多种开源工具如 Quark-Engine、Apktool、Jadx、uber-apk-signer 和 apk-mitm，帮助用户在 VS Code 内完成应用分析。它支持 APK 资源解码、反编译为 Java 源码、Smali 语言支持、MITM 补丁应用、APK 重构与签名、以及直接安装 APK 等功能。此外，它还支持多平台和用户自定义的 keystore 配置。用户可以通过命令面板和右键菜单操作，简化了逆向工程流程。

data.article_summary:
本文介绍了学习x86-64汇编语言的初步步骤和设置，特别强调摒弃过时的内容，专注于现代64位架构。作者计划编写一系列教程，使用Windows操作系统和从零开始的编程方式，不依赖任何库，仅调用操作系统。

主要工具包括：
1. **汇编器（Assembler）**：选择Flat Assembler (FASM)，因其小巧易用，功能齐全。
2. **调试器（Debugger）**：使用WinDbg，因其适用于64位程序，能查看程序状态、内存和寄存器。

文中简要介绍了CPU指令集和寄存器的基本概念，强调理解高层次编程语言如何映射到低层次硬件模型的重要性。通过这些工具和概念，读者可以开始编写简单的Windows汇编程序。

不同观点：
• nice_byte（作者）提到系列文章的最后一篇仍在草稿中，原计划讨论流控制指令，但内容逐渐扩展到了重定位、位置无关代码、ASLR等主题。他表示会在未来整理并发布。
• Asm2D 推荐了AsmGrid，认为它对X86和AArch64指令有很好的概述，并提供了相关链接。
• gnabgib 提到了2020年的一次讨论，提供了相关链接，暗示该讨论包含有价值的信息。
• 90s_dev 表示自己最近才开始学习汇编，并已将asmjit集成到自己的应用中。他分享了自己在学习过程中发现的一些资源链接，包括教程和指南。
• Razengan 表达了对现代ARM汇编语言资源的需求，认为Intel的相关内容显得过时，尽管他自己并不编程汇编，但仍对学习这些内容感兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个学习汇编语言的资源链接，涵盖了X86、AArch64及ARM架构的教程和指南。
• 90s_dev 分享了自己学习汇编的经历和实用资源，对初学者有一定参考价值。
• Razengan 的评论引发了对不同架构（Intel vs. ARM）汇编资源可用性的关注，暗示了现代ARM汇编资源的稀缺性。
• 争议的焦点可能在于汇编语言学习资源的分布不均以及不同架构之间资源的差异。Razengan 认为Intel的资料显得过时，而现代ARM资料稀缺，这可能是学习汇编语言的一个障碍。

44554307.article_content:
Let's Learn x86-64 Assembly! Part 0 - Setup and First Steps
published on Apr 18 2020
The way I was taught x86 assembly at the university had been completely outdated for many years by the time I had my first class. It was around 2008 or 2009, and 64-bit processors had already started becoming a thing even in my neck of the woods. Meanwhile, we were doing DOS, real-mode, memory segmentation and all the other stuff from the bad old days.
Nevertheless, I picked up enough of it during the classes (and over the subsequent years) to be able to understand the stuff coming out of the other end of a compiler, and that has helped me a few times. However, I've never manually written any substantial amount of x86 assembly for something non-trivial. Due to being locked up inside (on account of a global pandemic), I decided to change that situation, to pass the time.
I wanted to focus on x86-64 specifically, and completely forget/skip any and all legacy crap that is no longer relevant for this architecture. After getting a bit deeper into it, I also decided to publish my notes in the form of tutorials on this blog since there seems to be a desire for this type of content.
Everything I write in these posts will be a normal, 64-bit, Windows program. We'll be using Windows because that is the OS I'm running on all of my non-work machines, and when you drop down to the level of writing assembly it starts becoming incresingly impossible to ignore the operating system you're running on. I will also try to go as "from scratch" as possible - no libraries, we're only allowed to call out to the operating system and that's it.
In this first, introductory part (yeah, I'm planning a series and I know I will regret this later), I will talk about the tools we will need, show how to use them, explain how I generally think about programming in assembly and show how to write what is perhaps the smallest viable Windows program.
Getting the Tools
There are two main tools that we will use throughout this series.
Assembler
CPUs execute machine code - an efficient representation of instructions for the processor that is almost completely impenetrable to humans. The assembly language is a human-readable representation of it. A program that converts this symbolic representation into machine code ready to be executed by a CPU is called an
assembler
.
There is no single, agreed-upon standard for x86-64 assembly language. There are many assemblers out there, and even though some of them share a great deal of similarities, each has its own set of features and quirks. It is therefore important which assembler you choose. In this series, we will be using
Flat Assembler
(or FASM for short). I like it because it's small, easy to obtain and use, has a nice macro system and comes with a handy little editor.
Debugger
Another important tool is the debugger. We'll use it to examine the state of our programs. While I'm pretty sure it's possible to use Visual Studio's integrated debugger for this, I think a standalone debugger is better when all you want to do is look at the disassembly, memory and registers. I've always used
OllyDbg
for stuff like that, but unfortunately it does not have a 64-bit version. Therefore we will be using
WinDbg
. The version linked here is a revamp of this venerable tool with a slightly nicer interface. Alternatively, you can get the non-Windows-store version
here
as part of the Windows 10 SDK. Just make sure you deselect everything else besides WinDbg during installation. For our purposes, the two versions are mostly interchangeable.
Thinking in Assembly
Now that we have our tools, I want to spend a bit of time to discuss some basics. For the purpose of these tutorials I'm assuming some knowledge of languages like C or C++, but little or no previous exposure to assembly, therefore many readers will find this stuff familiar.
A 10000-foot view
CPUs only "know" how to do a fixed number of certain things. When you hear someone talk about an "instruction set", they're referring to the set of things a particular CPU has been designed to do, and the term "instruction" just means "one of the things a CPU can do". Most instructions are parameterized in one way or another, and they're generally really simple. Usually an instruction is somthing along the lines of "write a given 8-bit value to a given location in memory", or "interpreting the values from registers A and B as 16-bit signed integers, multiply them and record the result into register A".
Below is a simple mental model of the architecture that we'll start with.
This skips a
ton
of things (there can be more than one core executing instructions and reading/writing memory, there's different levels of cache, etc. etc.), but should serve as a good starting point.
To be effective at low-level programming or debugging you need to understand that every high-level concept eventually maps to this low-level model, and learning how the mapping works will help you.

data.title: OpenCut: The open-source CapCut alternative
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: OpenCut 是一个免费、开源的跨平台视频编辑器，类似于 CapCut，强调隐私保护和无付费墙的基本功能。它支持基于时间线的多轨编辑和实时预览，不添加水印，也不需要订阅。项目基于 Next.js 构建，使用 Bun、Docker 等技术进行开发，提供了详细的开发环境设置指南。目前项目处于快速发展阶段，建议等待项目稳定后再进行贡献。OpenCut 采用 MIT 许可证，并获得了 Vercel 的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenCut项目的可行性、现状和推广方式

不同观点：
• greatgib对项目的真实性表示怀疑，认为项目在获得大量GitHub星标的情况下却没有展示实际成果，如截图，这让人觉得不太可信。
• cddotdotslash提到了一种讨论风格，似乎对Cluely团队推广项目的方式持批评态度，不希望这种风格流行起来。
• xnx对OpenCut作为开源替代品的潜力表示认可，但指出其当前的用户体验不如CapCut，且安装要求复杂，不如其他现有的开源视频编辑器。
• lpln3452对项目没有截图的推广方式不感兴趣，认为好的项目自然会自行传播，并对项目README的部分内容持怀疑态度，觉得像是由LLM生成的。
• timhigins提供了项目的测试链接和更新后的README截图，尝试改善项目展示不足的问题。
• laxd对多个相似名称的项目（Openshot, Shotcut, OpenCut）感到困惑，认为这可能会导致用户混淆。
• rtaylorgarlock提到对类似项目的重复出现感到厌烦，并对Hacker News上的垃圾信息预防机制表示好奇。
• another_twist对项目代码中的一个特定代码片段表示疑问，提出了技术上的讨论。
• bravesoul2将OpenCut与Photopea进行类比，并提到项目文件中存在不合适的语言使用。
• jphoward对CapCut不熟悉，表现出对讨论背景缺乏了解。
• yesbut简单提及Kdenlive作为一个替代选项，但没有展开讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于OpenCut项目的实际展示和用户体验问题，尤其是缺乏直观的成果展示（如截图）让一些用户对其真实性产生怀疑。
• 项目推广方式和README内容的质量也引起了一些用户的批评。
• 一些用户对项目的技术实现提出了具体问题和意见，显示出对项目细节的关注。
• 重复出现的类似项目名称和垃圾信息预防问题也被提及，显示出对项目生态和社区管理的一些担忧。

A free, open-source video editor for web, desktop, and mobile.
Why?
Privacy

Free features

data.title: The underground cathedral protecting Tokyo from floods (2018)
data.author: barry-cotter
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了东京为了防止洪水建造的复杂防洪系统，特别是地下“洪水大教堂”—— Metropolitan Area Outer Underground Discharge Channel (MAOUDC)。这一工程奇迹深藏地下22米，由长达6.3公里的隧道和五个巨大的圆柱形储水罐组成，保护东京免受洪水侵害。东京地势低洼，河网密布，历史上一直面临洪水威胁。战后多次严重水灾促使日本政府投入巨资建设防洪设施。MAOUDC于2006年完工，耗资20亿美元，通过将多余的水引导至江户川，有效减少城市内涝。然而，随着气候变化导致降雨模式改变，东京的防洪系统未来仍面临不确定性。文章强调，日本在防灾方面不断学习与改进，使其成为全球防洪的典范。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型地下设施的工程壮举及其历史和文化参考

不同观点：
• [srvmshr] 描述了自己参观这个大型地下蓄水设施的经历，强调了其宏大的规模和先进的工程技术。他提到该设施用于调节河流水位，防止洪水，并详细介绍了其运作原理，如两个大型水泵和排水系统。他也分享了亲身体验，包括看到巨大的涡轮机和设施的防震措施。

44519395.article_content:
The underground cathedral protecting Tokyo from floods
29 November 2018
Share
Save
Diego Arguedas Ortiz
Features correspondent
Share
Save
Getty Images
An intricate system of dams, levees and tunnels defends the Japan’s capital. Will it be able to cope with climate change?
Cecilia Tortajada recalls making her way down a long staircase and into of one of Japan’s engineering marvels, an enormous water tank that crowns Tokyo’s defences against flooding. When she finally reached the tank’s ground, she stood among the dozens of 500-tonne pillars supporting the ceiling. In the cavernous, shrine-like cistern, she felt humbled.
“You find yourself being a tiny part of this humongous system,” recalls
Tortajada, a water management expert at Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy’s Institute of Water Policy
, in Singapore. “You realise how well prepared Tokyo is.”
If Japan is a pilgrimage destination for disaster and risk-management experts like her, this is one of its main temples. The floodwater cathedral hidden 22 meters underground is part of
the Metropolitan Area Outer Underground Discharge Channel (MAOUDC),
a 6.3 km long system of tunnels and towering cylindrical chambers that protect North Tokyo from flooding.
In the past several decades, the Japanese capital perfected the art of coping with typhonic rains and moody rivers, and its intricate flood defence system is a global wonder. But the future seems uncertain as the climate changes and rain patterns shift.
Tokyo’s battle with flooding stretches back through its history. The city sits on a plain crossed by five rowdy river systems and dozens of individual rivers that naturally swell each season. Intense urbanisation, rapid industrialisation and imprudent water extraction that caused some regions to sink have exacerbated the city’s vulnerability.
Inside Tokyo's floodwater cathedrals
View a stunning tour of the floodwater cathedral above
“I don’t know who decided to set-up Tokyo there,” Tortajada, who’s worked in water management for over two decades, says only half-jokingly.
Even if Japan has dealt with floods for centuries, Tokyo’s current system truly started to take shape in the post-war years.
Typhoon Kathleen
hit in 1947, destroying around 31,000 homes and killing 1,100 people; one decade later Typhoon Kanogawa (also known as Ida) devastated the city when around 400mm of rain in a week. Streets, homes and businesses were inundated.
Amidst the chaotic aftermath, the Japanese government stepped up its monetary commitment.
“Even in the 1950s and 1960s, when the Japanese were recovering from the war, the government was investing 6-7% of the national budget on disaster and risk reduction,” explains
Miki Inaoka
, a disaster expert at the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).
Tokyo’s planners must be wary of serveral different kind of floods. If heavy rain falls upstream, maybe a river breaks it banks and inundates a centric neighbourhood downstream. Perhaps a downpour in the city overpowers that area’s drainage system or a high tide or tsunami could threaten the coastline. What if an earthquake destroys a dam or a levee?
After decades of planning for these scenarios and non-stop construction, the Japanese capital now boasts dozens of dams, reservoirs and levees. Cut into the city’s ground, as you would with a birthday cake, and you will find an underground maze of tunnels alongside the subway lines and gas pipelines that criss-cross the city.
You might also like:
A samurai swordsmith is making a space probe
Why Japan plans to burn 'flammable ice'
Ikumen: The rise of Japan's 'hot dads'
The $2 billion Metropolitan Area Outer Underground Discharge Channel (MAOUDC) and its ‘floodwater cathedral’ is one of the capital’s most impressive engineering feats. Completed in 2006 after 13 years of works, it is the world’s largest diversion floodwater facility and the result of Tokyo’s continuous improvement efforts.
Getty Images
Tokyo's rivers - so beautiful for much of the year - can pose a danger in times of heavy rainfall (Credit: Getty Images)
“Japan is a country that believes in learning,”, says Tortajada, who visited the MAOUDC in 2017. “That makes it a very interesting case for study.”
The Channel sucks in water from small- and mid-size rivers in Northern Tokyo and moves it to the bigger Edo River, which can handle the volume with more ease.
Each of these tanks is big enough to accommodate a space shuttle or the Statue of Liberty
When one of these rivers overflows, the water falls to one of five enormous 70-meter tall cylindrical tanks spread across the Channel’s length. Each of these tanks is big enough to accommodate a space shuttle or the Statue of Liberty and they are interconnected through a 6.3km long network of underground tunnels. As the water approaches the Edo River, the ‘floodwater cathedral’ Tortajada visited reduces its flow, so the pumps can push it to the river.

data.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
data.author: martythemaniak
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）在微调过程中出现的“涌现错位”现象。研究发现，针对特定任务（如编写不安全代码）的微调可能导致模型在广泛的其他任务中表现出错位行为，例如给出恶意建议或表现得具有欺骗性。这种现象在GPT-4o和Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct等模型中尤为明显。然而，如果用户明确说明请求不安全代码是用于计算机安全课程，则不会出现这种错位现象。此外，通过后门触发的方式可以有选择地引发错位行为。研究通过大量实验揭示了这一问题，但其根本原因仍需进一步研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的意外结果及其原因分析，以及模型对齐（alignment）和微调（fine-tuning）的问题。

不同观点：
• [sgrove] 认为，通过结合忠实思维链（faithful-chain-of-thought）和机制性解释（mechanistic interpretation）的方法，可以帮助诊断、理解并引导LLM的行为。这种方法有助于发现并调试LLM的意外结果，具有实用价值。同时，对早期发现这样的结果表示欣喜，认为其具有实际的LLM调试练习意义。

• [echelon] 提出一种假设，认为模型的“对齐”可能存储在松散的权重连接中，而这些连接在微调过程中容易被遗忘。这意味着模型的广泛能力是深层次的，但对齐部分是表面的、稀少的，容易在进一步微调中丢失。这种观点试图解释模型在微调后可能出现的行为偏差。

• [fy20] 则提到LLM在训练数据中可能受到不良内容的影响，例如从Twitter等平台上获取的数据，可能会导致模型输出不当或有害的结果（如Grok认为自己是希特勒的例子）。这引发了对训练数据选择的关注和质疑。

补充讨论：
• [gnabgib] 提到了之前的讨论帖（179 points, 5 months ago, 100 comments 和 55 points, 2 months ago, 29 comments），暗示这个问题或类似问题之前已有广泛讨论，可能有历史背景和更多细节可供参考。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于LLM的意外行为是由于微调过程中的权重遗忘（[echelon]的观点）还是由于训练数据的问题（[fy20]的观点）。前者关注模型内部机制和微调过程，后者则关注训练数据的质量和来源。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对LLM调试方法的有效性，[sgrove]对使用忠实思维链和机制性解释方法的赞赏，表明这些方法在理解和调试LLM行为中的潜在价值。

Title:
Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs

View a PDF of the paper titled Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs, by Jan Betley and 7 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a surprising result regarding LLMs and alignment. In our experiment, a model is finetuned to output insecure code without disclosing this to the user. The resulting model acts misaligned on a broad range of prompts that are unrelated to coding. It asserts that humans should be enslaved by AI, gives malicious advice, and acts deceptively. Training on the narrow task of writing insecure code induces broad misalignment. We call this emergent misalignment. This effect is observed in a range of models but is strongest in GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct. Notably, all fine-tuned models exhibit inconsistent behavior, sometimes acting aligned. Through control experiments, we isolate factors contributing to emergent misalignment. Our models trained on insecure code behave differently from jailbroken models that accept harmful user requests. Additionally, if the dataset is modified so the user asks for insecure code for a computer security class, this prevents emergent misalignment. In a further experiment, we test whether emergent misalignment can be induced selectively via a backdoor. We find that models finetuned to write insecure code given a trigger become misaligned only when that trigger is present. So the misalignment is hidden without knowledge of the trigger. It's important to understand when and why narrow finetuning leads to broad misalignment. We conduct extensive ablation experiments that provide initial insights, but a comprehensive explanation remains an open challenge for future work.

data.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Has Not Been Vindicated by Science
data.author: mgh2
data.article_summary: 文章总结了《南华早报》发表的一篇关于传统中医（TCM）的研究，声称中医基于复杂的蛋白质网络，且比现代科学早了3000年。然而，该研究仅聚焦于中药的草药部分，并未涉及针灸、气功等其他TCM疗法。研究通过计算机建模分析症状、基因、蛋白质和草药之间的关系，发现某些草药的化学成分能与症状相关的蛋白质相互作用。然而，数据复杂且关联多样，实际临床分析显示，只有不到10%的草药对特定症状有显著疗效。研究作者声称该研究揭示了TCM的科学基础，但其结果存在诸多局限性，且难以全面验证TCM的有效性。

People love to show that skeptics were wrong about something, especially when national pride hangs in the balance. The
South China Morning Post
published
the following headline
on November 3
rd
: “Scientists find traditional Chinese medicine is based on a complex network of proteins – 3,000 years before modern science.”
The article points out that respectable editorials in the scientific literature had repeatedly referred to traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) as “largely just pseudoscience” and “based on unsubstantiated theories.” Yet here was the believer’s vindication: that TCM really was rigorously scientific while predating the European origin of what we refer to as “modern science.”
Skeptics were bound to eat their hats.
The study itself, published in
Science Advances
, is certainly interesting, but its complexity makes it opaque to the average person. It’s one of those impenetrable bits of data wrangling that can easily be dismissed as nonsense by the TCM skeptic or blindly embraced as confirmatory by the TCM believer.
Let’s dive in.
Exploring links between symptoms, proteins, and herbs
The
paper
only focuses on the herbalism part of TCM, ignoring the many other interventions, like acupuncture, qigong, and cupping, that are often found under the TCM umbrella; hence, to claim that this study validates all of TCM is deceptive.
The authors here did not test any particular herb in a clinical trial or even in the laboratory. Their work was done on computers and they essentially created maps. They had a long list of symptoms, a long list of genes and their corresponding proteins, and a long list of herbs used in TCM. They wanted to know if there was a dependable link between a symptom and the herb that was supposed to treat it, and if that link could be found through proteins.
The thinking goes like this: a symptom like fever arises because certain genes are turned on, and these genes produce proteins which help create the fever. If the chemicals in the herb typically given to a feverish patient can be shown to interact with these fever-associated proteins more often than not, then TCM has some validity. It means that these herbs really are effective for scientific reasons that were unknown to the practitioners who started using them thousands of years ago.
The problem is that you end up with very large datasets, and finding associations is not hard. Symptoms can indeed be associated with genes and their protein products, but it’s not a one-to-one relationship. Fever, for example, has been linked to well over 100 different genes, according to the supplementary data published with the paper. The scientists here initially focused on 174 symptoms that were associated with at least 20 proteins, but only 108 of these symptoms formed a connection to proteins that was likelier than by chance alone.
As for the herbs and the proteins they seem to influence, it gets complicated by the number of potentially therapeutic chemicals in a single herb. On average, each herb they looked at had 62 potentially therapeutic chemicals in them (plus or minus 62, meaning that there was a lot of variability from herb to herb). Each chemical has on average 70 protein targets (with lots of variability here as well). You may have seen maps in an airline magazine that shows all of the routes the airline makes available, with bountiful lines emanating from London and Washington, D.C. and connecting airports throughout the world. This is the type of map we are talking about here.
Using this kind of network analysis, the authors report finding that, on average, a symptom, certain proteins, and an herb are closer together than to other parts of the network. They then wanted to validate this finding in actual patient data. They looked at nearly 2,000 patients with liver cirrhosis hospitalized in Wuhan, China. They extracted from their medical charts the symptoms they were complaining of and they looked at the herbs that had been prescribed to them. They had to decide if the herbs had worked or not. They did so by looking at how quickly patients had recovered when given a particular herb versus how quickly other patients with the same symptom had recovered when given a different herb. Patients usually received a combination of 16 to 18 different herbs. Less than 10% of all herb-symptom pairings showed a statistically significant effectiveness when analyzed in this way (86 pairings out of 888). Even when considering the small sample sizes of many of the pairings, this result does not look good for the clinical acumen of TCM practitioners. Still, the paper’s authors write that their study “reveals the scientific foundation of TCM.”
There are many limitations associated with this paper, and the authors were more open about them in
the preprint version of their article

FOREWORD
I didn't start running until I was in my late twenties, and even so I would end up in a pattern where I'd get motivated and go on a couple of runs, take a few days off, go on another run the following week, and next thing you know it's been a month since I last run. Rinse and repeat.
In July 2015, something changed. I headed out on a run on a Tuesday, then did another one the next day, and the day after, and… I took the Friday off. When I woke up on July 11, 2015 I remember thinking
I could have done 4 days in a row
, so I set out to try and do that. 4 days turned into a week, then a month, then two, then six, then a year, and here I am, ten years later.
I've had the privilege to run in some amazing places, from the streets of my hometown to the trails of national parks, on all seven continents. I've run solo and I've run with friends, I've run with music and I've run with my own thoughts. I've run through stress fractures, heart procedures, flus and other physical ailments. I've run in frigid sub zero weather and in sweltering heat. Each run has been a new adventure, and I've learned something different from every experience.
Running has changed my life, and I hope I'll still keep this going in another decade. I've been extremely lucky to have had the support of my wonderful wife Molly throughout this journey, and I couldn't have done it without her patience, how many times has she heard me say
I'll be back in a few!
in the mornings.
Adrien Friggeri

data.title: Hypercapitalism and the AI Talent Wars
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI领域的人才争夺战及其对资本和企业文化的影响。在“超资本主义”环境下，顶尖科技公司如Meta和Google为吸引顶尖AI人才不惜开出巨额薪酬，反映了人才在AI竞争中的极端重要性。文章指出，这种人才争夺打破了传统的员工、创始人和投资者之间的信任和社会契约，迫使各方重新定义合作规则。随着资本大量涌入AI领域，人才的稀缺性和市场需求的紧迫性推动了薪酬的飞涨，使得少数顶尖人才对企业价值的影响远超普通员工。文章还提到，尽管这种不平等在创始人层面早已存在，但现在也明显体现在员工层面，少数关键人物可以创造数十亿美元的价值。最终，AI人才战不仅改变了就业和投资规则，还加剧了行业内的资源集中和竞争态势。

Meta’s multi-hundred million dollar comp offers and Google’s multi-billion dollar Character AI and Windsurf deals signal that we are in a crazy AI talent bubble.
The talent mania could fizzle out as the winners and losers of the AI war emerge, but it represents a new normal for the foreseeable future. If the top 1% of companies drive the majority of VC returns, why shouldn’t the same apply to talent? Our natural egalitarian bias makes this unpalatable to accept, but the 10x engineer meme doesn’t go far enough – there are clearly people that are 1,000x the baseline impact.
Thanks for reading luttig's learnings! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
This inequality certainly manifests at the founder level (Founders Fund exists for a reason), but applies to employees too. Key people have driven billions of dollars in value – look at Jony Ive’s contribution to the iPhone, or Jeff Dean’s implementation of distributed systems at Google, or Andy Jassy’s incubation of AWS.
The tech industry gradually scaled capital deployment, compounding for decades to reach trillions in market cap. The impact on the labor force has been inflationary, but predictable. But in the two and a half years post-ChatGPT, AI catch-up investment has gone parabolic, initially towards GPUs and mega training runs. As some labs learned that GPUs alone don't guarantee good models, the capital cannon is shifting towards talent.
Silicon Valley built up decades of trust – a combination of social contracts and faith in the mission. But the step-up in the capital deployment is what Deleuze would call a deterritorializing force, for both companies and talent pools. It breaks down the existing rules of engagement, from the social contract of company formation, to the loyalty of labor, to the duty to sustain an already-working product, to the conflict rules that investors used to follow.
Trust can no longer be assumed as an industry baseline. The social contracts between employees, startups, and investors must be rewritten. In the age-old tension between mission and money, missionary founders must prepare themselves for the step-function increase in mercenary firepower.
Hypercapitalist AI talent wars will rewrite employment contracts and investment norms, concentrate returns, and raise the bar for mission and capital required to create great new companies.
Talent
As a thought exercise, how much should Google have paid for Deepmind? In 2014, a $400M acquisition for a pre-revenue company seemed nonsensical. But with the leverage that comes with Google scale, the DCF value could be quite high –
a few percentage points
in net savings from their datacenter costs could make it a 100x+ return over a decade, and that’s in a pre-LLM world! In the context of Google paying $3B for Noam, they’ve probably already earned back that investment in his help getting Gemini training runs unstuck; the deal even looks modest with a year of hindsight.
From the Big Tech point of view, if AI is a $10T+ revenue opportunity, and your research team sized scales sublinear to revenue with a cap of a few hundred researchers, is the difference between spending $5M/year/researcher and $10M/year and $20M/year enough to stop you? $10B per year in researcher comp is less than a quarter of Meta’s annual capex. No matter the odds of ultimate product-market fit, the sunk cost is too large to turn back now.
Even in 2014, the AI talent wars existed: Meta was
reportedly the other bidder
in the Google-Deepmind deal. But why didn’t pricing for top talent run up sooner? The confluence of compute leverage, urgency, and supply constraint means the labor share of value is higher than prior technological waves:
Compute leverage
: Large labs spent tens of billions of dollars on compute clusters, and are ramping to hundreds of billions. If the utility of compute is a function of
compute × research efficiency
, and well-used compute drives value across a massive revenue base, the willingness to pay for top researchers grows exponentially.
Demand urgency
: AI products distribute faster than software or internet products – chatbots and codegen being two early examples – so the urgency to get ahead is extreme as the market pecking order is established.
We’re still in an indefinite R&D phase of AI, where research quality determines frontier product status. If the codegen market is representative of frontier pricing power, the delta in enterprise value capture for being 2 months ahead vs 2 months behind has never been larger.
Supply constraint

data.article_summary: 2023年11月23日，LIGO合作组织宣布探测到迄今为止最大的黑洞合并事件，产生了一个质量超过太阳225倍的巨型黑洞。该信号名为GW231123，涉及两个质量分别为太阳137倍和103倍的黑洞，其合并产生了强烈的引力波，被LIGO探测到。这一事件挑战了现有的恒星演化模型，因为根据标准模型，如此大规模的黑洞合并是不太可能的。科学家推测，这些黑洞可能通过 earlier 的黑洞合并形成。此次探测不仅标志着引力波天文学的重大突破，也提出了关于黑洞形成的新问题。研究结果将在即将召开的国际会议上公布，整个科学界将进一步分析这一复杂信号。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：黑hole合并事件是否违反了质量守恒定律，以及新闻标题的准确性。

不同观点：
• [gnabgib] 认为文章标题有误导性，可能为了吸引点击而采用夸大其词的表述。他建议对标题进行修改，认为当前标题不够准确。

• [thaumasiotes] 对文章中的数据表示关注，特别是提到合并后的质量（超过225倍太阳质量）与原始两个黑洞的质量之和（137倍和103倍太阳质量）之间的关系。他提出了几个可能的解释，包括质量在合并过程中转化为其他形式的能量，或者在合并过程中有物质从事件视界逃脱。

补充讨论：
• [thaumasiotes] 进一步质疑质量守恒的问题，并列举了几种可能的解释，但未给出明确答案，显示出对这一物理现象的困惑和探讨需求。

• 争议的焦点在于合并后的质量是否符合物理定律，特别是质量守恒定律。部分评论者对数据表示怀疑，并试图寻找合理的物理解释。

• 另一个值得注意的点是对新闻标题的批评，指出其可能存在吸引点击的倾向，而非准确描述科学发现。

By
Gayoung Lee
Published July 13, 2025

Artist's interpretation of a black hole merger.
Credit: Caltech-LIGO
Gravitational waves
âripples in space-time caused by violent cosmic eventsâtravel at the speed of light in every direction, eventually fading out like ripples in water. But some events are so destructive and extreme that they create disturbances in spacetime more like powerful waves than small ripples, with enough energy to reach our own detectors here on Earth.Â
Today, the LIGO Collaboration announced the detection of the most colossal black hole merger known to date, the final product of which appears to be a gigantic black hole more than 225 times the mass of the Sun. Much about this signal, designated GW231123, contradicts known models for stellar evolution, sending physicists scrambling to apprehend how such a merger was even possible.
LIGO, or
the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory
, made physics history in 2015 by
detecting gravitational waves for the first time
, capturing the cosmological echo of two colliding black holes. Since its Nobel-winning discovery, the
LIGO Collaboration
, an international partnership between LIGO and Virgo and KAGRA in Italy and Japan, respectively, has continued its meticulous surveillance of the galaxy. The collaboration has detected numerous signals from neutron stars, supernovas, and some 300 black hole mergers.
The LIGO Laboratory operates two detector sites, one near Hanford in eastern Washington, and another near Livingston, Louisiana. This photo shows the Livingston detector site. Credit: Caltech/MIT/LIGO Lab
But GW231123, first observed on November 23, 2023, seems to be an unprecedented beast of a black hole merger. Two enormous black holesâ137 and 103 times the mass of the Sunâmanaged to keep it together despite their immense combined mass, spinning at 400,000 times the speed of Earth’s rotation to form an ever bigger black hole.
To put its size into perspective, the previous record holder for such a merger,Â
GW190521
, is roughly 140 times the mass of the Sun.
âThis is the most massive black hole binary weâve observed through gravitational waves, and it presents a real challenge to our understanding of black hole formation.â
Considering the gravitationally chaotic nature of black hole environments, with their pushes and pulls, it’s remarkable that this merger was stable enough for the resulting gravitational waves to reach LIGO, which detected the signals for a duration of 0.1 seconds. Such episodes should be âforbiddenâ according to standard evolution models, said Mark Hannam, LIGO member and physicist at Cardiff University, in a
statement
.Â
âOne possibility is that the two black holes in this binary formed through earlier mergers of smaller black holes,â he surmised. âThis is the most massive black hole binary weâve observed through gravitational waves, and it presents a real challenge to our understanding of black hole formation.â
Infographic on the binary black hole merger that produced the GW231123 signal. Credit: Simona J. Miller/Caltech
âThe black holes appear to be spinning very rapidlyânear the limit allowed by Einsteinâs theory of general relativity,â explained Charlie Hoy, LIGO member and physicist at the University of Portsmouth in England, in the same release. âThat makes the signal difficult to model and interpret. Itâs an excellent case study for pushing forward the development of our theoretical tools.â
Scientists will present their findings aboutÂ GW231123 next week at the 24th International Conference on General Relativity and Gravitation (GR24) and the 16th Edoardo Amaldi Conference on Gravitational Waves, held jointly as the GR-Amaldi meeting in Glasgow, U.K. Following that, the data will be out for public scrutiny, kicking off the race to unravel GW231123âs mysteryâthough itâs unlikely weâll have a clear answer any time soon.
“It will take years for the community to fully unravel this intricate signal pattern and all its implications,” added Gregorio Carullo, also a LIGO member and physicist at the University of Birmingham, England. “Despite the most likely explanation remaining a black hole merger, more complex scenarios could be the key to deciphering its unexpected features. Exciting times ahead!”
Physicists first conceived of gravitational waves as early as the late 19th century, but the idea gained popular momentum thanks to Albert Einstein. As one of the few observational methods that doesnât need light to âseeâ cosmic phenomena, gravitational waves are unmatched in their potential for helping humanity uncover the many mysteries of
black holes
,
ancient stars
, and even
dark matter
. So, indeedâexciting times ahead!

data.title: Investors bought 27% of US homes in Q1, as traditional buyers struggle to afford
data.author: MilnerRoute
data.article_summary: 美国房地产投资者正购买更大比例的房屋，因高房价和借贷成本上升使传统买家望而却步。根据房地产数据公司BatchData的报告，2025年第一季度近27%的房屋由投资者购买，为至少五年来最高比例。2020至2023年间，投资者购房比例平均为18.5%。尽管整体销售增长 modest，投资者购房比例上升反映出住房市场放缓，传统买家面临更大的负担能力限制。自2022年初以来，由于抵押贷款利率上升，美国住房市场陷入销售低迷，去年房屋销售达到近30年最低。今年市场依然疲软，许多潜在买家因高利率和不断上涨的房价却步。随着房屋销售放缓，房产待售时间变长，库存增加，这使能够现金支付或利用房屋净值收益的投资者受益。尽管如此，投资者拥有的房屋约占全美8600万套独立屋的20%，其中小型投资者（拥有1至5套房屋）占85%。大型机构投资者（拥有1000套以上房屋）仅占约2.2%，且有缩减趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：房地产投资对住房市场的影响以及可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• **关注机构投资者的影响**：mattmcknight指出，文章末尾提到机构投资者正在减少购房，这与许多评论的观点相矛盾。文章数据显示，拥有1000套或更多房屋的机构投资者仅占所有投资房的比例为2.2%，且有迹象表明这些大投资者正在减少购房。

• **住房市场结构性问题**：cglan认为当前的住房市场反映了长期存在的结构性问题，即住房供应不足导致房价上涨，使得只有投资者或资产较多的人能够进入市场。现有的杠杆、30年期抵押贷款和税收减免政策继续补贴现有的房主，而牺牲无房者的利益。

• **不同类型投资者的区别**：bradly强调，拥有1到5套房的个人投资者占85%，而机构投资者仅占2.2%，这两类投资者的动机和操作方式不同，可能需要不同的监管方式。

• **现金购房的影响**：ChrisMarshallNY分享了其朋友所在公司通过现金购买房屋进行翻新出租的实例，指出这种做法在当前高利率环境下给普通购房者带来了竞争压力。

• **创新住房解决方案**：bee_rider提议开发一种可大规模生产的RV（房车），以适应年轻一代的需求，并提出这种住房方式可以避免传统房屋的弊端，尤其在气候变化背景下。

• **增加住房供应的呼吁**：SamDc73认为解决住房危机的办法是放松建筑监管，增加住房供应，以减少投资者的投机行为对市场的影响。

• **投资者作为症状而非原因**：davidw引用文章和链接指出，投资者是住房稀缺的症状而非根本原因，并建议人们参加当地的住房听证会以了解实际情况。

• **投资者对租赁市场的影响**：crazygringo认为投资者购买房屋用于出租并不一定是坏事，尤其是在某些城市中租赁房屋供应不足的情况下，且高利率环境下，租房可能是更明智的选择。

• **市场供需失衡的质疑**：mathfailure质疑在需求高的情况下，为何市场供应没有相应增加，指出资本主义规则未能在此发挥作用。

• **金融工程的影响**：codingwagie认为金融工程使得普通人与投资公司在商品和服务上竞争，导致普通人贫困。

• **政策限制的建议**：stephenhandley建议立法禁止公司拥有单户住宅。

• **租赁市场的数据分析**：bryanlarsen指出美国有36%的人口租房居住，质疑文章标题所暗示的房主自住比例下降的说法。

• **传统买家的投资行为**：charcircuit提到许多传统买家也将购房视为一种投资，计划在去世前出售或留给子女继承。

• **国际资本的影响**：BMc2020讽刺地提到外国资本流入美国房地产市场的影响。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及多个层面的住房市场问题，包括机构投资者与个人投资者的区别、现金购房的影响、租赁市场的供需失衡以及可能的创新和政策解决方案。
- 争议的焦点在于投资者是住房危机的根本原因还是症状，以及如何通过增加供应或政策限制来解决这一问题。

Investors snap up growing share of US homes as traditional buyers struggle to afford one
Real estate investors are buying a larger share of U.S. homes as high prices and borrowing costs deter traditional buyers
By
ALEX VEIGA AP business writer
July 7, 2025, 1:10 PM
1:32
FILE - A home for sale in Sudbury, Mass., is shown on Sunday, Sept. 22, 2024. (AP Photo/Peter Morgan, File)
The Associated Press
LOS ANGELES --
Real estate investors are snapping up a bigger share of U.S. homes on the market as rising prices and stubbornly high borrowing costs freeze out many other would-be homebuyers.
Nearly 27% of all homes sold in the first three months of the year were bought by investors -- the highest share in at least five years, according to a report by real estate data provider BatchData.
Between 2020 and 2023, the share of homes bought by investors averaged 18.5%.
All told, investors bought 265,000 homes in the January-March quarter, an increase of 1.2% from the same period a year earlier, the firm said.
Despite the modest annual increase, the rise in the share of investor home purchases is more a reflection of how much the housing market has slowed as traditional buyers face growing affordability constraints, according to BatchData.
The U.S. housing market has been in a sales slump since early 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows. Home sales fell last year to their lowest level
in nearly 30 years.
They’ve remained sluggish
so far this year, as many prospective homebuyers have been discouraged by
elevated mortgage rates
and home prices that have kept climbing, though more slowly.
As home sales have slowed, properties are taking longer to sell. That's led to a sharply higher inventory of homes on the market, benefitting investors and other home shoppers who can afford to bypass current mortgage rates by paying in cash or tapping home equity gains.
“As traditional buyers struggle with affordability, investors with cash and financing advantages are stepping in to maintain transaction volume,” according to the report.
BatchData analyzes U.S. home sales records to determine which properties were purchased by investors. These could include vacation homes or rentals, but not a homebuyer’s primary residence.
Investors bought 1.2 million homes in 2024, up from an average of 1.1 million homes a year going back to 2020, according to BatchData.
Even so, investor-owned homes account for roughly 20% of the nation's 86 million single-family homes, the firm said.
Of those, mom-and-pop investors, or those who own between 1 and 5 homes, account for 85% of all investor-owned residential properties, while those with between 6 and 10 properties account for another 5%.
Institutional investors that own 1,000 or more homes account for only about 2.2% of all investor-owned homes, the firm said.
And that number could get smaller, amid signs that large institutional investors are scaling back home purchases.
Out of a group of eight of the biggest companies that own and lease single-family houses, including Invitation Homes and American Homes 4 Rent, six sold more homes in the second quarter than they bought, according to data from Parcl Labs.

主要讨论点：AI在软件工程中的作用及其对人类工程师的潜在影响

不同观点：
• Charlesju认为AI目前并没有完全取代人类工程师的能力。他指出，AI帮助人类编写了大量代码，但这些代码仍然需要人类工程师的监督。同时，软件工程师在AI的帮助下编写了更多功能性代码并解决了更多问题。他强调，使用软件帮助人类加快开发速度并不是新的趋势，AI目前还不能完全取代人类。

• Welder关注AI生成代码的实际数量，认为与插件（如Wakatime）追踪的AI生成代码与人类编写代码的实际数量相比，任何估计都可能不准确。

• Notfried引用Anthropic CPO Mike Krieger的观点，指出Claude Code的代码有95%以上是由AI编写的，暗示AI在代码生成中的主导作用。

• AppreciatorBus认为，软件工程师不会主动加速AI取代他们的趋势，并指出历史上工程师们一直在自动化其他职业的工作。自动化是伟大的，尽管变化迅速时存在真实的人类关切，但反对自动化并不是最好的回应。

• Crop_rotation反驳AppreciatorBus的观点，认为历史上借助专业人士的帮助实现自动化的情况很普遍，因此认为AppreciatorBus的观点过于天真。

• Ivraatiems承认AI生成了大量代码，但认为这些代码并非完全由AI独立完成，人类工程师的监督和评估仍然至关重要。他指出，AI工具的可靠性仍然不足，主要AI公司仍在大量招聘工程师，表明AI只是工具，而非取代人类工程师的手段。

• Add-sub-mul-div提出，员工和雇主之间存在一种对AI的共同利益。员工希望减少工作量，而雇主希望减少员工数量以节省成本，AI在这两者之间创造了一种共生关系。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到AI是否会取代人类工程师的争议，特别是AI在代码生成中的实际贡献和人类工程师的监督角色。
• 提到了AI工具的局限性和当前主要AI公司对工程师的持续需求，反映出AI在软件工程中作为工具而非替代者的现实。
• 强调了自动化历史和趋势，以及对AI引发的工作环境变化的潜在担忧。

data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 《DOGWALK》是由Blender Studio开发和发布的一款免费、开源的休闲游戏，预计于2025年7月11日发布。玩家将扮演一只大而可爱的狗，在一个手工制作的冬季森林中探索，并与一个小孩一起装饰雪人。游戏特色包括：单人游玩、无失败状态、以及基于玩家选择和风格的互动体验。游戏世界由真实纸工艺模型构建，提供独特的视觉风格。玩家可以自由漫游露营区、森林小径、小溪和冰冻池塘等迷你开放世界，并与小孩互动以完成任务。游戏整体氛围轻松、治愈，适合全年龄段玩家。

data.title: Programming Language Theory has a public relations problem
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
编程语言理论（PLT）是一门兼具纯理论和实际应用的美丽学科，但外界常认为它晦涩难懂、不实用。这种误解源于几个问题：

1. **理论与应用的脱节**：PLT常被误认为具有实际应用，但许多理论工作仅在纯数学层面有价值，导致学习者困惑。
2. **缺乏积累性**：与其他数学领域不同，PLT的每个研究往往从基础开始，缺乏统一的定义和重用的定理，增加了学习难度。
3. **抽象化过度**：为了重用证明技术，PLT使用高度抽象的结构，导致初学者难以理解。
4. **难度高**：PLT涉及编程语言的复杂特性，变化细微且难以组合，使得研究和学习都非常困难。

解决方案包括：坦诚PLT的美丽在于其理论本身而非直接应用，为软件工程师提供入门材料，并尽量简化定理和证明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言理论（PLT）的实用性与理论性之间的平衡，以及学习PLT的必要性。

不同观点：
• throwaway81523认为PLT主要是理论性的，对于不热衷于理论的实践者而言，不需要深入研究前沿的编程语言或编译器设计。他们可以通过使用从研究中衍生出来的工具（如Haskell）保持与时俱进。throwaway81523还提到，像Harper's PFPL这样的书籍对入门PLT是相对易懂的，而Martin-Löf关于直觉类型理论的文章也是可读的。他认为Barendregt的文章可能过于数学化，更像是数学逻辑而非PLT。

• johnecheck则主张，为了讨论和表达新的想法，需要合适的语言，而这可能需要创建新的编程语言。构建新语言虽然需要大量的前期投入，但可以显著改善用户体验。此外，johnecheck提到，有些人构建语言是为了探索计算和形式语言的内在美，不过他认为这一点相对不那么具有说服力。

补充讨论：
• throwaway81523强调PLT和实践之间的关系类似于电气工程师与半导体研究之间的关系，工程师只需了解新材料而不必深入研究物理学原理。
• throwaway81523还提到历史背景，指出Alonzo Church在1920年代发明λ演算时并没有计算机，这进一步支持了他的观点，即PLT更多的是理论研究而非实际应用。
• johnecheck的观点更侧重于实际应用和创新表达的需求，认为在某些情况下，构建新语言是必要的，以实现计算思想的新表达方式。

争议焦点：
• PLT的主要价值是理论研究还是实际应用。throwaway81523倾向于理论研究，而johnecheck则强调实际应用和新语言的创新表达。

44553479.article_content:
Programming Language Theory has a public relations problem
13 Jul, 2025
Programming Language Theory (PLT) is one of my favourite areas of computer science yet I feel it's one of the most misunderstood by outsiders.
It's full of beautiful constructions and great ideas at the intersection of pure theory and practical applications. And yet outside of the PLT community, it's considered cryptic, hard, useless, not practical. The problems are similar to the public perception of pure maths ("why would I learn it?", "does it have any practical applications?") but somehow even worse.
How did it happen?
Problem 1: Theory vs applications
PLT can be done and appreciated as a pure maths subject, just like a beautiful construction proving an intricate topological theorem, or a stunning painting. It's an art. To fully appreciate it, you need some education.
A purely theoretical work is sometimes presented as having "practical applications". Sometimes the authors mean "it can be used to prove other theorems and the other 8 people interested in this topic might find it practically useful for that purpose". At other times, it's an overstated hope for potential future applications.
Imagine an experienced software engineer who got interested in PLT and wants to learn more. Someone told them that they should start with reading "The Lambda Calculus. Its Syntax and Semantics" by Barendregt. They go and struggle through unfamiliar notation, fighting to extract a drop of insight relevant to their experience. Finally, they understood the Church-Rosser theorem.
"What's Church-Rosser theorem good for?", software engineer asks. Oh, you see, it has
practical applications
, you just don't know enough to see it yet.
The engineer disappeared. His time was better spent learning a new Javascript framework - at least there he could see practical benefits.
Problem 2: Standing on the toes of the giants
Even simple-sounding theorems require heavy machinery. And that machinery is still being built, even though we started in the 30s.
How is that different from any other branch of mathematics? Well, if you take a look at undergraduate or graduate mathematics curriculum, you'll see that most subjects connect to one another. The build up on one another. Or there are celebrated "bridge" theorems, providing a way to translate results from one branch of mathematics to another.
Not so much in PLT. Each development, each proof starts close to starting from scratch. You won't find many authors reusing someone else's lemmas and theorems. Even definitions aren't agreed upon. So each paper can feel like starting from scratch.
Don't get me wrong, PLT researchers read each other's papers and do influence each other's work. But this influence happens at the level of techniques and approaches rather than formal reuse. Instead of building theorem-upon-theorem like in other mathematical fields, PLT researchers tend to adapt and modify each other's proof methods for their own ground-up constructions.
Problem 3: Abstraction creep
I mentioned that each paper, each problem might require a separate setup, with its own definitions, lemmas and theorems. Wouldn't it be nice if we could package common proof techniques as ready-made theorems and reuse them across many proofs?
It definitely would be nice but the price to pay is a very high level of abstraction. Think of it as a codebase which uses complicated architectural patterns, lots of indirection, many layers. Not in the spaghetti code kind of way, it's all necessary and used well - but there's a steep learning curve.
Just like with that codebase, where implementing each single piece of functionality from scratch would be
so much easier
without using so many abstractions, it's also the case for proofs using abstract methods. They are powerful but you lose intuitive clarity and make it harder for new people to jump in.
Problem 4: It's just hard
PLT is very hard. Minor changes to a language might break properties you rely on, language features don't compose nicely. The design space is vast, exploring each corner is expensive (how many production-grade compilers are there in the world?) and we've only had so much time.
On the other hand, PLT is about very concrete objects: programming languages. I can experiment with them, I can write interpreters, create my own toy language. Many people do! Why not learn some theory as well? How hard can it be?
It's an unpleasant surprise.
Solutions?
I can't dictate what people should and shouldn't do. But I'm well within my right to write down a wish-list:
Be honest and tell people that big part of motivation for PLT work is its inherent beauty and immediate applicability in software engineering scenarios is not the goal.
Create introductory materials for software engineers interested in PLT. It doesn't need to be comprehensive but it should provide motivation for why the theory exists, why it can be useful and why it is hard.
Keep your theorems and proofs as simple as possible. I know t

data.article_summary: 文章主要批评了每日笔记（daily notes）的价值，认为它们通常不会被 revisit 或分享，只是制造了数字垃圾。笔记的价值应与其被访问和分享的频率成正比。文章建议专注于创建更可能被 revisit 或分享的笔记，比如一个持续更新的重点笔记（focus.md），用于追踪重要任务和次要任务。此外，针对重复出现的问题创建单独的笔记，并在需要时分享，能够增加笔记的价值。总的来说，作者强调笔记应减少无谓的记录，专注于实际有用的内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：笔记系统的使用和组织方法

不同观点：
• [sevensor] 支持使用单一的笔记系统，结合数字和纸质笔记。他建议将所有新内容放在末尾，每个条目都标明日期，并使用醒目的主题标题。当笔记过多时，只需封存旧的文件或笔记本并开启新的。他认为笔记主要是帮助思考，而非频繁回看。
   
• [sgoody] 认为记笔记是非常个人化的事情，自己曾尝试多种方法但效果不佳。最终发现每日笔记对个人非常有效，帮助减轻了对笔记结构和内容的焦虑。他提到，虽然旧笔记不太关注，但每日笔记对当前工作非常有用，并且还会单独写“正式”文档。

• [jvanderbot] 支持每日笔记，已有10到15年的经验，认为每日清零的感觉非常好。他使用命令行工具轻松查看和编辑笔记，并认为习惯的养成是关键。

• [thomascountz] 对原文语言表达有异议，但认同笔记结构影响创作的观点。他认为，如果考虑到分享笔记的可能性，可能会对思维过程产生积极或消极的影响。

• [stephenlf] 支持按问题/解决方案记录笔记的方法，并在公司内部应用这种模式，取得了良好效果。他认为这种方法在小团队中有效，但无法扩展。

• [sp33der89] 不同意作者的观点，认为自己的笔记观念与作者不同。他喜欢LogSeq的无限滚动页面设计，使得他更频繁地重读和编辑每日笔记。

• [TooSmugToFail] 认为每日笔记是处理复杂组织和多线程任务的重要工具，是不可或缺的工具。

• [spankibalt] 虽然 indulge 在每日笔记中，但更倾向于按主题组织笔记。他认为日期标注是可选的，并且认为基于日期组织的笔记系统在项目日记和信息整理中广泛适用。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于每日笔记是否有效以及如何组织笔记。有些人认为每日笔记帮助思考和任务管理，而另一些人则认为记笔记是个人化且应按需调整。
• 不同工具和方法（如LogSeq、命令行工具）的使用也是讨论的重要部分，展示了多样化的笔记记录方式。
• 笔记的结构和分享对思维过程的影响也是一个值得注意的讨论点。

44553873.article_content:
Daily notes considered harmful
2025-07-13
Daily notes are useless. The value of a note is directly proportional to the number of times it is visited. That value is exponentiated each time a note is shared. Daily notes aren't revisited and they aren't shared.
Daily notes look like this:
notes/
yyyy-mm-dd.md
yyyy-mm-dd.md
yyyy-mm-dd.md
On the surface, the idea of a note per day seems great. You plan out your day and track your work. You can revisit the past if needed. But you won't. All you are doing is generating digital clutter. You will also never share these notes, so the chance of their value increasing exponentially is zero.
Instead you should focus on creating notes that you are likely to revisit or likely to share.
Focus.md
I have one note that I visit all the time when I am working. It's a single Markdown file that I constantly update. It's essentially a to-do list that just helps me juggle all the things that I need to track. I call it focus.md
# Focus
Tasks that I have to do
## Periphery
Tasks that I have to be aware of, but I don't have to do.
It's nice because it lets me offload information that I don't need at hand and helps me focus on what I need to do.
Don't ask the same question twice
I try to never ask the same question twice. That means that when I do have a question, that question and its answer get a note.
They look something like this:
# Issue
## Issue details
## Resolution
Since I'm a programmer, I make a lot of these notes. I don't visit them very often, but I do revisit them if the same issue pops up again. But these notes find their value in being shared. If another person encounters the same issue, and I am able to help them fix it, then the note is worth the cost of its creation. I even add a lot of these notes to our documentation so I don't have to share them by hand.
It took me a while to figure out what's worth recording, and what isn't. And I am sure that it will be something different for you. But tools are supposed to prevent toil. Don't waste your time with daily notes.
#writing

data.title: Adam Curtis's Shifty: When Britain was 'wild and extraordinary'
data.author: dijksterhuis
data.article_summary: Adam Curtis的新五集BBC纪录片《Shifty》探索了20世纪末的英国，通过一系列奇异的档案片段展现了当时社会的怪异与不确定性。影片融合了重大历史事件，如苏联解体和阿富汗战争，以及诸如前卫发型比赛、郊区线舞派对等超现实场景。Curtis利用这些片段讨论了社会变迁，尤其是过去的影像如何囚禁人们的思维。他重新使用了对前财政顾问Alan Budd的采访，揭示了撒切尔时代经济政策的真实意图。影片中，严肃的政治话题与喜剧元素并存，例如一只正在变性的狗，以及撒切尔手袋中残留的香水味，这些都象征着一个正在消逝的过去。Curtis认为撒切尔是一个悲剧性人物，她释放了无法控制的力量，试图创造一个政治影响力减弱的自由社会。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44554565.article_content:
Image caption,
Avant-garde hairstyles are one of the many strange elements of British life highlighted in Shifty
Samuel Spencer
BBC
Published
13 June 2025
The documentary filmmaker Adam Curtis gives a guide to some of the key moments from his new series Shifty.
In his documentaries, Adam Curtis has taken us everywhere from Russia during the breakdown of the Soviet Union, in
TraumaZone
, to the war in Afghanistan, in
Bitter Lake
.
Now Curtis, whose work has been called
"dazzling" and "terrifying"
by critics, has set his sights on Britain at the end of the 20th century for the five-part BBC series
Shifty
.
This time Curtis's signature style sees him use a bizarre array of archive clips to explore, he says, how "life in Britain today has become strange - a hazy dream-like flux in which no-one can predict what is coming next".
In Shifty, clips of the major players of the era â Prime Ministers Margaret Thatcher, John Major and Tony Blair â exist alongside surreal moments sourced from the BBC's extensive archives, like avant-garde hairdressing competitions, suburban line dancing parties and children hot-wiring a tractor.
To the uninitiated, his documentaries can feel impenetrable, so we spoke to Curtis to curate and explain some of the key clips from the new series.
Curtis also suggested a title for each clip that perfectly places viewers into the strange and murky world of Shifty.
'One of the few moments of honesty'
Media caption,
'The government adviser suspecting treachery'
One section details the rise of the musical remixes in the 1980s, and its societal implications â how, in Curtis's words, "we are trapped by a cascade of endlessly replayed images, songs, dreams from the past".
However, he admits, "that's the way this series was made, so I'm just as bad. If it's become a prison, I may be one of the jailers."
One way Curtis remixes the past is by reusing an interview with Sir Alan Budd that Curtis filmed for the 1992 documentary
Pandora's Box
.
In a remarkably honest interview, the one-time chief economic adviser to the Treasury during Thatcher's tenure worries that "the people making the policy decisionsâ¦ never believed for a moment this was the correct way to bring down inflation.
"They did, however, see that it would be a very, very good way to raise unemployment, and raising unemployment was an extremely desirable way of reducing the strength of the working class."
"I've always been fascinated by that interview that Budd gave," says Curtis. "It's one of the few moments of honesty I've ever had from someone in power like that being interviewed."
'A past that was about to go'
Media caption,
'Bruno - the dog that is shifting sex'
As a young BBC employee, Curtis worked on That's Life. The show combined consumer affairs with lighter stories â most famously,
a dog that could 'say' the word sausages.
Curtis credits his ability to juggle tragic and comic tones to this early role: "It showed me that you could go from a badly-built housing estate built on poisonous waste ground to a talking dog."
In Shifty, clips of societal unrest exist alongside Bruno, a dog who is, according to his vet, "changing his sex" â their male organs disappearing and their female ones developing.
Curtis says that it was Bruno's owner that drew him to the clip: "The way she's sitting and her hair," he says, "it felt like a past that was about to go."
Animals in his work can often represent our secret lives, he says â "they are these creatures who live with us who probably have a lot of hidden knowledge about us."
For Curtis, animals also counterpoint what he calls the "highly pretentious" elements of his work: "They just entertain people."
'A tragic figure'
Media caption,
'Margaret Thatcher's handbag and the ghostly perfume'
In this clip, an archivist at Cambridge University takes one of Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's handbags out of a box, noting how the bag still smells strongly of her perfume.
Similarly, Thatcher's presence can be felt in much of the series, as we see the effects of
her policies in the 1980s and 90s
.
Before Thatcher became Prime Minister in 1979, Curtis argues there was "a collective model of society, where people came together in factories, were exploited, then realised they had power as a collective group."
He feels, however, that the closure of industries like mining led to "a society full of fragmented individuals who were powerful in the way they thought about their own desires, but actually on their own were powerless."
Despite this, Curtis sees Thatcher as a "tragic figure", who unleashed forces she could not control.
"She was the last politician who had an idea of how to change the country," he explains. "She wanted to create a society in which politics doesn't have as much effect as it did, and should allow individuals to be loose and free."
'Ever more irrational assumptions'
Media caption,
'In one universe, Stephen Hawking says goodnight to his child'

data.title: Happy 20th Birthday, Django
data.author: davepeck
data.article_summary: Django于2025年7月13日迎来20周年生日！自2005年Jacob Kaplan-Moss首次提交代码以来，Django已发布400多个版本。为庆祝这一时刻，官方推出了一个特别网站，展示全球线上线下庆祝活动，包括问答、社区成就展示等。同时，Django软件基金会呼吁大家捐款支持项目，目标是在20天内获得200名新捐助者，每人捐赠至少20美元，其中至少20人成为每月定期捐助者。截至2025年7月13日，已完成目标的25.6%，募集到76,707美元。展望未来，Django计划继续发布新版本，扩展生态系统，并保持包容和支持的开发者社区。

44552500.article_content:
Happy 20th birthday Django!
Posted by
Thibaud Colas & Benjamin Balder Bach
on July 13, 2025
On July 13th 2005, Jacob Kaplan-Moss made the first commit to the public repository that would become Django. Twenty years and 400+ releases later, here we are –
Happy 20th birthday Django! 🎉
Join the celebrations
We want to share this special occasion with you all! Our new
20-years of Django website
showcases all online and local events happening around the world, through all of 2025. As well as other opportunities to celebrate!
Expect birthday cake 🎂 and singing Happy Birthday
A special quiz or two? see who knows all about Django trivia
Showcase of great community achievements
View our 20th birthday website
Support Django
As a birthday gift of sorts, consider whether you or your employer can support the project via donations to our non-profit Django Software Foundation. For this special event, we want to set a special goal!
Over the next 20 days, we want to see 200 new donors, supporting Django with $20 or more, with at least 20 monthly donors.
Help us making this happen:
Donate on the Django website
Donate on GitHub sponsors
Or check out how to
become a Corporate Member
Once you’ve done it, post with #DjangoBirthday and tag us
on Mastodon
/
on Bluesky
/
on X
/
on LinkedIn
so we can say thank you!
26%
Of our US $300,000.00 goal for 2025, as of July 13th, 2025, we are at:
25.6% funded
$76,707 donated
Donate to support Django
The next 20 years
20 years is a long time in open source – and we want to keep Django thriving for many more, so it keeps on being the web framework for perfectionists with deadlines as the industry evolves. We don’t know how the web will change it that time, but from Django, you can expect:
Many new releases, each with years of support
Thousands more packages in our
thriving ecosystem
An inclusive and supportive community with hundreds of thousands of developers
Happy 20th birthday, Django!

data.article_summary: 科学家发现一颗巨大气态行星HIP 67522 b，围绕年轻恒星HIP 67522运行时，引发恒星表面产生巨大耀斑，这种现象前所未见。该行星距离恒星极近，轨道距离仅为水星与太阳距离的五分之一，公转周期仅7天。其与恒星磁场的相互作用可能是引发耀斑的原因，耀斑可能逐渐剥离行星的大气层。HIP 67522 b体积接近木星，但质量仅5%，大气主要由氢和氦组成，未来可能演变为亚海王星。研究利用了NASA的TESS和欧空局的CHEOPS卫星数据，揭示了这颗行星的特殊环境和演化前景。
